A government spokesperson said: “Hosting the Fifa Women’s World Cup 2035 would be a major opportunity for the UK, delivering a significant economic boost to communities across the country and helping drive a decade of change in women’s sport.

“Government guarantees are an important part of any bid for a major event on this scale and we have engaged with Fifa throughout the process to ensure a proportionate approach. We are now looking forward to Monday’s hosting decision.”

Fifa has been approached for comment.

Sports.title: Premier League clubs vote through new rules to increase legal protection for board
Sports.content:
Clubs rallied behind the Premier League’s leadership in a key vote on Thursday, overwhelmingly backing new rules that would protect the chief executive, Richard Masters, from potentially damaging lawsuits.

A vote to expand the legal indemnity afforded to Premier League directors was won 18-2 at a shareholders’ meeting in central London, granting Masters and other figures greater protection in the event they were subjected to legal action as a consequence of doing their job.

Manchester City are understood to be one of two clubs to vote against the extension of indemnity, and one unnamed side spoke out at length against the measures during the meeting. The other vote against was by Nottingham Forest, who felt insufficient time had been granted to consider the proposal.

The rule change follows reports that the organisation’s leadership may be named in possible legal action by City’s Abu Dhabi sponsors, who have claimed their reputations were damaged as a result of the excoriating verdict of an independent commission regarding City’s breaches of the league’s financial rules. City have appealed against the verdict.

This week the Abu Dhabi telecommunications giant and City sponsor Etisalat released a statement describing the contents of the verdict as “entirely false and defamatory”. Referring to the independent commission’s report as “the published findings of the English Premier League”, Etisalat said it was “actively considering all options relating to its rights and associated legal remedies in this matter”.

The details of any increase of indemnity, including who would cover any potential costs, were not discussed in the meeting.

The chief refereeing officer of Pro Ref, Howard Webb, attended and came under sustained questioning from club executives over recent referee and video assistant referee failures.

A report by the independent key match incidents panel this week found there had been two serious mistakes that were not corrected by the VAR during the most recent round of matches. Webb is understood to have acknowledged that performance in matchday 10 had been “poor” but argued that apart from that weekend, key metrics on decision-making had been trending in the right direction this season.

Sports.title: Thomas Frank admits he has a point to prove after taking reins at Crystal Palace
Sports.content:
Thomas Frank has admitted he has a point to prove on his return to management as he aims to steer Crystal Palace away from relegation trouble after taking over as manager.

The Dane was confirmed as Pierre Sage’s successor on Monday with Palace at the bottom of the table after 10 matches having conceded 24 goals – the most in the Premier League. They face a crucial trip to Coventry on Saturday and Frank admitted he had been “surprised about how good it feels” after returning to work for the first time since being sacked by Tottenham in February.

The 53-year-old spent most of the intervening period travelling, working as a pundit at the World Cup and taking in trips to Japan, Australia and his native Denmark, where he was visiting friends and family when he received the SOS call from Palace last week. Frank previously spent seven years in charge of Brentford but left Spurs after just eight months with a win ratio of 34.2% – the worst of any permanent manager in the club’s history. He believes he has learned from that experience.

“I think you’ve all got an ego,” he said. “Some are better at controlling it than others. For me, it’s not the critics. It’s more what I can bring myself, what I can learn, what I can prove, how I can get better. I think that’s the big thing.

“In this world there’s a lot of clever people out there. But they only know a 10th of the truth. And that’s a 10th of the truth at Brentford and a 10th of the truth at Tottenham. That’s just the way it is – if you can’t handle that as a coach or a player or whatever, then you shouldn’t be in this business. I’m just very happy to be back in the game, very happy to be in a fantastic club, at Palace, where you walk in the door and you just feel the energy. You feel the people. It just feels good.”

Frank said he is planning to pick Roy Hodgson’s brains in the coming days after recalling a conversation they had when the former England and Palace manager was still at Selhurst Park.

“I was thinking, does it ever go away? The worry, do you get more relaxed about everything?” he asked Hodgson. “‘No chance, it’s impossible.’ I thought it would have been a little bit easier with age and experience. But in a way can’t help ourselves. I know what I want and the direction we should go in.”

Justin Cochrane – one of Thomas Tuchel’s assistants for England – has joined as first-team coach and took his first session with Palace on Monday less than 24 hours after the Nations League victory over Spain in Madrid. He is expected to be joined on Palace’s backroom staff by Bernardo Cueva, with Frank confirming that a deal with Chelsea is “very close” for the Mexican. Both worked with Frank at Brentford, where he spent almost nine years as an assistant and then manager. He is also hoping to add Andreas Georgson from Tottenham, who has been credited for his prowess on set-pieces: an area that Palace have struggled with for some time.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino calls for Manchester United to show no fear against Liverpool
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino has called on Manchester United to have “no fear” when they travel to Anfield on Sunday for his first game. The Argentinian does not want his players to take a backward step as he targets a fast start.

United are 18th in the Premier League and Liverpool fourth but the head coach will not accept any self-doubt. Pochettino is known for being attack-minded and is keen to instil those ideals, but will have had only three days with the players since replacing Michael Carrick.

“We are going to Anfield with the idea to win and be brave and to be Manchester United,” Pochettino told the club’s website. “The history talks for us, and what we need to expect. We need to be sure that we are brave and we are protagonists and go there with no fears and challenge a very good team like Liverpool.”

Pochettino arrived in Manchester on Wednesday after an overnight flight, having taken charge of his final USA match against Haiti. He toured the training ground and held meetings with senior staff and players not on international duty.

Members of Pochettino’s staff were in place earlier in the week as they seek to revitalise a team with one league win. Pochettino is waiting for United to ratify the appointment of Sílvia Tuyà, a strength and conditioning coach who worked with him with the USA. She travelled with him by private jet to Manchester but was not named among the staff later in the day.

“We need to go little by little, step by step,” Pochettino said. “We cannot go too fast but also we need to, at the same time, attack the priorities to build something.”

He said it was important he and his staff adapt to the culture of the club. “And then, with this sense of knowing the history of the club, try to create all together, because we are all different, a culture, a philosophy that can respect that identity, the history of the club. But at the same time, performing. If we don’t perform, the responsibility is mine.”

Pochettino has coveted the United job and is a keen admirer of Sir Alex Ferguson, whom he describes as “the best coach in history”. Since the Scot’s retirement in 2013, United have failed to match his success but Pochettino said he was looking at “the potential of the club”. The weight of past achievements has hindered individuals over the past 13 years.

“The players need to express their talent,” Pochettino said. “We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now: it’s to work with them and try to take the pressure.

“Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it’s too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back. When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your teammates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

He sounded an upbeat note, saying: “With the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.”

United’s total borrowings have risen to £784.5m, with long-term debt up by almost £100m over the past year. Figures published for the three months to 30 September show long-term borrowings of £577.4m, compared with £481.2m 12 months earlier. United’s cash reserves fell from £80.5m to £55.5m during the same period despite an increase in revenue.

The club reported a quarterly net loss of £18.1m, compared with £6.6m ​in ​the same period a year earlier. Revenue rose by 4% to £146m.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Football’s political gamers face off at Fifa with the real-life final boss
Sports.content:
GAME ON!

Although the millions of gamers who are pulling sickies would beg to differ, the release of Grand Theft Auto VI wasn’t the most exciting midnight launch involving a sprawling enterprise full of shady characters. Over in Zurich, the clock also struck 12 on the candidate deadline for next year’s Fifa presidential election, leaving those of us who have no interest in video games with our own chaotic, multi-billion-dollar sandbox where untouchable bosses bend the rules to suit themselves. While online carjackers are busy exploring a “most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world”, football’s real-life power brokers are gearing up for a March showdown in the actual city of Rabat.

For years, Gianni Infantino has looked nailed-on to glide into a fourth term of office completely unopposed, but following his disastrous Fifa Forward Enterprise wheeze to flog stakes in the World Cup to his American pals on the cheap, many of the emperor’s former allies have finally turned against him. In the wake of the revolt, European national associations withdrew their backing for Infantino and, on Thursday morning, Fifa confirmed the 56-year-old will face his first contested election since parking his backside on the throne a decade ago. Sadly for all those who would like nothing more than to see him deposed, Infantino remains the red-hot favourite in what will be a three-horse race.

Leading the charge for the mutineers is Philippe Diallo, the 63-year-old French Football Federation president who was unanimously anointed as Europe’s preferred candidate after their actual preferred candidate, Arsène Wenger, decided not to throw his chapeau in the ring. His billing by Uefa’s vice-president, Laura McAllister, as a man “who can instigate real, meaningful and lasting reform” at Fifa conveniently overlooks the fact that, as recently as five months ago, Diallo’s own federation signed a letter formally endorsing Infantino again. Joining Diallo in the battle to prise Gianni’s fingers off the levers of power is Kozo Tashima, the 68-year-old honorary president of the Japan FA. He could yet stand aside to avoid a split of the vote from Fifa’s 211 members who want Infantino booted to the door marked “Do One!”. Unfortunately, Ramon Vega, the former Switzerland and Tottenham defender, won’t be on the ballot. He had again announced his candidacy but proved unable to scare up the five member-association endorsements required.

Between now and Fifa’s March congress, all three candidates must pass a Fifa eligibility and integrity check, a feat which shouldn’t be beyond the two pretenders, given Infantino has repeatedly come through it with flying colours while helping to overhaul the committees tasked with marking his papers along the way. Assuming he once again clears the hurdle of being vetted by his own organisation, the next four months promise a familiar blur of private jets, palm-greasing and disingenuous crawling. While a generation of gamers will spend winter pulling off virtual heists in Vice City, when it comes to bending the rules in your favour, nobody plays the game quite like the Fifa final boss.

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Join Yara El-Shaboury from 8pm GMT for minute-by-minute updates from Arsenal 1-1 OL Lyonnes in Women’s Bigger Cup.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“It’s not that I don’t ‘care’ about the price, it’s that the market is the market; it doesn’t depend on me. Calmness always, perspective … I know strikers are measured by goals but, well, the days I don’t score I’m sure I will be able to walk off the pitch and say that, no matter what happened, I helped my team, doing a load of other things. It is what it is” – Gonzalo García, the Spanish U-21 forward and great nephew of Rita Hayworth, gets his chat on with Sid Lowe about his £34m switch to Fulham, the pace of the Premier League and more.

View image in fullscreen Gonzalo García, in warmer climes. Photograph: Pablo Garcia/The Guardian

RECOMMENDED SUBSCRIBING

Sport in Focus picks out the best photos of the past seven days. Get it delivered to your inbox every Friday by signing up here.

double quotation mark When I first saw the photo in yesterday’s Football Daily, I thought Mauricio Pochettino had opted for a short back and sides, presumably to pre-empt him tearing his luscious locks out in frustration at forthcoming poor results/terrible January transfer window/petulant sniping from sulky squad members. Then I realised he was in the back seat, all but entirely obscured by the rear-view mirror, in which he could perhaps see his sense of job satisfaction disappearing …” – Phil Taverner.

double quotation mark That photo of Pochettino being chauffeured by a beefy driver answered one of my burning questions: what’s Ange Postecoglou doing these days?” – Mike Wilner (and others).

Sports.title: Gonzalo García: ‘I love Craven Cottage – the fans can reach out and touch you’
Sports.content:
The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one.

Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field.

Hayworth’s family was from Seville province. “I know she was a great actress but I’m afraid I have to admit I’m not one for old films,” García concedes in an even tone. “My uncles played rugby for Ciencias and practically all of them were in the national team together. They tried to get me to play with my cousins, but I was always more into football.” He was good at it too: another Spain international, the Club World Cup’s top scorer, playing for Real Madrid.

Then this summer, with opportunities limited, he joined Fulham, his introductory interview conducted in impeccable English. Having joined Madrid aged 10, he was leaving home for the first time, as Fulham’s record signing, at 22. He had the language and intelligence to embrace it. As for being uprooted, he was used to that, growing up in Argentina and Chile as well as Spain.

“From very little my parents impressed upon me the importance of study, learning languages,” García says. “I’m at Villanueva university [in Madrid]. I started with dual honours business and analytics, although that became difficult with my profession. Now it’s just business, and I’m trying to arrange with the university how best to handle it [from London]. My parents considered it fundamental to speak English and I was always at international schools.

View image in fullscreen Gonzalo García plays football for Spain’s under-21s but his uncles were international rugby players. Photograph: Pablo Garcia/The Guardian

“Every two or three years we would change city. Obviously, there would be phases when I felt: ‘Pfff, again?!’ Having to move home because of my parents’ work. But I look back and feel grateful because, seen with perspective, it gives you opportunities to meet new people, see new places, learn. I’ve always had foreign friends with whom I spoke English.”

García has been joined at Fulham by César Palacios and Manuel Ángel from Madrid’s academy. Three 22-year-olds, like your very own Erasmus course. “Nah,” García says, laughing. “I wouldn’t call it an Erasmus because we’re talking about a big, ambitious career step. We’re grateful for the trust placed in us. I’ve been pleasantly surprised by London, a huge city with people from all nationalities and cultures and Fulham fit the situation I was in, the desire to grow.

“Álvaro Arbeloa explained the project, convinced me. I’d worked with him in Madrid. He knows me perfectly, how far he can push me. Equally, I know what he wants of me. That helps … [Arbeloa] told me it was a project that it will take time but that he needed me. I’m very, very happy. It’s one of the world’s best leagues, if not the best.”

And the toughest? Is English football as wild as it looks? “Yes!” García replies. “They had told me it was demanding, hard, but …” He cracks up. “I have to admit it still surprised me. That first game against Chelsea, I finished really, really tired. It was box to box, intense, a lot of running. Bit by bit I’m adapting. The intensity and pace is very different.

“Spain is more tactical, a bit more technical. English football is pace. You can’t lose concentration for a second, not a second. Anything can happen any moment. How many Premier League games are decided late? Suddenly there’s a goal in the 90th minute and again on 93. It’s your corner and their chance. The level of concentration, that constant transition, is what most sets the Premier League apart.”

Despite defeat on that opening day against Chelsea, García scored. A superb goal followed against AFC Wimbledon in the Carabao Cup. “It was super special to do it at Craven Cottage. I love how close the fans are – they can reach out and touch you. But I don’t consider myself someone who’s easily satisfied. I’m not like that. I always want more, more, more.”

View image in fullscreen ‘Álvaro Arbeloa explained the project at Fulham, he convinced me,’ says Gonzalo García. Photograph: Joe Giddens/PA

García hasn’t scored since and Fulham went five league games without a win, pressure building. Which is where the calmness comes in. By the time they faced Hull, Arbeloa appeared on the edge of the sack, questions asked about his signings, García especially. Were three Madrid academy kids really what Fulham needed? Was the coach’s relationship with them not such a good thing after all?

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

No player is impermeable to what is said, García admits, but he insists: “We treat that as outside noise. And we all knew that the beginning wouldn’t be easy. There’s a change of cycle: the coach goes, a new coach comes, there are signings, a different system, idea. Everyone has to adapt: those already at the club and those of us who are new. We’re young too. Results weren’t going our way but we had good intentions: to play good football, build, apply the manager’s ideas bit by bit. We had to remain calm.”

Fulham go into Saturday’s game at Manchester City unbeaten in four in the league, the sense of them shifting towards something more pragmatic not shared by García. “I don’t think we changed anything against Hull,” he says of a game Fulham won 1-0. “We didn’t do anything we weren’t already doing. Nothing. Maybe we controlled the small details that hurt us but the idea was the same. The players were very clear what the manager asked, very firm: it was just a question of time. You have to be patient. If you watch Fulham, you see the manager’s idea: have the ball, construct attacks well, show maximum intensity constantly with and without the ball. Aggressive, ambitious.”

View image in fullscreen Gonzalo García has not scored for Fulham since August: ‘I know strikers are measured by goals.’ Photograph: Joe Giddens/PA

Chances are coming for García but goals aren’t. He has started every league game but not scored or assisted since the opening day. Yet if there is a sense of a man feeling the pressure, that’s not repeated here; instead there’s an evenness, an ease. And a smile when another, more welcome, stat is raised: he has made more off‑the‑ball runs into the area than anyone. Something to hold on to, perhaps, a process that will pay off. “Really?” he says. “Well, I’m happy for people to see that a striker can help the team without the ball. In the end, it’s about following the manager’s instructions.”

In the end, though, teams will be judged on results and strikers on goals, price too. He knows: this is what he does, the path he chose. “Pressure depends on how you look at it, really,” García says. “Football is [very psychological]. It happens fast: it doesn’t give you time to enjoy good moments or linger on bad ones. It’s a rollercoaster – up there, down here. It’s not flat, but you maintain balance, work daily, improve: go in, focus, repeat.

“It’s not that I don’t ‘care’ about the price, it’s that the market is the market; it doesn’t depend on me. Calmness always, perspective … I know strikers are measured by goals but, well, the days I don’t score I’m completely sure I will be able to walk off the pitch and say that, no matter what happened, I helped my team, doing a load of other things. It is what it is.”

It is also time. A head peers around the door, the bus is going. García holds out a hand, apologises again. “It’s been a pleasure,” he says.

Sports.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
Sports.content:
It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it.

But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio. From one of the absolute greats.

Danny died last week. In a beautiful tribute on the Spurs podcast he hosted – A View From the Lane – Charlie Eccleshare pointed out the irony that for someone so articulate and erudite and able to do so much more than just “the football”, his most iconic moment is so simple. Even the opening noise – not even a real word – is perfect in that context.

Terms such as pioneer and trailblazer often get thrown out in moments like this. But Danny really was. I first met him at BBC London more than 20 years ago. As someone who’d listened to him and Danny Baker as a teenager, I couldn’t really believe I was in the same office as them. His career was ridiculous, editing the NME and Q magazine, setting up Football365, but it was radio where I knew him. He understood the absurdity of life and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living by talking about football. I remember at TalkSport one World Cup – 2018 perhaps – wandering in and he was hosting a live match, watching a game on the TV just marvelling at the fact that this was a job, and that this was his job.

And he was funny. Blimey he was funny – what an ability to be blessed with. I listened to a best of Baker and Kelly Upfront from the old Radio 5 on YouTube the other day; amazing calls about Arthur Cox locking a disgruntled fan in his office for two and a half hours, a man playing football with a pig’s head in a sausage factory in Peckham: “I used to like the volleys when the eyes popped out.” Anyone who has tried to make funny football content, of any kind – radio, TV, podcasts, social media – owes him a debt of gratitude.

View image in fullscreen Danny Kelly on television in 2013. Photograph: Steve Meddle/Shutterstock

Last Wednesday Charlie Baker and I had to try to do him justice on TalkSport. Afternoon UK time, midnight till 3am for me in Australia. I was asleep when my phone rang and instantly presumed I’d slept through my alarm and missed the show. A millisecond of internal panic surged through me as I jumped up and cracked a shin on the bedside table. Danny would appreciate the ridiculous scene of me hopping around in the dark trying not to wake the kids while one of the bosses gave me the incredibly sad news.

If you’ve broadcast for any amount of time, you will be confronted with having to host shows just after someone has died. Jack Charlton, Terry Venables, Jimmy Greaves – but never before have I had to pay tribute to a friend.

Paul Hawksbee’s voice cracks and we all go. There are West Ham and Chelsea fans calling admitting they listen to his Spurs podcast because it’s him. There are all manner of texts recounting hilarious stories they heard on his shows over the last 30 years: the man who took a TV to a game in Northern Ireland so they could watch the FA Cup final, having to move around holding the aerial to keep the signal.

There’s a moment I think Danny would have found so funny, when I’m being sad – because it is sad, and I am sad – and into the break I read the sponsor’s lines: “This show is brought to you by Toolstation, first stop Toolstation” in such a maudlin way it’s as if I’m delivering a eulogy, just one sponsored by a hardware store. I catch myself just in time.

But, most important, there are so many messages from people who never met Danny, who never knew him, but who felt as if they knew him. We believed he would have wanted a bit of fuss made of him.

He definitely knew the enduring power of radio, even as the broadcasting landscape changes so quickly. It connects in a way nothing else can. And nothing said that more than messages we received from listeners who at one time or another were struggling and going through incredibly hard times and Danny’s energy, wit and joy were an escape and a tonic.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

There will be a million people more important in Danny’s life than me. Our paths crossed a great deal, but never for very long. I was a minuscule cog in his world – but Danny had so much love to give. Voice notes about how to broadcast remotely or celebrating Spurs’ win in Bilbao; the tributes showed he had almost infinite time for others.

It always feels such a bland cliche to say it’s impossible to consider someone so full of life not being there – we all know we have a sell-by date. At the start of October he had been given a choice: to ebb away slowly over a couple of years or have a big but very risky operation. Danny never ebbed.

He sent a big group WhatsApp voice note to many friends and colleagues, and I don’t think he would mind me writing what it said.

“I want you to know that I’ve enjoyed being around you, I’ve learnt from you, I’ve enjoyed working with you, you know how much I love my work – the fact I’m pretty good at it is secondary to how much I enjoy it, but look I’m very much hopeful that the boffins and my own determination will get me through this and we can all laugh about this message. But know how I care about you, how much you have meant in my life and on Thursday night or Friday morning when you look at the sky or feel the wind against your face, think about me and what’s happening and hopefully we’ll all have a pint and a laugh about this somewhere down the line.”

From “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH” to that – his words just hit the right tone every time.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino told to drop £71m Man United star and make statement for Liverpool clash
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino must omit Bryan Mbeumo from the Manchester United squad to face Liverpool after his late-night video gaming.

That's a call made by talkSPORT chief football correspondent Alex Crook, whilst Troy Deeney told the new head coach to make a statement decision on his team.



4 Pochettino makes his debut as the United head coach this weekend at Liverpool, and been told to make some big decisions Credit: Getty

Mbeumo stayed up for the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI during the early hours of Thursday, Pochettino's first full day as United boss.

It comes after Pochettino called for a culture reset at Old Trafford as they languish in 18th in the Premier League.

Historic rivals Liverpool host United on Sunday in what will be a huge first test for the Argentine.



Three points are a must, and Crook wants to see Pochettino arrive at Anfield with an iron fist and leave Mbeumo, who signed last summer in a £71million deal from Brentford, out of the team.

Mbeumo should be dropped vs Liverpool

"I've almost got no words for this, honestly," Crook said of the forward on the Premier League All Access podcast for talkSPORT.



"Up until the early hours, seemingly, playing a stupid video game the day before the new manager arrives."

"How old is he, 15? Why is he letting people know about it?" he added. "There's your example, if you're Mauricio Pochettino, don't put him in the squad."



Deeney then explained that he would back Mbeumo if their Thursday training session was in the afternoon as he could rest during the day.

But, after Mbeumo posted his GTA loading screen on social media, he said: "I'm with you though, Crooky, you can't be making those things public, you can't be. No one should be knowing that you're online.

"And then secondly with that, it does send a terrible message, but if I'm the manager, a captain in that dressing room, you go, 'Go on then, let's see what you've got.

4 Crook doesn't want to see Mbeumo involved against Liverpool after staying up late to play GTA VI Credit: Getty



"'We're going to put you through the wringer today and when you're tired, and if you pull a calf or something, I'm going to let everybody know because this is the standard that was here before and you're not living up to it.'"

Pochettino told to make statement

Although Deeney can understand why Crook wants Mbeumo to be dropped, he named two other players who could potentially be left out of the squad by Pochettino.

Andrey Santos, a £50m signing from Chelsea, has underperformed at the club, whilst Diogo Dalot has been error-prone this season.

"I think he's going to have to make a little bit of a statement as well. I don't know who that person's going to be, but I think it's going to be one of these players that we expect," Deeney said.



"Maybe it's Santos as a bit of a, 'You're not up to scratch, you're not in the squad', and just let people know that he's laying a marker down. I think that would be a little bit too easy, a low-hanging fruit.

"I'd love to see it with a... I don't know, maybe just to make Crooky happy, a Dalot. Just say, 'You know what? I don't want you around the team'.

4 Santos is one player that Deeney believes could be left out of the side when they travel to Anfield Credit: Getty

4 Another contender is Dalot, who is one of the long-serving members in the current United squad Credit: Getty



"He has to lay a marker down to one of these players that have been playing week in, week out for the last four to five years, that have been part of this ever-growing rot and mould that's been coming in the club.

"And say, 'No, no more', and it has to send a shockwave to the rest of the team."

Sports.title: Reece Oxford joins new club four years after last game in shock return to English football
Sports.content:
Reece Oxford joins new club four years after last game in shock return to English football

Reece Oxford has joined League One outfit Bromley, subject to international, FA and EFL clearance.

Oxford, who arrives at the Ravens on a free transfer and will wear the No. 39 shirt, is poised to make his debut on Saturday against Reading.

2 Oxford burst onto the scene with West Ham but struggled to live up to his potential Credit: AFP

He is the first signing Bromley have made following Karl Robinson's appointment after he replaced Andy Woodman in the dugout at Hayes Lane.

What did Reece Oxford say about his move to Bromley?

"The new gaffer came in, hopefully I can help him out now, help the team and we can get some wins," Oxford said.

"I've been here for a few weeks now getting my fitness levels up. Everyone has been great. All I can do is give something back to them now."

Reece Oxford's turbulent years

Oxford had been without a club since he departed Bundesliga outfit Augsburg in May 2025.

The 25-year-old also had not made a competitive appearance since November 2022 due to a string of injuries.

Oxford started out in Tottenham's academy before he moved to West Ham in 2011.

He then became the Hammers' youngest-ever player when he started a Europa League first round qualifying tie in July 2015 aged just 16 years and 198 days.

Oxford burst onto the scene with an impressive performance marking Mesut Ozil out of the game during West Ham's 2-0 win at Arsenal on the opening weekend of the 2015/16 season - but that was as good as things got for Oxford with the Hammers.

Loan spells at Reading, Borussia Monchengladbach and Augsburg all followed from 2017 to 2019 before Oxford eventually left West Ham in August 2019.

He made a total of 17 senior appearances for the Hammers before his permanent move to Augsburg.

2 Oxford's last competitive appearance was in November 2022 Credit: AFP

Oxford enjoyed a bright start to life with Augsburg, logging 68 appearances in three seasons.

But muscle injuries and struggles with the long-term effects of COVID meant Oxford featured just three times for Augsburg from the 2022/23 season onwards.

How have Bromley performed this season?

Oxford is now hoping to reboot his career at Bromley, who sit last in League One.

The Ravens have endured a difficult start to life in the third tier having picked up just two wins from their first 13 games.

Bromley's poor run of form prompted Woodman's departure on October 22, bringing the curtain down on his five-and-a-half year tenure.

Robinson now has the difficult task of keeping Bromley afloat in the third tier.

The Ravens enter Saturday's fixture against Reading three points away from safety.

As for the Royals, they sit seventh with 22 points, just seven behind league leaders Huddersfield Town.

Sports.title: Manchester United fans told to watch for transfer clues as ‘heir to Lionel Messi’ linked
Sports.content:
Manchester United fans told to watch for transfer clues as ‘heir to Lionel Messi’ linked

Manchester United fans have been warned the club faces multiple hurdles in any bid to sign Nico Paz.

The Como midfielder has been strongly linked with a potential January move to Old Trafford.

4 United fans have been handed a warning over their pursuit of Paz Credit: Getty

Paz is one of Europe's most in-demand players ahead of the re-opening of the transfer window.

The 22-year-old has scored six goals and added eight assists in 14 appearances across all competitions for Cesc Fabregas' side this term.

Those include a brace and an assist in Como's 4-1 mauling of United in the Champions League last month.

However, the playmaker could soon become available as he enters the final 18 months of his contract.

Could United sign Paz in January?

Paz joined Como from Real Madrid in 2024, with the deal including a buy-back option for the Spanish giants.

talkSPORT's Ben Jacobs has provided an update on his future as links to the Red Devils continue to intensify.

Speaking to Hawksbee and Baker on Thursday, he explained: "I think it's one, Real Madrid do the buy-back and that seems to be the direction of travel.

"Two, don't discount a Como stay because he's doing fantastically there and he's very happy. He's got Champions League football and he's playing under Cesc Fabregas.

"Of course, people are going to [link the two]. Some believe Paz is the natural heir to Lionel Messi and you've got Mauricio Pochettino, who's Argentine.

"But at this stage, we have to look at Manchester United needing an out-and-out striker, far more of an old-fashioned No.9, probably with proven Premier League experience and then a left-back and a central defender.

4 Paz has been described as Messi's long-term heir for Argentina Credit: Getty

"If they sign another attacking playmaker, even though Paz is extremely versatile, you would think that would be an indication that Bruno Fernandes is going to depart.

"At this stage, Manchester United are still hoping that Bruno Fernandes either signs a new deal or they can trigger a one-year extension on his contract.

"Two proposals to Bruno Fernandes have been rejected, but Manchester United are still in talks."

United captain Bruno Fernandes has rejected two offers of a new contract from the club.

The 32-year-old's current deal expires in the summer, although the Red Devils hold the option to extend it by a further year.

United transfer latest

As for where United may strengthen in January, Jacobs added: "I think for Manchester United in particular, January is going to be a very interesting window because we know they want to be opportunistic, but there's either a lack of talent available in that seller's market or they have to think about budgets.

4 Fernandes would likely leave United if Paz was signed, says Jacobs Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

"We know that it was very difficult for them towards the end of the summer.

"My expectation is that Mauricio Pochettino will like to blood through young and developing talent.

"But by the same token, he knows the true reality of where Manchester United are currently in the Premier League table and therefore finding ready-made players is going to be really important.

"As for a number nine, people naturally will link Manchester United with Folarin Balogun, although there's been no contact yet.

"They'd like Dominic Calvert-Lewin. He's expected to sign a new deal at Leeds United.

"Calvin Bassey is going to be one to watch. Again, a player that you can drop in in multiple defensive positions.

4 Pochettino and United are set for a busy January transfer window Credit: Getty

"And then there's Antonee Robinson, who again Pochettino had with the US men's national team and was linked with Manchester United before.

"He would fulfil the ‘available potentially mid-season’, but also he’s of that kind of age where if they wanted to go for somebody younger in the summer, they might actually be able to bring in two full-backs.

"So I'm expecting Manchester United to be one of the busiest clubs in January.

"One, because of need and their league position and two, because they'll obviously want to back Mauricio Pochettino to allow him to hit the ground running."

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session secretly filmed on drone and posted online
Sports.content:
Mauricio Pochettino’s first Manchester United training session secretly filmed on drone and posted online

Talk about a brutal start to your Manchester United tenure.

A 12-minute long video capturing Mauricio Pochettino's first training session as Red Devils boss has been shared on YouTube.

2 Pochettino has wasted little time in meeting his new players and staff Credit: Getty



The footage was obtained via a drone and uploaded by a user named 'CC OVERVIEW'.

Mauricio Pochettino's first training session caught on video

In the clip, Pochettino has a number of United stars work on structured patterns of play against mannequins on one field.

On the other, Pochettino's assistants put several Red Devils players through their paces in a small-sided possession drill.

Man United did not comment on the story when contacted by talkSPORT.

It is a less than ideal start to life at Carrington for Pochettino, who was unveiled as United manager on Wednesday.



However, the Argentine does not have any time to dwell on the footage as he has his focus on an away trip to bitter rivals Liverpool.

The Red Devils head to Anfield on Sunday hoping to snap an eight-game winless run.



When was Mauricio Pochettino appointed as Manchester United manager?

Pochettino was appointed as United boss during the international break as predecessor Michael Carrick was sacked.

Carrick was handed the reins on a permanent basis in May following a successful interim stint.



But the Red Devils legend could not replicate his success from last term and oversaw just one league win from ten games.

2 Carrick oversaw just four wins in 16 games as United boss this season Credit: Getty

A 4-4 draw against Aston Villa in which United scored twice in second half stoppage time proved to be the final straw for United's decision-makers.

The club wasted little time in swooping for Pochettino, who went into the international break as the United States boss but finished it in charge of a European giant.



United was forced to pay a total of $12million (£9m) to prise Pochettino and his staff away from the USMNT, just three months after the Argentine extended his contract with the Stars and Stripes until 2030.

Pochettino's final game in charge of the US was a 2-0 win over Haiti in the second leg of their CONCACAF quarter-final clash.

It cemented an 8-0 thrashing on aggregate after the USMNT prevailed 6-0 in the first leg.

Manchester United's upcoming fixtures

There is little time for Pochettino to properly get his feet under the desk following the Liverpool clash.



United then travel to Sporting Lisbon for a Champions League fixture on November 25 before Pochettino oversees his first game as Red Devils boss at Old Trafford against Brentford just three days later.

The Red Devils enter Sunday's match sitting 18th on eight points after ten games.

Sports.title: Chelsea warned over loss on £55m star as Serie A clubs eye January transfer
Sports.content:
Chelsea must consider sending Jamie Gittens out on loan as they risk making a loss on his £55million transfer.

That's the view of European football journalist Andy Brassell, who has named the Serie A club that would be a logical move for the winger once the January transfer window opens.



4 Gittens is yet to have made a big impact at Chelsea due to fitness issues and inconsistent minutes since his £55m move Credit: Getty

Gittens joined Chelsea from Borussia Dortmund in July 2025 and has made 29 appearances in all competitions since then, scoring one goal.

The 22-year-old has played just two matches this season, both in the Carabao Cup, having dealt with an ankle injury he suffered whilst on England Under-21 duty in September.

Given that Morgan Rogers signed from Aston Villa for a club-record deal worth £117m, Gittens was linked with a loan switch to Roma.



Chelsea blocked their attempt as they wanted the ex-Manchester City starlet to stay for the season, despite him not playing a single minute in the Premier League thus far.

Reports from Italy have claimed that Napoli are interested in a move at the beginning of 2027, and their Serie A rivals Roma could reignite their interest as the Blues face a dilemma explained by Brassell.



Chelsea face Gittens transfer decision

"I think the problem that Chelsea have, because Gittens has really struggled since he's gone there, and Dortmund always felt like they were getting a really good deal for this, by the way, is they almost have to loan him," he told talkSPORT.

"Because at the moment, they can't sell him. They're taking a huge loss, even bearing amortisation in mind. They're going to take a huge loss on him. No one's going out there and paying a fortune for him at the moment. And that's without factoring in the wages.



"So from Chelsea's perspective, you don't just want to get him out of the building for the moment. I think you need to really replenish his value as an asset.

"So that means getting him out somewhere where he can actually show he's a good player still. And he has shown he's a really good player in the past.

"His last season at Dortmund, he was brilliant in the first half of that season, before it sort of went sideways in the back half of it."

4 An ankle injury has not helped Gittens' progress, and Brassell believes a loan to Roma would be ideal Credit: Getty



Who should Gittens sign for?

Brassell then determined which Serie A side with credited interest in Gittens would be the best option for his development.

"I think Roma is the obvious one because, well, from a couple of perspectives. From the Roma perspective, I think they are looking for that left-hand sided wide player.

"And there was, I think, at least a semi-expectation that they were going to use Rodrigo Mora in that role after signing him from Porto. Now, really, he's more of a natural No.10. And he's played in more of a natural No.10 role since Paulo Dybala has been injured.

"He's been playing brilliantly, by the way, of course. An assist against Manchester United, scored in three successive Serie A games at the time of recording.



"He's having a brilliant time with all the opportunities that he never got at Porto, where they privilege a more physically strong type of player.

"And really, I think the way that Roma are playing at the moment, you look at not just the fact that they're competitive in this early season in terms of making themselves a contender for the Scudetto, whether that's durable, we'll see.

4 A temporary exit from Chelsea could see Gittens return to his form from Dortmund, where he hit 31 goal contributions in 107 matches Credit: Getty

"But they're good to watch and they look fun to play for as well. I think that matters from the players' perspective. The fact that they whiffed on so many wide player targets, so Mason Greenwood, (Alejandro) Garnacho.



"They were interested in (Antonio) Nusa, who they never had anywhere near the money to make that happen, nevertheless. They asked about Gittens in the summer as well.

"So, I think bringing him in makes a lot of sense. They still want that wide player. And I think to be competitive and to enjoy your football from Gittens' end, it looks fun. There's no doubt about that.

On Napoli's interest, Brassell added: "We don't know who the coach is going to be by the time it gets to the winter window.

"Max Allegri is, if he's not on a hot seat, he's on an above-lukewarm one, I think it's fair to say. So quite what that means in terms of the business they're going to do in the market is a question.



"In terms of left-sided players, even though they've had injuries that put most of them out, they've got plenty of players who can play in that position. So you look at David Neres, Alisson (Santos), even (Antonio) Vergara, who can play in that position if he needs to as well.

"There are a lot of other options. I think if Napoli were looking to do something in the window, they would be looking to do something probably defensively.

"And maybe in midfield as well because there are doubts over the future of (Kevin) De Bruyne. And over the future of Andre-Frank Zambo Anguissa, who's out of contract at the end of the season.

4 Roma could look to go in for Gittens once again when the January transfer window opens in a few weeks Credit: Getty



"So they need to have a bit of a think about that. And Napoli are frugal as well."

"For me, Roma on loan at Christmas seems a very logical conclusion," Brassell concluded.

Sports.title: Barcelona in the mix for cut-price Erling Haaland deal amid Man City relegation threat
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland would fit in 'really well' at Barcelona - this could be the perfect destination if Manchester City are forced to sell.

That's according to European football expert Andy Brassell, who has tipped Barca to make a play for Haaland if City fail in their appeal against the Premier League's guilty financial charges verdict.

6 Erling Haaland faces an uncertain future at Manchester City Credit: AFP

City were found guilty of all charges against them in September relating to alleged breaches of FFP rules between 2009 and 2018.

The club have since appealed against the ruling, with a hearing set to take place in December.

If their appeal is unsuccessful, though, the Citizens are expected to be sanctioned by an independent commission in 2027.

It is not yet clear how exactly they could be punished, with speculation they could be handed a huge points deduction that would ensure they spend multiple seasons in the Championship.

Should this be the case, it would cast doubt over the future of Haaland and many of City's other star players.

With no relegation clauses, the club wouldn't have to let players go on the cheap, but it is unlikely Haaland would be content with anything less than Premier League and Champions League football - despite being contracted at the Etihad Stadium until 2034.

Could Haaland join Barcelona?

As City prepare for the worst as the outcome of their appeal looms, other European giants will no doubt be keeping close as they consider a potential swoop - with Haaland the pick of the bunch.

And while Barcelona's financial woes have been well documented in recent years, Brassell believes they would not pass up the chance to sign the Premier League's top goalscorer at a cut price.

He told talkSPORT: "Everyone always says that about Barcelona [their finances]. But the fact is they are back at the Camp Nou now. They do have more to spend than previously.

“Look, if you'd have asked this about Erling Haaland six months, a year ago, you'd get an absolute no way. It's not possible.

6 Haaland was won the Premier League Golden Boot in three of his four seasons in England Credit: Getty

6 Could Haaland follow Anthony Gordon from the Premier League to the Camp Nou? Credit: Getty

“But Manchester City's situation is what it is. I can't see him suiting up for them in the Championship.

“So, immediately, what's clear at first is if Erling Haaland is going to leave Manchester City, it's going to require a pay cut. There's no one else who's paying him what Manchester City is paying him."

While Haaland's arrival in any team would guarantee plenty of goals, Barcelona certainly haven't struggled in this area this term.

The Spanish giants have scored more goals than any other club in Europe's top five leagues with an astonishing 48 goals - 17 more than nearest rivals Real Madrid on 31.

However, they have done so without an established No.9, having failed to replace their main source of goals in the summer after Robert Lewandowski's departure for Chicago Fire, while Ferran Torres also left to join PSG.

With their pursuit of Julian Alvarez falling through, Brassell believes Barca could make Haaland if he becomes available at the right price.

6 Barcelona's star duo Lamine Yamal and Raphinha have shouldered goalscoring responsibilities this term without an out-and-out striker Credit: Getty

He added: "From a Barcelona perspective, you look at it and think they've scored at an unbelievable rate so far this season - which is so surprising, given that they didn't get Julian Alvarez and that they lost some valuable sources of goals last season - Lewandowski, Ferran, Marcus Rashford.

“Also, just to go back and reiterate - they did not spend that Julian Alvarez money. I don't know what Manchester City could charge for Erling Haaland, say, if they were playing in the Championship.

“And I'm guessing, because of the relationship that Erling Haaland has with Man City, I think rather than downing tools until he was sold, I think he would probably work with City to find the right deal.

“The fact is, if they've got to get rid of ten, 12 players - which is not an impossibility if they were to find themselves in the division below, or doomed to relegation and not in the Champions League, whatever the final agreed punishment is - they're not going to be able to sell all these players for the value that they are.

"They're going to have to get a lot of players off the wage bill."

Brassell explained: “I guess we're talking about Erling Haaland at slightly lower than market rate, or maybe even slightly lower than market rate. So it does bring Barcelona back into the equation.

6 Haaland has scored a staggering 176 goals in 212 games for Manchester City Credit: Getty

6

“And I think really, Barcelona are always going to be like they are under [president] Joan Laporta - going for the big stars, speculating to accumulate, that approach.

“And I do think when you look at the speed and the flexibility of that front part of the Barcelona team, you can see exactly how he would click.

"You look at that 2022/23 treble-winning season, and just the width of that, the front of that Manchester City team, you could see how it would fit really, really well.”

"If you had a little question, it would be, 'Does he press vigorously enough? Is he involved enough?'

"He's not an Anthony Gordon, I think it's fair to say. But if he's out there, Barcelona are definitely in the mix.

"The fact that they didn't get Julian Alvarez, and there's the feeling that Atletico really don't want to do business with Barcelona, then that sort of makes you think they're going to have to look elsewhere."

While Brassell admitted bitter rivals Real Madrid are also likely to join the race for Haaland should he become available, he reiterated that Barca will be right in the mix too.

He rounded off: "If City are selling, Barcelona are interested for sure."

Sports.title: Simon Jordan defends Stan Kroenke as mystery loan has Arsenal fans demanding answers
Sports.content:
Simon Jordan believes Arsenal owner Stan Kroenke has no obligation to provide answers for curious fans over a personal loan.

Kroenke sparked the intrigue of Gunners supporters when, as part of a loan with Deutsche Bank, he used the club's shares, broadcast income and the training ground as security.



2 Gunners owner Kroenke is worth an estimated £20billion Credit: Getty

But Jordan leapt to Kroenke's defence and claimed using the items listed as collateral was 'standard fare' in football.

Simon Jordan's verdict on Stan Kroenke's loan

"The big question is, how much is it (the loan), what was it for, how has it affected Arsenal and what jeopardy does it put Arsenal in," Jordan said on Thursday's White and Jordan.

"I would suggest that, currently, there's not a lot of concern, is there? Arsenal are Premier League champions. Their investment into the football club over the last four, five years has been significant. The evolution of the football club has been far more compelling than it has been in some time.



"Whilst they might want answers, it's not an obligation upon the ownership to provide them."

The size of Kroenke's loan involving the Arsenal assets has not been disclosed, although City AM reports the Gunners owner has every intention of pumping the funds back into the club.



It was also reported the funds are not being used to help bankroll another one of Kroenke's sports teams or for his own personal use.

What did the Arsenal Supporters Trust say about Stan Kroenke's loan?

But it has not stopped the Arsenal Supporters Trust (AST) from seeking clarification over Kroenke's loan.



"We are assured that this process is a rearrangement of the existing debt structure," the AST said in a statement.

"Whilst KSE remains the primary lender to Arsenal, Barclays loan arrangements have ended. KSE has had a long standing loan arrangement with Deutsche Bank going back to the full takeover in 2018. The KSE debt to Deutsche Bank is now to be secured by the assets of Arsenal."

The AST statement continued: "The club first took on substantial debt to pay for the Emirates Stadium in the early 2000s. Since then there has been a charge against the stadium and revenues.

2 Arsenal was forced to restrict its spending due to the construction of the Emirates, which was completed in 2006 Credit: Getty



"Whilst stadium security was previously provided to Barclays Bank this charge has been satisfied and released. This indicates that short term working capital and overdraft facilities will be provided by KSE from the Deutsche loan."

The AST added it has requested the club to provide further updates regarding Kroenke's loan at the Arsenal Advisory Board's next meeting in December.

Stan Kroenke's sprawling sports empire

News of Kroenke's mystery loan comes as his company, Kroenke Sports and Entertainment (KSE), closes in on the acquisition of Major League Baseball (MLB) franchise Los Angeles Angels.

The transaction is valued at an eye-watering $4billion (£3bn) and is expected to be completed in January.



Once the deal is complete, the Angels will become the only MLB team under the KSE umbrella.

Other teams owned by KSE include the Los Angeles Rams (NFL), Denver Nuggets (NBA), Colorado Avalanche (NHL), Colorado Rapids (MLS) and lacrosse team Colorado Mammoth.

Intriguingly, all of the KSE-owned teams, with the exception of the Rapids, have won their respective leagues since 2021.

Sports.title: Simon Jordan: This is my advice to Amad Diallo after ‘shut your mouth’ spat with fan
Sports.content:
Simon Jordan: This is my advice to Amad Diallo after ‘shut your mouth’ spat with fan

Amad Diallo told a content creator: 'Shut your mouth' in a viral social media exchange.

The Manchester United forward snapped back at an Instagram user following criticism after the Ivory Coast's draw with Gambia.

3 Diallo hit back directly at the fan in a social media outburst Credit: Getty

Diallo provided an assist in Tuesday's Africa Cup of Nations qualifier, but was unable to help his side claim all three points.

Instead, he came under fire in the aftermath of the match for hitting the crossbar from close range.

The criticism appeared to strike a nerve with Diallo, who furiously replied to one fan's video assessment on Instagram.

Commenting on the post, he wrote: "Just shut your mouth, bro. You’re talking too much now. Go play in my place if it bothers you that much."

His reaction quickly went viral, with screenshots of the response being shared across multiple social media platforms.

Jordan's advice for Diallo

talkSPORT's Simon Jordan came to Diallo's defence on Thursday, but admitted he needs to remember his high profile in such incidents.

Speaking on White and Jordan, the former Crystal Palace chairman explained: "You look at this and go, why would you want to give this individual that’s operating in the digital space any credibility?

"Because all you’re going to do is give him more recognisability, more followers, more people that relate to what he’s doing because you’ve just given him the credibility. You have just given him that credibility.

"We also know tragically that there is an industry of people called influencers that are taken quite seriously by commercial brands that want to use them to be able to gain currency with various generations of potential consumers or people they want to influence.

"So there’s a flip side of that which means that in a social and digital age sometimes people like me can just say ignore them and have no opinion on what they say and don’t get involved in it.

3 Jordan has defended Diallo for his reaction but advised him to 'remember' who he is Credit: Getty

"But there’s also this traction that can be gained from what people say about you and sometimes you have to nip it in the bud.

"Nipping it in the bud is probably being quite clever and putting them on the spot. If you feel the necessity to involve yourself in a conversation with somebody that’s not particularly complimentary about them you should be wise about how you do it.

"Not get into a conversation that takes it down to the vernacular, but these are young kids and they’ve grown up in a social media age.

"He needs to remind himself that he is the elite professional footballer and the guy sitting on a keyboard in his mum’s bedroom is not."

Diallo's recent form

Diallo is into his sixth full season with United having arrived from Atalanta in January 2021.

Whilst he has become a fan favourite at Old Trafford, he has not scored for the Red Devils since December 15, 2025, a run spanning 25 matches.

3 Diallo was criticised after hitting the bar from close range for the Ivory Coast against Gambia Credit: AFP

Injury absences have contribute to his goal drought, though, with Diallo making just eight appearances across all competitions so far this term.

Meanwhile, at international level, he has now won 25 caps for the Elephants.

The 24-year-old started his nation's latest match in Bakau, Gambia before being withdrawn in the 65th minute.

Ivory Coast were leading at the time after Diallo had set up Luck Zogbe for the opener.

However, his costly miss saw the visitors squander the chance to double their lead before Gambia turned the match on its head with two goals of their own.

Only an equaliser in the eighth minute of stoppage-time for the Ivory Coast salvaged a draw.

Sports.title: Blackpool sack their manager just seven hours after wishing him happy birthday: 'Have a great day, Gaffer!'
Sports.content:
Blackpool sack their manager just seven hours after wishing him happy birthday: 'Have a great day, Gaffer!'

Blackpool have sacked manager Ian Evatt just hours after wishing him a happy birthday.

Evatt had been in charge for a year and his final match was Saturday's 1-0 away defeat by fellow strugglers AFC Wimbledon, when his squad was decimated by illness. The result left the Seasiders immediately above the League One relegation zone and followed a run of one win and six defeats in ten league games.

Blackpool’s social media team had earlier wished Evatt a happy 45th birthday with the pay-off line: 'Have a great day, Gaffer!'

Three hours later, Evatt was relieved of his duties, and the club began the search for their ninth manager in eight years.

Evatt’s contract was set to run until June 2028. He joined last October following his exit from Bolton Wanderers in January 2025.

Blackpool later thanked the 45-year-old for his efforts during his time with the club.

Blackpool sacked manager Ian Evatt just hours after wishing him a happy 45th birthday

Blackpool posted the birthday message just after 9am in the morning, with Evatt's sacking then confirmed at 4pm

JORDAN'S OFFER TO SEND SACKED BOSS A BIRTHDAY CARD Former Crystal Palace chairman Simon Jordan famously claimed to have sacked Trevor Francis on his birthday back in 2003. Francis' dismissal has become an often told tale, with Jordan writing sixteen years after the event that he had even offered to send the former England star a birthday card. Recent reports have also involved the suggestion that Francis had mumbled 'but its my birthday' back to Jordan when he was given his marching orders. Whether these events played out as told are unclear. But Crystal Palace officially announced Francis' departure on April 18 in 2003, with his birthday falling a day later. 'I am totally committed to playing in the Premier League and I will ensure the new manager can achieve this aspiration,' Jordan wrote on Crystal Palace's website at the time. 'I would like to thank Trevor for all his hard work and would like to wish him the very best for the future.' Jordan then turned on the players, adding: 'I'm not watching next year what I've had to watch this year. At times we've been a disgrace. 'I've asked the management staff to tell me who should go. They can see the players who are performing and those who are not and you will see in the summer, out they will go. The players will be told when it suits me. I care about them as much they care about me.' Francis had reportedly told his players in a parting shot: 'Well, lads, I've been sacked – have a good summer holiday.' Palace appointed Steve Kember as manager in the summer and despite Jordan's hopes of automatic promotion, rather than the play-offs, found themselves in a relegation battle in November. Iain Dowie was appointed as manager the following month and guided Palace into the play-offs, with the Eagles triumphing in Cardiff to secure promotion to the top flight.

Steve Thompson will step in to take charge of the team against Wigan Athletic this weekend, his fourth spell as caretaker, alongside Stephen Crainey, Stephen Dobbie and Steve Banks.

During a hugely successful playing career at Bloomfield Road, Evatt made over 250 appearances for Blackpool. In his six years at the club, he played a vital role in their rise from League One to the Premier League, which included two successful play-off campaigns.

On arrival as a manager, he amassed 13 points from a possible 15 in December 2025 to lift them out of the relegation zone, although they lost ten and won two of their next 15 matches in all competitions.

They finished the campaign strongly, with six wins in seven games as part of a sequence of one defeat in 13 between mid-March and the end of August, only to struggle again this season.

Sports.title: Andriy Shevchenko hits back at explosive Mykhailo Mudryk claims in blame game over failed drugs test: Ukraine chief accuses £89m star of 'slander' and demands apology
Sports.content:
Andriy Shevchenko hits back at explosive Mykhailo Mudryk claims in blame game over failed drugs test: Ukraine chief accuses £89m star of 'slander' and demands apology

Mykhailo Mudryk has been accused of 'baseless slander' by Ukraine FA (UAF) president Andriy Shevchenko after the former blamed his failed drugs test on the national team's setup.

Between November 2024 and July 2026, Mudryk was banned from football after testing positive for the substance meldonium.

The 25-year-old, who is currently on loan at Tottenham from Chelsea, was initially handed a four-year ban after being charged by the Football Association for failing a doping test. He was able to return when a seismic resolution was struck after changes to the 'scientific reporting standards'.

In a bombshell two-hour interview with Ukrainian journalist Dmitry Gordon via his YouTube channel, Mudryk laid the blame for his situation with the Ukraine national team - something Shevchenko vehemently denies.

'Loud statements have been made about the UAF and the Ukrainian national team. This is baseless slander against our people, who do their work honestly and professionally,' the UAF president said in a statement to The Athletic.

Shevchenko, who played for Chelsea during his time, doubled down on his stance by declaring Mudryk should apologise for his accusations if he has no evidence to substantiate them.

Mykhailo Mudryk (left) has been accused of 'baseless slander' by Ukraine FA (UAF) president Andriy Shevchenko after he blamed his failed drugs test on the national team's setup

Mudryk has won 28 caps for Ukraine but is yet to represent them since his ban was overturned

'After Mykhailo became a Chelsea player, the club sent a letter to the UAF requesting that he not be given any medication during national team training camps,' he continued.

'The national team staff complied with this request. Head coach Serhiy Rebrov also approved for Mykhailo to have two of his personal specialists work with him at the training camps. These were the exact people who monitored his regimen and recovery, and helped him with his daily routine.

'The UAF completed all necessary checks in this case. We provided Mudryk's representatives with the information they requested and remained in contact with those working on the case.

'I know the people who have worked with the national team for many years. I trust them, because throughout all this time there have been no incidents in the team that could make anyone doubt their professionalism. If Mykhailo has evidence to back up his words, let him provide it. If no such evidence exists, I expect him to publicly retract his accusations and apologize to the people whose honesty and professionalism he has called into question.'

In his interview, Mudryk - who is yet to add to his 28 caps for his country since returning from his ban - laid the blame at Ukraine's door.

'I had never heard of a drug like meldonium, never seen it, never come across it in my life. I only learned about it when they told me the news. I definitely have ideas. It's a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe,' the winger said.

'This drug could only have got into my body where I was, and that's Ukraine. There are no such drugs in England. It supposedly stimulates your heart and helps you, as far as I understand, handle physical load better.

'I was at home and Chelsea's management came to see me and they said we needed to talk. Then they say you've returned a positive doping test and now you're facing a ban.

He is currently on loan at Tottenham from Chelsea but has only played once so far this season

'You can't believe it's true. You can't believe this is happening to you. If I'd ever taken anything anywhere, I'd have understood that this conversation might happen one day.

'At least I'd have understood it was possible. But when you spend a huge pile of money on watching your diet, on a nutritionist, on a chef. When you spend that much money every year on all these things, that's the last thing you expect. Because it speaks for itself: that you take things very seriously, like nutrition, everything that goes into your body, you watch it very closely.

'Otherwise there'd be no need to spend money on it, because you could manage without it. They tell you this news, and you sit there, and you kind of listen to them but don't hear them.

'At some point you just go into a trance. It feels like you're falling in a dream off a skyscraper. You're flying down, you feel yourself flying down, and only in a dream do you wake up when you hit the ground, but in real life you don't wake up, you just keep falling. It hits you very hard mentally. At that moment the tears came later.'

Mudryk, who joined Chelsea for £89million from Shakhtar Donetsk, has only made one substitute appearance for Tottenham so far this season due to an ankle injury.
