Sports.title: Devin Haney Refuses To Admit Ryan Garcia Exposed His Style
Sports.content:
Devin Haney is still trying to convince fans he knows how to beat Ryan Garcia in a rematch, yet he refuses to admit what actually happened in their first fight. During his appearance on Club Shay Shay, Haney kept falling back on the same old excuse about Garcia’s left hook, calling them “PED punches.”

“It’s boxing. You get caught,” said Haney on Club Shay Shay. “But those PED punches … they were a little different.” Later, when asked whether he’d ever felt that kind of power in the division, he went right back to the positive drug test again.

Ostarine does not make a fighter drop his right hand every time he throws a jab. That was Haney’s biggest problem all night. He kept stepping forward behind his jab, ducking his head, and lunging in to clinch with his right glove down at his chest. Garcia saw that bad habit from a mile away and timed him with left hooks over the top. You do not need banned substances to hit a guy whose chin is sitting wide open.

Haney boasted about getting off the canvas three times, saying it proves he can take a punch. He also broke down what Conor Benn did wrong when Benn walked into Garcia’s shots. It is funny how Haney can spot another fighter’s mistakes from ringside, yet he still refuses to look in the mirror and fix his own. Until he admits his style is tailor-made for Garcia’s left hook, a rematch will end the exact same way.

Before Haney even thinks about fixing his mistakes for Garcia, he’s got to deal with IBF welterweight champ Liam Paro on December 19. You can tell Haney wants that Garcia rematch badly because the first fight wrecked his reputation with fans and killed his leverage at the negotiating table.

Looking past Paro is a massive mistake, though. If Haney loses that unification fight, he isn’t getting near a Garcia rematch anytime soon unless he’s willing to walk in coming off a loss, and you know the purse split would be totally against him in that spot.

Sports.title: Canelo Alvarez Given WBC Green Light for Willy Hutchinson, Will Eddy Reynoso Block It?
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez has a clear path back to 175 pounds if he wants it. WBC president Mauricio Sulaiman told Sky Sports on Thursday that the sanctioning body would approve a fight between Canelo and WBC light heavyweight champion Willy Hutchinson as Hutchinson’s first title defense.

The WBC discussed Hutchinson’s mandatory status at its convention in Acapulco, but Sulaiman confirmed the organization left the division without an official ruling. Without a mandatory challenger ordered, the Scottish fighter could move directly from his November 7 decision win over Joshua Buatsi into a bout with Canelo.

The next move is with Canelo, who reclaimed the WBC super middleweight belt by outpointing Christian Mbilli on October 31.

“It would certainly be approved, champion against champion,” Sulaiman said to Sky Sports regarding a potential Canelo move back up to light heavyweight.

The real issue may not be the WBC, however, but trainer Eddy Reynoso. Once Reynoso scouts the Buatsi tape and sees Hutchinson’s length, lateral movement, and busy jab, he could easily decide the stylistic headache outweighs the reward of another belt at 175.

Moving up to face Hutchinson would certainly be courageous on Canelo’s part, yet there is a big difference between courage and plain common sense. Behind the scenes, it would be no surprise to see Reynoso steer Canelo toward safer, more lucrative waters at 168 against someone like Hamzah Sheeraz, defending his newly reclaimed title against a big UK draw rather than spending 12 frustrating rounds trying to track down Hutchinson.

Hutchinson’s win over Buatsi showed why he would be a problem fight for Canelo. He used his footwork to create space for counters and banked early rounds before Buatsi’s pressure and body work began to close the distance. Two judges scored the bout 115-113, proving Hutchinson can be made uncomfortable when forced to defend on the inside. For Canelo, the main question is whether he can apply steady pressure early enough to keep Hutchinson from building a large lead.

In past losses to Dmitry Bivol and Terence Crawford, Canelo struggled against fighters who controlled distance and refused to stand in front of him. Bivol used a jab to dictate the distance and fired combinations whenever Canelo stood behind his high guard. Crawford frequently changed angles, made Canelo miss, and countered before Canelo could move his feet. Hutchinson utilizes a similar formula. He scores with a sharp jab, follows up with quick combinations, and moves out of range before Canelo can return fire.

Against Mbilli in Riyadh, Canelo benefited from an opponent who marched forward and offered steady counterpunching opportunities. Hutchinson would force Canelo to be the aggressor, slip the initial shot, and exit before the second punch comes. Canelo carries the heavier power when he closes the distance, yet Hutchinson is capable of winning rounds on activity and movement while Canelo looks for a single opening. Allowing Hutchinson to control the early tempo would leave Canelo chasing the fight by the midpoint.

Canelo previously captured a light heavyweight title by stopping Sergey Kovalev in 2019 before dropping a decision to Bivol in his only other appearance at 175. Buatsi provided a workable blueprint for getting to Hutchinson through sustained forward pressure and targeted body shots. Canelo possesses the tools to execute that same game plan, provided he starts fast and stays committed even when Hutchinson makes him miss.

Sports.title: Simon Jordan Tells Eddie Hearn To Shut His Gob Over Fury vs. Joshua Undercard
Sports.content:
Simon Jordan is dead right to tell Eddie Hearn to shut his gob about the Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua undercard. Hearn has been running around bellyaching that the December 11 bill at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff is weak, even though he and Frank Warren spent years failing to make the main event happen themselves.

“If Eddie Hearn pops up telling you he could do an undercard that’s better, that’s fabulous, but you couldn’t make the main event. So sit down and shut up,” Jordan said on talkSPORT Boxing. “You and Frank [Warren], with respect, had years to make this fight.”

Now that somebody else finally got Fury and Joshua across the finish line, Hearn wants to act like he has all the answers for the undercard. The truth is, Hearn has no vision and no clue what fans actually want to see. Looking at the fights he floated to iFL TV, fans should be glad he is not running the show.

Hearn bragged to iFL TV that Joe Cordina had agreed to terms to face Manny Pacquiao, who turns 48 in December, and also wanted to throw Cordina in with WBO lightweight champion Abdullah Mason. Putting a Welsh two-time titleholder like Cordina on the card might please the local Cardiff crowd, as Jordan noted, but it does nothing for fans watching in the U.S. and Canada, and regular Brits barely care either. Zuffa got it right by leaving him off the show.

Giving a 34-year-old Cordina an undeserved title shot against Mason makes zero sense anyway. Cordina has not fought a good opponent since his eighth-round blowout loss to Anthony Cacace back in May 2024. That was ages ago, and beating Jaret Gonzalez Quiroz and Gabriel Flores Jr. since then does not earn him a shot at Mason.

Dragging a 47-year-old Pacquiao out to face Cordina is even worse. Pacquiao’s name might trick a few casual American fans into glancing at the poster, but nobody in North America is paying to watch Cordina. He was never a draw in America even when he held a belt at super featherweight.

The rest of Hearn’s matchmaking ideas are just as weak. Wanting Dave Allen to face Andy Ruiz Jr. or sticking Pacquiao in with Jack Catterall, Conah Walker, or Lewis Crocker sounds like a desperate attempt to unload Matchroom fighters onto a giant pay-per-view stage.

Jordan is dead right that the organizers need real fights before Fury and Joshua make their ring walks around 1 a.m., because fans shelling out big money deserve better than cheap filler. Hearn whining from the sidelines while pitching washed-up legends and domestic mismatches just proves Zuffa was smart to ignore him.

Sports.title: Low WBO Bid Would Expose Shakur Stevenson Real Value
Sports.content:
Shakur Stevenson needs to vacate his WBO light welterweight title right now before the November 30 purse bid exposes what promoters actually think he is worth. WBO president Gustavo Olivieri ordered the bid for 11 a.m. Atlantic time (10 a.m. ET) at WBO headquarters in San Juan, Puerto Rico, and the organization plans to stream the entire thing live on social media for his mandatory defense against Raymond Muratalla.

If a live-streamed WBO purse bid comes back at $3 million or $3.5 million, every promoter in boxing gets hard proof that Shakur’s open-market value is a fraction of what he demands.

Those last three paydays on Turki Alalshikh cards against Josh Padley, William Zepeda, and Teofimo Lopez clearly warped Stevenson’s view of his own drawing power. He started acting like a Canelo Alvarez-level attraction, even reportedly walking away from a $7 million offer from Zuffa Boxing to fight Jose Valenzuela because he wanted $15 million.

If $7 million was too low for Valenzuela, Stevenson is obviously not taking $3 million to $3.2 million from a purse bid to risk his unbeaten record against a heavy-handed puncher like Muratalla (25-0, 17 KOs). None of his last three opponents he’s beaten hit as hard as Muratalla, who gave up his IBF lightweight belt to chase this shot at 140 pounds.

By dropping the WBO strap before November 30, Stevenson can control the story, pretend he is moving on to bigger fights against Devin Haney or Gervonta Davis, and avoid the embarrassment of watching a low bid go viral. That leaves Muratalla waiting for the WBO to work down its top 15 rankings to find a contender willing to fight him for the vacant title.

An ultra-low winning bid on November 30th brands Shakur as a non-draw without Saudi money. Rival fighters like Devin Haney, Ryan Garcia, and Gervonta Davis already use Stevenson’s defensive style and ticket-selling history against him in negotiations. A low winning bid hands them ammunition to demand an 80-20 or 75-25 split in their favor whenever talks start, arguing that Stevenson cannot generate revenue unless Turki Alalshikh is writing the check.

Sports.title: Matchroom Weighs Quick Teremoana Return After Ahio Fight
Sports.content:
Matchroom is considering a quick return for Teremoana Teremoana after his second-round stoppage of Hemi Ahio. Promoter Frank Smith said the team would decide within 24 to 48 hours whether to get him out again soon. Petar Milas looks like a sensible next opponent if Matchroom wants to move Teremoana up a level and give him a chance to get some rounds in.

Teremoana called for a shot at Australian heavyweight champion Ivan Ivić, saying he’d heard he was the mandatory challenger. Smith said Matchroom had already made Ivić several offers for what he called “really good money,” and the champion hadn’t taken the fight. With several Matchroom cards coming up, there’s little reason to build the next date around an opponent Smith says has already passed.

“If he wanted to get out quickly again, that’s something we are looking at right now,” said Smith after the Ahio fight. He said he wanted to give Teremoana time to rest after the fight and the training camp before making a decision.

Milas is ranked one place above Teremoana on the IBF list discussed here. That’s the kind of incremental move that makes sense on a short turnaround. Guido Vianello would be a tougher option, while Efe Ajagba or Justis Huni would represent a bigger jump. Milas is a matchmaking option, and Smith gave no indication that Matchroom had approached him.

Teremoana said he’d leave the opponent to his team. He also said he wanted Ahio to get up after the second knockdown because he wanted more ring time. That gives Matchroom a clear brief if it brings him back quickly. Find someone who can extend him past the early rounds and make him work for a win.

The bigger question is whether Teremoana’s team is trying to manufacture an artificial fighter designed to make a big killing without ever facing anyone dangerous. If this is all just artifice to build a hype job and create a pseudo star, we won’t see a true step up in opposition for his next fight.

Some fans believe Matchroom ran that exact same play with Anthony Joshua, who was matched carefully through much of his career and made massive money without beating high-level opposition. Once Joshua finally stepped in against the real thing, he lost to Oleksandr Usyk and Daniel Dubois.

If that is the blueprint for Teremoana, it could be a long time before he faces a genuinely good opponent, and by the time it happens, there will likely be huge money on the line.

Sports.title: O’Shaquie Foster May Have to Earn Shakur at 140
Sports.content:
O’Shaquie Foster is still pushing for a fight with Shakur Stevenson, but his path to getting it likely runs through a credible light welterweight contender first. Shakur is focused on lucrative matchups, and Foster brings a sharp counterpunching style capable of spoiling his night on the scorecards without generating the ticket sales or viewership to make the gamble worthwhile.

Foster revived the callout after Stevenson reached out to congratulate him. While Foster acknowledged the gesture and praised Stevenson as a great fighter, he made it clear that their fractured relationship keeps the matchup personal for him.

“We had a good relationship back then, but it’s where it’s at now,” Foster told Fight Hub TV. “So, you know, we still need to make that happen across the ring from each other.”

According to Foster, “stuff was said” and “the lines was crossed.” Still, the push for the bout has come almost entirely from his side. Stevenson’s message gave Foster an opening to put his name back in the mix, while Shakur has shown minimal public interest in taking the bait.

If Shakur ever warms up to the idea, he will almost certainly demand the fight at 140. That puts the pressure on Foster to move up from 130 and handle the extra weight. Foster has the patience to make Stevenson lead and work harder than he wants to, though proving he can hold his ground and make his counters hurt against natural junior welterweights remains an unanswered question.

Stepping up to 140 will make the fight against Shakur possible, and beating an established name in the division would give Foster real leverage at the negotiating table. The catch is that he would be taking on a dangerous opponent with no promise that Stevenson waits on the other side. Foster has the personal motivation to take that chance, yet Stevenson still requires a payday large enough to justify risking an upset.

Sports.title: No Handouts: Crawford Demands Canelo Shot for Lester Martínez After His Own Shortcut
Sports.content:
Terence Crawford wants to know why Lester Martínez is still waiting for a shot at Canelo Álvarez, though he is overlooking the business and boxing realities that put Christian Mbilli in line first.

Mbilli held the full WBC super middleweight title, which Canelo won from him by decision on October 31. Martínez holds only the interim belt and does not bring the leverage, name value, or resume needed to force his way into a massive payday.

Crawford and Martínez trained together under Brian “BoMac” McIntyre, who still coaches Martínez and prepared Crawford for his 2025 victory over Canelo. Loyalty to a former gymmate clearly played a role when Crawford focused on WBC president Mauricio Sulaimán on X, pointing out that Mbilli and Martínez fought to a draw:

“I don’t get it. It’s crazy how the @wbcmoro say Lester not good enough to fight @Canelo but Mbilli was. This the type of stuff I don’t like with these sanction bodies, they pick and choose. How being the interim champion not good enough for a chance at the championship.”

What Crawford leaves out is how Canelo’s career actually operates at this stage. Canelo is being paid enormous money by Turki Alalshikh, and Turki is focused on global spectacles, not charity mandatories for fighters the casual public has never heard of. Outside of hardcore boxing circles, Martínez is virtually unknown, and complaining on social media will not talk him into a fight he has not earned.

There is also a glaring double standard in Crawford’s complaint. Crawford himself received a massive shortcut in 2025 when he was allowed to skip the entire 160-pound division and jump straight to the front of the line to challenge Canelo for the undisputed 168-pound championship without facing a number one contender or grinding through the mandatory path. Nothing about that was fair.

Crawford got the fight because Turki liked him, and he was lucky to even arrive there undefeated after struggling badly in his previous bout against Israil Madrimov. Many fans felt Crawford lost that fight, yet he escaped with the decision, bypassed the sharks at middleweight and super middleweight, and walked straight into a title shot he had not earned in the division.

Even after winning the belts, Crawford did not rush to defend them against dangerous, low-reward fighters like Martínez or IBF champion Osleys Iglesias before stepping away.

Now Crawford is upset that his former gymmate is not receiving the same special treatment. Martínez has none of Crawford’s star power or backing, and his thin resume does not justify a handout. He did not look impressive in his interim title bouts against Immanuwel Aleem in March or Luka Plantić over the summer, and he was fortunate to escape the Mbilli fight with a draw after leaning heavily on excessive shoving while the referee let it slide.

If Crawford wants his former gymmate to land a fight with Canelo, the answer is simple: tell him to go earn it in the ring. Martínez needs real wins over legitimate opposition like IBF champion Osleys Iglesias, Darius Fulghum, Bektemir Melikuziev, or top middleweights moving up like Janibek Alimkhanuly and Carlos Adames. Until he beats serious threats and builds a case the public cares about, Canelo has no reason to give him the time of day.

Sports.title: Devin Haney Says Shakur Stevenson Fight “Has to Happen”
Sports.content:
Devin Haney is already talking about a fight with Shakur Stevenson like it’s a sure thing, claiming it “has to happen.” Looking at the rest of the welterweight division, you can’t blame him for eyeing that payday.

Outside of a Ryan Garcia rematch, nobody else brings the kind of money and spotlight that Stevenson does. The problem is that Haney is looking way too far ahead. He still has to survive Liam Paro first, and Garcia is lurking right behind him.

“I think that it has to happen. I think it’s just a big fight,” Haney said during an appearance on Shannon Sharpe’s Club Shay Shay. “I think that he’s going to keep winning. I’m going to keep winning, and eventually we’re going to have to meet.”

Realistically, Teofimo Lopez is one of the only other fighters who can help Haney sell a massive event. Conor Benn might get there if he keeps stacking wins, and Keyshawn Davis is still building up to that level of star power.

Guys like Richardson Hitchins, Rolly Romero, and Brian Norman Jr. would all make for solid matchups, yet none of them spark the kind of heated debate that Haney versus Stevenson does. Fans have argued for years over who has the sharper skills, and they will gladly open their wallets to settle it.

The problem Haney has is that there’s no way of knowing whether Shakur’s career will go downhill. He’s already lost almost an entire year on his extended victory lap after beating Teofimo last January. What we’re seeing here from Shakur is his chase of exclusively big paydays sidelining him, causing him to lose out on that great gig he had with Zuffa.

Haney needs to focus on putting the fight together with Shakur as soon as possible while he’s still in demand. The way his career looks now, it’s following in the same direction as the Charlo brothers. Jermell and Jermall went from headlining major events to sitting on the shelf for roughly three years, and by the time they finally resurfaced, the sport had moved right past them. Now they are stuck fighting on undercards for a fraction of what they used to make.

If Stevenson walks away from the Raymond Muratalla purse bid over low money, he is heading straight down that exact same path. That puts the pressure squarely on Haney to push for this fight immediately before Stevenson tanks his own value.

Ghana News.title: We must never forget this man
Ghana News.content:
Inspector Issa Kanjarga: The Ghanaian Police Officer Who Defied A Colonial Order And Helped Prevent A Massacre On 28 February 1948.

Imagine standing in front of a crowd of unarmed men, knowing that your superior has ordered you to open fire. You are wearing the same uniform, carrying the same weapon, and serving under the same colonial authority. But at that moment, you must make a decision: obey the order or save lives.

On February 28, 1948, at Christiansborg Castle in Accra, a Gold Coast police officer reportedly made a decision that would put him on the wrong side of his colonial superiors but earn him a place in Ghana’s history.

His name was Inspector Issa Kanjarga.

He defined his superior, and screamed in an indigenous language that his colleagues should not obey orders to fire on their own compatriots.

Ghana News.title: From Toronto Driveways to African Ports: Inside a $4.5 million stolen-car network
Ghana News.content:
The international trade in stolen luxury vehicles has suffered a major setback after Peel Regional Police in Canada arrested 12 people and recovered 96 stolen vehicles valued at approximately $4.5 million in an extensive investigation into an alleged organised auto-theft network.

The operation, code-named Project Cadetta, uncovered what investigators describe as a sophisticated criminal network involved in stealing, concealing, transporting and exporting high-value vehicles from the Greater Toronto Area (GTA).

According to a news release issued on November 16, 2026, Peel Regional Police laid 231 charges following an investigation launched in March 2026 in partnership with the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA).

At the centre of the investigation was a warehouse in Brampton, which police allege was being used as a major staging point where stolen vehicles were concealed inside shipping containers before being transported towards Canadian ports for export to West Africa.

However, investigators say the operation extended well beyond the warehouse.

Police allege that they uncovered a wider criminal network operating across the GTA and surrounding jurisdictions, with five key suspects responsible for coordinating the theft, movement and export of stolen vehicles.

Other accused individuals allegedly played supporting roles at different stages of the operation, including loading vehicles, moving shipping containers and transporting vehicles whose identification numbers had allegedly been altered.

The recovery of 96 vehicles has raised questions about how many stolen cars may have already left Canada and reached international markets before investigators could intercept them.

An organised criminal supply chain beyond the driveway

Project Cadetta highlights how organised vehicle theft can extend far beyond the individuals who physically steal vehicles.

Investigators allege that the operation involved several layers of criminal activity, from stealing vehicles to transporting, concealing and preparing them for export.

The findings are particularly concerning because stolen vehicles are not simply disappearing from residential driveways. According to police, some are allegedly being channelled into international shipping networks through organised criminal operations.

Deputy Chief Nick Milinovich of Peel Regional Police described organised auto theft as a predatory business model operated by transnational criminal syndicates.

He said Project Cadetta had helped dismantle the alleged supply chain, from street-level thieves to international export brokers.

The 96 vehicles recovered included luxury sport utility vehicles (SUVs), pickup trucks and other high-value models. Their estimated combined value is $4.5 million.

Of the 12 individuals arrested and charged, nine were released with future court dates, while three were initially held for bail hearings and subsequently released.

Police also confirmed that arrest warrants had been issued for additional individuals and that further charges were anticipated as investigations continued.

Ghana and Nigeria in the international auto-theft investigation

For Ghanaians and Nigerians, particularly those living in Canada and those involved in the international vehicle trade, Project Cadetta carries an important cross-border dimension.

Previous auto-theft investigations in the GTA have raised concerns about criminal networks allegedly shipping stolen Canadian vehicles to West African destinations, including Ghana and Nigeria.

In earlier investigations, York Regional Police uncovered alleged networks involving vehicle thieves, traffickers and individuals responsible for loading stolen vehicles into shipping containers for export.

One such operation, Project Victory, resulted in the recovery of 70 stolen vehicles valued at approximately $4.5 million. Police also linked the alleged network to 32 stolen vehicles that had been shipped to Ghana or Nigeria.

Another investigation, Project Majestic, focused on the theft of Lexus, Toyota and Honda SUVs.

These investigations demonstrate why Canadian authorities are increasingly treating organised auto theft as a cross-border and international criminal activity rather than simply a local property offence.

However, the nationalities of those arrested in Project Cadetta have not been established in the police announcement. It would therefore be inaccurate to associate the accused with any particular nationality without confirmation from investigators or court records.

Similarly, the recovery of vehicles allegedly destined for overseas markets does not mean that every person purchasing a luxury vehicle in Ghana or Nigeria is connected to criminal activity.

Nevertheless, the investigations raise important questions for international vehicle buyers, shipping companies, vehicle dealers and port authorities about the movement and resale of stolen vehicles across borders.

What happens to vehicles already shipped overseas?

One of the major questions emerging from these investigations concerns vehicles that may have left Canada before police could identify and recover them.

In previous investigations in the GTA, police reported that stolen vehicles were transported to the Port of Montreal, sometimes by road and sometimes in shipping containers moved by rail, before being loaded onto vessels bound for overseas destinations.

This presents a significant challenge for Canadian and international authorities: identifying and recovering stolen vehicles after they have crossed international borders.

The CBSA's involvement in Project Cadetta highlights the importance of intelligence-sharing and coordinated inspections of shipping containers.

Acting Regional Director General Trishann Pascal said CBSA officers play a critical role in preventing stolen vehicles from reaching international markets through targeted container examinations and referrals.

For prospective buyers in Ghana and Nigeria, the investigations also underline the importance of conducting proper checks before purchasing imported vehicles.

A luxury vehicle offered at an unusually attractive price should not automatically be considered a bargain. Buyers are advised to verify its documentation, ownership history and vehicle identification number (VIN) before completing a transaction.

A vehicle that appears to be legally registered in one country could still be linked to an unresolved theft investigation in another.

The fight against organised auto theft continues

Peel Regional Police report that auto thefts across the region have declined by more than 50 per cent since reaching a peak in 2023, with a further 10 per cent year-to-date reduction recorded in 2026.

While the figures indicate progress, Project Cadetta demonstrates that investigators continue to face organised criminal networks capable of operating across municipal, provincial and international boundaries.

The next challenge will be determining whether the latest arrests will lead investigators to additional suspects, overseas buyers, shipping intermediaries and other individuals allegedly involved in the criminal supply chain.

For the owners whose vehicles have been stolen, recovering them represents more than a financial victory. It is also about restoring a sense of security, protecting livelihoods and ensuring that criminal networks cannot turn ordinary Canadian neighbourhoods into starting points for international illegal trade.

The investigation remains ongoing. Anyone with information is urged to contact the Peel Regional Police Commercial Auto Crime Bureau on 905-453-2121, extension 3410.

One thing is clear: the fight against organised auto theft cannot end at Canada's borders. If stolen vehicles are being moved across oceans, the response must extend across borders as well.

Ghana News.title: Goldfields wins overall CSR company at Ghana Club 100
Ghana News.content:
Mining giant Goldfields Ghana Limited emerged as the overall winner in the Corporate Social Responsibility category at the 22nd Ghana Club 100 Awards in Accra.

The company was also ranked in the top three on the Club 100 rankings, following MTN Ghana and Newmont, respectively.

The Ghana Investment Promotion Authority held the 22nd edition of the Ghana Club 100 Awards to recognize top-performing companies contributing to economic growth and demonstrating exemplary business leadership.

Speaking to JoyBusiness, Senior Vice President of Goldfields, Elliot Williams, said the award is a testament to the CSR initiatives by the company and encourages them to do more for the host communities and the people of Ghana.

“We have been doing corporate social responsibility long before it was recognized in the rankings, and for us, we always want to give back to our communities and improve the living conditions of our people—not just for the awards, but for a positive impact in their lives. We have a positive outlook, and we can assure you that more will be coming in our CSR journey," he said.

After presenting awards to the top three companies, President John Dramani Mahama urged indigenous businesses to identify opportunities within the government's $10 billion New Economy Programme and position themselves to benefit.

Chief Executive of the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority, Simon Madjie, said the agency remains committed to supporting businesses by facilitating investment and addressing challenges in the business environment.

The theme for the 22nd Ghana Club 100 Awards is "Investing in Ghana's New Economy—Building a Productive Economy That Creates Value and Competes Globally."

Ghana News.title: Ghanaian among 21 arrested in Canada over alleged towing industry crime network
Ghana News.content:
A Ghanaian is among 21 people arrested and charged in Canada following a major police investigation into alleged organised crime, violence and criminal activities within the Greater Toronto Area (GTA) towing industry.

The investigation, code-named Project Swords, has resulted in 112 criminal charges and exposed what police describe as an alleged criminal network involved in murder conspiracies, firearms trafficking, vehicle theft, arson, fraud and other serious offences.

The Ghanaian, identified as Foster Nyarko, 34, of Vaughan, was among those named in a November 18, 2026, announcement by the Toronto Police Service.

The investigation was conducted in partnership with York Regional Police, Durham Regional Police Service and the Ontario Provincial Police. It culminated on November 12, when officers carried out coordinated enforcement operations, arrested several suspects and executed search warrants across the GTA.

Police allege that the organisation was led by Manoharan (Mano) Subramaniam, 43, of Whitby, who is accused of directing a conspiracy to murder two individuals connected to the towing industry.

Investigators say three individuals were arrested before the planned killings could be carried out and have been charged with conspiracy to commit murder.

The investigation points to an alleged escalation in competition for control of the towing business, an industry that provides essential roadside assistance but has increasingly become associated with violence and criminal activities, according to police.

How towing industry disputes escalated into violence

Police say the GTA experienced a significant increase in violence involving competing groups seeking control of the towing industry from early 2023.

The reported incidents included homicides, shootings, arson, intimidation and extortion.

One of the most alarming incidents was a mass shooting at a pub in Scarborough in March 2025, which left 12 people injured.

The scale of the violence is also reflected in Toronto's shooting statistics.

Police reported that 62 shooting and firearm-discharge incidents in 2024 were connected to tow-truck disputes, representing nearly 13 per cent of all such incidents in the city.

The figure declined to 18 incidents in 2025, representing seven per cent, and fell further to five incidents in 2026 up to the date of the announcement.

Police attribute the reduction partly to coordinated investigations targeting competing criminal organisations.

Project Swords follows Project Yankee, an earlier investigation targeting another faction known as "The Union".

Together, the two operations focused on what investigators described as the two largest competing groups associated with violence in the GTA towing industry.

The 21 accused named by police

The Toronto Police Service identified the following 21 individuals as having been arrested and charged in connection with Project Swords:

Dinesh Battula, 38, of Toronto. Fedrol Bryan, 41, of Toronto. Harithas Gnanalingam, 48, of Beaverton. Vathsuthan Gobalakirishnan, 41, of Whitchurch-Stouffville. Mohamad-Ali Hamam, 29, of Toronto. Dogan Kruezi, 29, of Toronto. Foster Nyarko, 34, of Vaughan. Shiv Patel, 31, of Toronto. Ratnakumar Pirakalathan, 46, of Toronto. Suman Pushparajah, 45, of Toronto. Nirjan Raguthas, 25, of Markham. Sivanesan Rajendram, 50, of Keswick. Sadeed Rehman, 28, of Oshawa. Kokul Senthilvel, 32, of Toronto. Piratwipan Sivakumaran, 34, of Pickering. Manoharan Subramaniam, 43, of Whitby. Thanugopithan Sugumarasungam, 30, of Toronto. Thanaraj Thangarajah, 39, of Toronto. Jeyanan Thangavadivel, 41, of Whitby. Kiranpal Toor, 26, of Caledon. Kranthi Vasireddy, 37, of Toronto.

The charges outlined in the police announcement include conspiracy to commit murder, participation in a criminal organisation, firearms trafficking, possession of stolen property for trafficking, altering vehicle identification numbers, conspiracy to commit arson, fraud and breach of trust.

Subramaniam faces two counts of conspiracy to commit murder, as well as charges of assault, uttering threats and conspiracy related to fraud.

Nyarko and Sadeed Rehman face several charges connected to their alleged participation in a criminal organisation involved in trafficking stolen vehicles, possessing property obtained through crime and altering vehicle identification numbers.

Mohamad-Ali Hamam also faces multiple charges relating to alleged participation in a criminal organisation, stolen-vehicle trafficking and attempts to alter vehicle identification numbers.

The police announcement further identifies firearms-trafficking allegations involving several accused, including Shiv Patel, Kokul Senthilvel, Thanugopithan Sugumarasungam and Thanaraj Thangarajah.

Piratwipan Sivakumaran, who is identified as a correctional employee, has been charged with breach of trust.

Investigation uncovers alleged criminal activities beyond towing

The investigation reportedly uncovered criminal activities extending beyond disputes over roadside assistance contracts.

Police said officers seized several firearms, including a converted fully automatic firearm, 84 rounds of ammunition and approximately 250 grams of cocaine.

According to investigators, six arrests were linked to an alleged organised vehicle-theft operation, two to an arson investigation, three to fraudulent physiotherapy clinics and one to an alleged breach of trust involving a correctional employee.

Investigators also allege that Subramaniam exercised control over businesses and their finances, even where some associated properties and businesses were registered in the names of other individuals.

The businesses identified included Williams Towing and Bob's Towing.

Following the enforcement operation, the Toronto Police Service immediately terminated its contractual relationship with Williams Towing, which had provided contracted services in four police divisions.

Temporary service providers have since been engaged while the police service makes arrangements for a longer-term procurement process.

Police outline next steps

Toronto Police Chief Myron Demkiw credited cooperation among the participating police services and government partners for the outcome of the investigation.

The Ontario government's Ministry of the Solicitor General provided funding for the operation, with additional support from Criminal Intelligence Service Ontario.

Although police have described Project Swords as a significant disruption of organised crime, the investigation has also drawn attention to concerns about how criminal networks allegedly penetrate legitimate businesses and exploit essential services.

For residents and legitimate towing operators, the concern extends beyond competition for business contracts to whether the industry can operate without threats, intimidation and violence.

The 21 accused are expected to face criminal proceedings, but the allegations against them have yet to be tested in court. They are all presumed innocent until proven guilty.

Police are appealing to anyone with information about the investigation to contact the Toronto Police Service on 416-808-2510.

As the GTA continues to grapple with the consequences of years of alleged violence within its towing industry, Project Swords marks another significant phase in efforts to establish the full extent of the criminal networks and identify the individuals and businesses allegedly connected to their activities.

Ghana News.title: Canada Police extend authority to publish image of 17-year-old suspect in murder of Ghanaian teen
Ghana News.content:
The suspect, Cameron Marlor.

Toronto Police have secured an extension of judicial authorisation to publicly identify a 17-year-old suspect wanted in connection with the murder of 18-year-old Ghanaian, Malik Abass, as a Canada-wide manhunt continues for two suspects.

In an update issued on Thursday, November 19, 2026, police confirmed that they had obtained an extension of the authorisation under Section 110 of Canada's Youth Criminal Justice Act, allowing them to release the identity and photographs of 17-year-old Cameron Marlor.

The authorisation, which was due to expire, will now remain in force until Tuesday, November 24, 2026, at 12 noon.

Police have also confirmed that a Canada-wide warrant has been issued for Marlor, who is from Toronto, on four charges:

Second-degree murder. Attempted murder. Knowingly possessing a firearm without a licence. Possessing a loaded regulated firearm.

A second suspect, 19-year-old Armani Callender, also from Toronto, is wanted under a Canada-wide warrant on the same four charges.

The development expands police efforts to identify and locate the suspects as investigators continue their search and work to advance the homicide investigation.

Read Also: 18-year-old Ghanaian shot in Canada identified as victim of Toronto’s 33rd homicide in 2026

Malik Abass, an 18-year-old from Mississauga, was killed on November 7, 2026, in the area of Rathburn Road and The East Mall in Toronto.

Toronto Police have released photographs of the two suspects and are appealing to members of the public who may have information about their whereabouts to assist with the investigation.

Anyone with information is urged to contact the Toronto Police Homicide and Missing Persons Unit on 416-808-7400.

The killing of the young Ghanaian has drawn attention to the search for answers surrounding his death, with his family and the wider community awaiting developments as police intensify efforts to locate the two suspects.

The manhunt remains ongoing.

Ghana News.title: Savannah NDC Secretary calls for unity after Regional executive election
Ghana News.content:
Lawyer Kudus Gbeadese, Savannah Regional Secretary of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), has urged party members in the region to put the outcome of the recent regional executive elections behind them and unite for the work ahead.

The party elected its regional executives on Sunday, November 15, 2026. In a statement following the polls, Mr Gbeadese acknowledged that the election day “came with its attendant issues” but stressed that the process was over and members must now focus on the future.

“That day came, and it is gone, and will never come on any calendar. After everything, God spoke, and some won, and others didn’t win,” he stated.

He appealed to the regional council of elders, regional, constituency and branch executives, as well as party members across the region and other stakeholders, to move beyond whatever disagreements may have arisen during the elections.

“Please and please, whatever happened on that day is past. We have opened a new chapter, and whatever we will write in this chapter is the most important thing,” he said.

Mr Gbeadese acknowledged that individuals would naturally have different interests and positions during the decision-making process. However, he said members must rally behind a common agenda once decisions had been taken to enable the party to move forward.

“We cannot make progress if we rehash the past and feed the same into decisions meant for the future,” he cautioned.

The Regional Secretary said he would need the support of all members, “excluding none,” to effectively administer the region, adding that his focus was now firmly on the task ahead.

He pledged to discharge his responsibilities with humility, dedication and fairness, while ensuring the transparency necessary for a successful administration.

Ghana News.title: 24-hour economy gradually creating jobs, but more work needed – Austin Gamey
Ghana News.content:
Labour expert Austin Gamey says Ghana's 24-hour economy initiative is gradually creating employment opportunities, although its impact may not yet be as significant as many Ghanaians expect.

His comments come amid growing debate over the government's claims that the 24-hour economy initiative is generating employment opportunities for young Ghanaians, with questions being raised about the number and nature of jobs created so far.



e says the initiative should be viewed as a long-term programme rather than an event, arguing that its implementation will take time to translate into substantial job creation.

Speaking in an interview on JoyNews' The Pulse on Thursday, November 19, Mr Gamey said some private and public organisations operating within the Tema Free Zones enclave and the harbour area are already running round-the-clock operations.

According to him, the expansion of 24-hour activities at the Tema Port, particularly efforts to facilitate the clearance of goods throughout the day, is creating employment opportunities.

"Clearly, what it is is that some level of employment is being done within the space of the 24-hour economy. It may not be as plenty as people would wish, but they are working," he said.

Mr Gamey, who is also a consultant to some companies seeking to establish operations in Ghana, disclosed that major investments in renewable energy and agriculture are being pursued and could create significant employment opportunities when fully operational.

He cited plans for a 500-megawatt solar energy project in the northern part of the country, which he described as potentially the largest of its kind in Africa.

He also disclosed plans for a large-scale biogas plantation and a proposed palm plantation project in the Oti Region, where investors are seeking to secure about 40,000 hectares of land.

Mr Gamey said these projects, if implemented as planned, could generate substantial employment for Ghanaians.

He added that one of the companies involved was expected to conduct recruitment interviews on Friday, November 20, although he did not provide further details about the recruitment exercise.

The labour expert, however, cautioned the government against making excessive claims about the 24-hour economy before the programme is fully operational.

He said public expectations must be managed while the various projects and investments are being developed.

Mr Gamey also called for a broader understanding of employment in Ghana, arguing that public discussions often focus too narrowly on permanent jobs.

He explained that under International Labour Organisation (ILO) definitions, a person who works for at least one hour during the reference period is classified as employed.

He said employment also includes casual, temporary and contract work, which are common in sectors such as tourism, construction and other industries.

"Then you have casuals, and these all are found in our labour law. There are casual jobs. That is in America, that is in Britain, that is everywhere. It's in Ghana too," he said.

He added that temporary and contract workers should also be recognised as employed, even where their engagements are not permanent.

Mr Gamey maintained that understanding the different forms of employment is important in assessing the impact of the 24-hour economy and the country's broader labour market.

Ghana News.title: Shatta Wale denies neglecting son, says court ruling allowed him access in 2025
Ghana News.content:
Shatta Wale and son, Majesty

Dancehall artiste Shatta Wale has responded to allegations that he neglected his son, Majesty, insisting that a court ruling in 2025 granted him access to the child whenever he wanted.

In a Facebook post on Thursday, November 19, the musician, born Charles Nii Armah Mensah Jnr, acknowledged that he had not taken care of Majesty since 2023 but explained that the photographs being discussed were taken in 2025, after the court had ruled on his access to the child.

"Oh yes, I never took care of my son since 2023 but this was 2025 after the court said I could see my son anytime I want," he wrote.

He also criticised some people who had previously associated themselves with him, accusing them of making misleading claims about their closeness to him to gain public attention.

"One thing I learnt about people that came around me was to just lie to the public because they know everyone will say they were close to me and blah blah," he stated.

Shatta Wale thanked those who, he said, knew him well enough not to believe what he described as false accounts about his personal life.

Addressing his critics, he maintained that he would continue to stand by what he considered the truth, regardless of public opinion.

"Choose the lies cuz Shatta will always stand by the truth !!!! Long Live the King and his son Majesty (Bond)," he added.

Background to Shatta Wale and Michy's disagreement

The latest comments follow a public disagreement between Shatta Wale and his former partner, Diamond Michelle Gbagonah, popularly known as Shatta Michy, over their co-parenting arrangements and the welfare of their son.

The dispute intensified after Shatta Wale expressed concern about videos of Majesty selling orange juice under the sun at Aburi.

Speaking on Hitz FM's Afternoon Ride with Andy Dosty on November 17, the musician questioned why his son was involved in the activity when he had the resources, offices and employees to provide him with other opportunities.

He said he had bought several gadgets to help Majesty develop an interest in technology and appealed to Michy to put their past differences aside and work with him towards securing their son's future.

Michy, however, rejected suggestions that she had prevented the musician from seeing their son.

In response, on November 18, she alleged that Majesty had repeatedly attempted to contact his father without receiving responses, claiming she had witnessed the child making nine or 10 unanswered calls.

She also maintained that court arrangements allowed Shatta Wale to spend weekends with Majesty, from Friday to Sunday, and questioned why he had not consistently exercised that opportunity.

Michy further defended the child's involvement in the juice business, insisting it was his own initiative. She disclosed that Majesty had designed the product's logo and that the business had generated GH¢115,000. She maintained that he was not being forced to sell the drinks. .

While Shatta Wale maintains that the court granted him access to Majesty in 2025, Michy insists she has never prevented him from seeing their son, leaving both parents with differing accounts of their co-parenting relationship.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: US appeals court lets Trump end TPS deportation protections for Venezuelans
World.content:
The appeals court’s ruling prevents a lower-court decision from taking effect, which would block Trump from ending the TPS programme.

A United States appeals court has allowed the administration of President Donald Trump to move forward for now with the removal of deportation protections for Venezuelans.

The ruling on Wednesday cancels out a previous order by a lower-court judge that required the government to restore the Temporary Protected Status (TPS) of Venezuelans, which shields recipients against deportation.

The effort to end the TPS protections has proceeded despite humanitarian concerns.

Since taking office for a second term, Trump has sought to carry out what he calls the largest deportation effort in US history. Part of that agenda has been to roll back programmes like TPS.

But in September 2025, US District Judge Edward Chen blocked the expiration of TPS protections for Venezuelans, arguing that deporting those individuals would put them in harm’s way.

He also ruled that the Trump administration had overstepped its authority by seeking to shorten TPS extensions granted under the preceding president, Joe Biden. Such decisions, Chen added, needed to be taken with “careful study and analysis”.

Some 600,000 Venezuelans in the US were protected under TPS programmes.

The Supreme Court paused Chen’s ruling in October 2025. But that pause expired this month, and Chen’s order was set to take effect on Friday.

On Wednesday, the Trump administration filed an emergency request to the Supreme Court to extend the pause before Thursday’s appeals court ruling.

The appeals court’s decision does not nix the ongoing legal challenges to Trump’s efforts to revoke TPS extensions. But it allows the administration to suspend deportation protections while the challenges make their way through court.

The Trump administration has sought to strip large numbers of immigrants of their legal protections in a bid to render them deportable. Other programmes, like humanitarian parole, have also come under the administration’s scrutiny.



TPS allows foreign nationals already in the US to remain while conditions in their home countries are too dangerous or unstable to return to.

Humanitarian parole, meanwhile, allows people outside the US to come in on a temporary basis, often to escape similarly perilous conditions.

The Trump administration has argued that TPS designations are meant to be temporary — and that previous presidencies extended such protections without cause.

It has also maintained that conditions have improved in places like Venezuela, where a US military action on January 3 resulted in the abduction of President Nicolas Maduro.

Human rights advocates, however, have noted that Maduro’s government remains largely intact. That leadership has been accused of abuses ranging from arbitrary imprisonment to the torture of political dissidents.

The US Department of State currently warns against travel to Venezuela, citing issues such as crime, kidnapping and poor health infrastructure.
