World.title: Why are Bukele’s Salvadoran troops in Haiti and what have they achieved?
World.content:
With crowds rallying behind El Salvador’s deployment in Haiti, analysts question whether civilians are any safer.

Share Why are Bukele’s Salvadoran troops in Haiti and what have they achieved? on social media

The streets of Haiti’s capital, Port-au-Prince, rang out on Tuesday and Wednesday with chants from local residents in support of a president who was not their own: El Salvador’s Nayib Bukele. In a country where the scars of foreign intervention run deep, some Haitians are placing their hopes on another foreign force, this time from El Salvador, to help take their neighbourhoods back from armed gangs.

Thousands turned out to cheer on the roughly 2,500 soldiers Bukele has sent since October. What began as a narrow mission to rescue four missing Salvadoran aviation technicians has grown into a much broader military operation.

For some of those who marched, the intervention is exactly what the country needs after years of kidnappings, killings, and displacement, with little sign of relief.

But even with the Haitian government’s backing and a warm reception from the public, questions are growing about what the troops are doing on the ground and what kind of mark Bukele will ultimately leave on Haiti.

Why are Salvadoran troops in Haiti?

The immediate trigger came on October 18, when four Salvadoran aviation technicians working with the United Nations-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF) went missing after armed men attacked their vehicle near Port-au-Prince.

The force was created to help Haitian authorities deal with a security crisis that has grown more severe since the 2021 assassination of President Jovenel Moise. According to Reuters, gangs now control more than 80 percent of the capital region, with Haitian and international forces struggling to reclaim that territory.



Shortly after the technicians went missing, Bukele announced a new military operation in Haiti, sending 100 special forces soldiers to rescue them. Since then, he’s sent about 2,500 in total.

Most of them are operating outside the UN-backed force and outside the UN support office’s monitoring mechanisms, according to UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric.

And the deployment itself has turned from a narrow rescue operation to a broader offensive against Haiti’s gangs, with Salvadoran soldiers joining Haitian security forces, the GSF, and private contractors, including Blackwater founder Erik Prince’s Vectus Global.

Bukele, who gained international notoriety for a crackdown on gangs in El Salvador that led to a sharp decline in crime but has drawn widespread condemnation over human rights abuses, has been aggressively promoting the deployment on social media.

He has posted dramatic videos of helicopter attacks on gang leaders’ properties and, more recently, footage of rallies cheering on his troops.

“I never expected anything like this,” he wrote in a Tuesday post accompanying a video of a rally. “I hear you loud and clear. I love you, too.”

Neither the Haitian government nor the Salvadoran government replied to Al Jazeera’s requests for comment about the troops in Haiti.

Why are some Haitians cheering on the Salvadoran troops?

The troops have landed amid a worsening humanitarian crisis in Haiti, with nearly 1.5 million people displaced from their homes, and violence making it difficult to access food and basic services. More than 22,000 people have been killed in gang-related violence, including security operations, since 2022, according to Reuters.

At rallies in Port-au-Prince and other parts of Haiti, demonstrators voiced support for the deployment. Some who spoke to The Associated Press news agency described losing loved ones to gang violence and being forced to leave their homes.

“The support we see from many Haitians comes from sheer desperation after years of failure and widespread terror,” Louimann Maceus, president of the human rights organisation Ensemble des Citoyens Competents a la Recherche de l’Egalite des Droits de l’Homme en Haiti (ECCREDHH), told Al Jazeera. “People are exhausted.”

“There is a genuine hope, especially among the hundreds of thousands of internally displaced people we work with who just want to return safely home,” said Maceus, who lives in Port-au-Prince.



That hope, he said, follows years of frustration with UN-backed forces, which he said had done little to improve security.

The Salvadoran deployment already outnumbers the GSF, according to numbers from the GSF’s special representative Jack Christofides, on October 18, when it had just surpassed 2,000 personnel.

International Crisis Group analyst Diego Da Rin also links some of the enthusiasm to what he describes as a really effective communication campaign by Bukele, whose videos of strikes on gang leaders’ homes are all over Haitian social media.

“These are symbolic wins that everybody was waiting for,” he said, adding that AI-generated videos were also circulating of gang leaders being arrested.

But support for the deployment is not universal. Da Rin pointed to the residents of gang-controlled areas.

“Many of these people, who clearly see the risks in these iron-fist operations, are extremely scared of being attacked and being collateral damage of any of these operations,” said Da Rin.

What have Salvadoran troops actually achieved?

Security force clashes and drone strikes targeting gangs increased by 46 percent in the 21 days after the start of the deployment, compared to the 21 days before it, according to the conflict monitoring group the Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project (ACLED).

ACLED estimated more than 100 people were killed in the same period, including at least 26 civilians.

Haiti’s Justice Minister Patrick Pelissier, however, said on Monday that the government had received no reports of civilian casualties in the latest operations, which it described as professional, according to Reuters.

Bukele has used social media to highlight what he sees as the offensive’s successes.

After Salvadoran troops joined Haitian police and a government task force in a November 8 attack on a house belonging to Wilson Joseph, leader of the powerful 400 Mawozo gang, Bukele posted video of helicopters repeatedly firing at the building, as people ran away from the area.

Joseph reportedly was not there and survived the attack.

A few days later, Haitian national police and Bukele announced that they’d retaken control of the national football stadium. Bukele shared video of robot dogs armed with rifles moving through the corridors of the stadium alongside troops, although it’s unclear how exactly they were used in the operation.

Da Rin said it was worth noting that police initially credited their officers and the task force with retaking the stadium before handing control over to Salvadoran troops, who set up a base there.

The stadium is a useful spot to launch operations against nearby gang strongholds, he added, but it represented a relatively small gain from positions Haitian forces had already secured.



On Wednesday, Bukele posted another video showing a helicopter attack on the home of Jeff Larose, leader of the Taliban gang, which controls the area of Canaan in northern Port-au-Prince.

It was not clear whether the attack had killed Larose or whether Haiti’s police or army had participated. The GSF was not involved, according to The Associated Press.

For displaced people looking to return home, the gains have yet to make a tangible difference, said Da Rin.

After the attack on Joseph’s house, none of the security forces set up a permanent presence in the area, he said.

“Armed groups were able to return and are now intimidating residents, searching their phones, threatening people suspected of sharing information with the security forces,” Da Rin told Al Jazeera.

He warned that forces appeared to be “in a race” to show results without a unified strategy to sustain them.

Salvadoran officials have said they plan to leave once the missing technicians are found. Joseph, leader of the 400 Mawozo gang, told the Associated Press earlier this month that they were dead, but their fate remains officially unknown.

“The priority should be to plan the most difficult part, how the forces will work together to establish lasting control,” said Da Rin.

Why are some experts concerned about the deployment?

The terms of the Salvadoran deployment haven’t been made public.

Amnesty International has called on both governments to explain who oversees the troops, what rules govern their use of force, and how civilians can safely report abuses.

On Monday, Salvadoran Vice President Felix Ulloa said the agreement would be kept under wraps until diplomatic conditions allowed its release and accused critics of having a “hidden agenda”.

Sam Vigersky, a fellow with the Council on Foreign Relations who studies emergency relief in response to armed conflict, said the lack of monitoring or publicly shared rules of engagement for Salvadoran troops operating outside the GSF means “we do not know what collateral damage might come of these offensives”.

For Vigersky, the lesson from past interventions, including a UN peacekeeping mission whose personnel brought cholera to Haiti and were implicated in widespread sexual abuse, is that “oversight matters”.

“Absent that,” he said, “the deep scars that Haiti has already from these past UN or other operations are only likely to grow.”

World.title: Will the Shenzhen summit safeguard world peace?
World.content:
Xi, Putin and Trump issue ‘Peace Declaration’ after historic summit.

A three-way meeting between the leaders of China, Russia and the United States has yielded a number of commitments.

Xi Jinping hosted Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump in the city of Shenzhen, China on Thursday.

In a joint statement called a “Peace Declaration”, the three countries’ presidents pledged to safeguard international security and increase the production of refined petroleum products.

They also stressed that a nuclear war should never be fought because it cannot be won.

And they agreed to keep channels of dialogue open to resolve conflicts such as the war in Ukraine.

But how will Xi, Putin and Trump turn these commitments into actions?

Presenter: James Bays

Guests:

Andy Mok – Senior research fellow at the Center for China and Globalization

Aaron Glasserman – Distinguished fellow at the Weatherhead East Asian Institute at Columbia University

Alexander Bratersky – Independent journalist and specialist in Russian foreign policy and Russia-US relations

World.title: How vaccine fears fuelled a major measles comeback in the US
World.content:
How vaccine fears fuelled a major measles comeback in the US

NewsFeed How vaccine fears fuelled a major measles comeback in the US

Measles is making a comeback in the US as vaccination rates fall. Misinformation, autism claims and growing vaccine skepticism have all played a part in the country’s worst outbreak in decades. Al Jazeera’s Farah Samir looks at what’s going on.

World.title: Anthropic becomes most valuable AI firm as shares soar in stock market debut
World.content:
While the basics of the technology have been around for decades, the more recent advent of more powerful computers and related components have allowed the processing of more data than ever.

The result has been AI chatbots that simulate human speech and operate more quickly tasks like software coding, digital image generation, and searching the internet.

It represents a new way of using computers that has led to the rapid rise of Anthropic, which started just five years ago and is best known as the maker of the popular AI chatbot Claude.

As the first purely AI company to go public, Anthropic will almost certainly see significant swings in price on the stock market going forward, according to Ben Barringer, who leads technology research at Quilter Cheviot.

The "initial exuberance" will wear off, Barringer said, pointing to what happened with SpaceX earlier this year.

That company, led by Elon Musk, saw shares jump by about 10% on the first day of trading, taking the company to a record-breaking valuation of $2.2 trillion.

Within a month shares had fallen below their debut price, and have mostly fallen further since.

Most tech companies see their shares fall after hitting the stock market, often after reporting quarterly results for the first time.

But many such companies, including Meta, Amazon and Google, have gone on to become the largest and most profitable corporations in the world.

With Anthropic, investors are not only looking at a notable tech company with a major valuation, and a potentially big future in business, but a company that is the first of its kind on the stock market.

"There's no obvious peer to compare it to," Neil Wilson, an investor strategist at Saxo UK, said.

So, as individual investors and even researchers and investors at large funds ask themselves if Anthropic is really worth $1.5 trillion, or even more, there will be few answers available.

"We'll have a stab at it," Wilson said. "I don't think anyone really knows."

A few things will likely impact the company's success on the stock market in the near-term.

One of those things is the prospect of new laws governing the use of AI tools. In the US, where Anthropic is based, Democrats will be in many more positions of power come 2027, and several politicians have already said they will be looking to ensure AI tools are safe and have some guardrails attached.

On Thursday, the same day Anthropic went public, a bipartisan group of lawmakers formed the House AI Safety and Innovation Caucus, which will work specifically on AI regulation and safety considerations.

A significant driver of this kind of scrutiny is Anthropic itself. Company executives, including co-founder and CEO Dario Amodei, have been outspoken in their purported fears that future AI tools will become so capable they will outsmart humans, to the point where extinction is possible.

Anthropic has always put itself forward in public as an AI company that takes the safety of its technology very seriously.

Daniela Amodei, Anthropic's president and sister of Dario Amodei, boasted on Thursday that the company "had an AI safety team before we launched our first product".

"AI carries real risks," she added.

Despite the company's claims that the technology it is building at a rapid pace could be dangerous, Anthropic has made one of the quickest trips from start-up to IPO in history.

World.title: Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya minority, top UN court rules
World.content:
Myanmar has been found guilty of committing genocide against its Rohingya minority by the International Court of Justice (ICJ).

The verdict marks the first time a state has ever been found to have committed genocide by an international court.

Yuji Iwasawa, president of the UN's top court, said Myanmar had the "intention to destroy" a substantial part of the Rohingya population and engaged in "extensive destruction of evidence" to hide its crimes.

A military crackdown in 2017 killed thousands of Rohingya and forced more than 700,000 to flee Buddhist-majority Myanmar, formerly known as Burma. Myanmar denied the claims against it, saying its forces had responded to attacks by armed groups.

World.title: Trump, Putin and Xi release 'peace declaration' after historic meeting
World.content:
US President Donald Trump and his Russian and Chinese counterparts Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping have issued a "joint declaration of peace" following historic trilateral talks.

The three leaders met for 90 minutes in China's south-eastern city of Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.

While the presidents have previously had one-on-one meetings, these are their first trilateral talks.

In the declaration, they said "nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought" and that the countries planned to increase the production and supply of petroleum. They also said they were "committed to reform the UN" to respond more effectively to global challenges.

Thursday's statement also flagged the issue of immunity enjoyed by state officials and said "they agreed that the International Criminal Court and other similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction".

Trump praised the trilateral meeting calling it "a great and highly consequential trip", in a social media post while flying back to Washington on Air Force One.

In the same post, the president announced he would host a news conference to talk about the trip on Friday at the White House.

While in China, Trump met Putin ahead of the trilateral, in their first meeting since August 2025, where the US president greeted his Russian counterpart as his "friend".

He also spoke with Xi in a separate conversation, describing the pair's relationship as "very special".

Beyond the warmth and shared niceties, however, the three men had different goals and motivations for the sit-down.

World.title: Europe ready for talks with Russia on ending war in Ukraine, leaders say
World.content:
European leaders have said they are ready for negotiations with Russia on ending the war in Ukraine, in a strong show of support for Kyiv.

"Europe has a clear and consistent and united negotiating position," UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham said, while German Chancellor Friedrich Merz stressed that Moscow's "maximalist demands are not realistic".

They were speaking at Berlin's summit of Ukraine's allies known as the Coalition of the Willing.

Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner, one of the two US envoys who were in Berlin, said the US president wanted to make a deal with Moscow "with Europe by his side". Russia's Vladimir Putin has so far rejected any European role in the US-led peace talks.

Trump had earlier held historic trilateral talks in Shenzhen, south-eastern China, with Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping and later dialled into the Berlin summit from Air Force One.

In a lengthy press conference following his talks with Trump and Xi, Putin addressed the question of multilateral peace talks, saying the Americans were "insistently" asking Russia to allow the Europeans to take part.

Putin claimed Russia was not against the idea but said Moscow wanted to clarify "what Europe will bring to these talks".

"That is why, through diplomatic channels, we have invited the Europeans to come to Moscow in order to determine their positions. And after that, we will decide in what format we will continue the dialogue with Ukraine."

But Putin also said that "every day" Russia heard that European leaders were talking about war coming in 2030. "But we are not planning to attack anyone... Is that normal? I do not think so," he said. Still, Putin added, Russia understood that "discussing issues linked to security in Europe is pointless without the Europeans".

Jared Kushner told reporters that the US president had come away from Shenzhen believing that "peace is achievable".

Striking an upbeat note, Kushner said that the Russians were willing to trust the instinct of the US envoys "on our behalf" that the Europeans should be at the table and that Moscow was now "comfortable" with Ukraine having security guarantees based on the idea enshrined in Nato's Article Five that requires allies to come to a country's defence if it comes under attack.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, who also was at the summit in Germany's capital, has long sought a guarantee equivalent to Nato's collective defence clause, and there has been little indication that Putin would accept that kind of condition.

Russia rejects outright the idea of Ukrainian membership of Nato, but reports say US negotiators have mulled the idea of giving Kyiv Article Five-style guarantees without being part of the Western defensive alliance if it agrees to painful territorial concessions.

Zelensky and the three European leaders â Merz, Burnham and French President Emmanuel Macron â were not as upbeat as Kushner, and the Ukrainian president made clear that the Russian president had spurned every proposal so far: "Putin has always said no."

The German chancellor was equally sceptical, although he said with US involvement the chance of peace was increasing. Europe was willing to enter "serious discussions on European security" with Russia, he explained, "as long as it's matched with a serious discussion and only first a peace agreement with Ukraine".

"These talks have to begin, and we will accept if conditions are acceptable for Europe and Ukraine," said Merz.

He also said any attempts to divide Europe into spheres of influence run by major powers was unacceptable, amid concerns on the continent that this issue may have been on the agenda at the trilateral talks in Shenzhen.

World.title: Dozens missing after boat carrying migrants sinks off Senegal's coast
World.content:
Senegalese authorities are continuing search operations after a boat said to be carrying between 50 and 100 migrants capsized in the Atlantic Ocean.

Four bodies have reportedly been recovered so far. Dozens of people are still missing.

Personal belongings were found on the badly damaged boat, which washed ashore near the village of Yenne, south of Dakar. Search operations continued throughout Wednesday and were due to resume on Thursday.

This comes less than two weeks after a shipwreck off the coast of the north-western town of Thieppe killed at least 39 people, in one of Senegal's deadliest migration disasters.

Oumar Sow, a representative of the village chief, said the latest tragedy happened around 02:00 local time (02:00 GMT).

"Cries could be heard coming from the pirogue that were audible even from the beach," the AFP news agency quoted him as saying.

A survivor questioned by the police said there were about 100 people on the boat, including five women, AFP reported.

However, a local official told Reuters news agency it was carrying 50 people, adding that the boat hit a rock as migrants were transferring from small fishing boats to a larger vessel.

Police recovered identity documents, several mobile phones and personal belongings from the wreckage, including a school enrolment document.

At a cabinet meeting on Wednesday, President Diomaye Faye expressed concern about a renewed increase in irregular departure by migrants hoping to reach Europe.

He instructed the interior ministry to prepare a report examining the factors driving the dangerous journeys and proposing measures to tackle the problem.

Following last month's tragedy, Faye had urged Senegalese people not to risk their lives attempting the dangerous sea crossings.

Many thousands of people from West Africa have died or gone missing trying to flee conflict, authoritarian rule or poverty in recent years.

The UN's migration agency IOM said last month that it had recorded at least 454 deaths and disappearances off the West African coast this year alone.

It warned the figures were likely to be an underestimate, as many boats disappear without leaving survivors or a trace.

The Senegalese navy said it had rescued more than 1,400 people on Monday and Tuesday this week.

World.title: Putin vows 'far more painful' response to Ukraine's strikes on Crimean Bridge
World.content:
Moscow's retaliation for attacks on the Crimean Bridge will be "far more painful" than Kyiv's strikes, Vladimir Putin has vowed.

In the early hours of Thursday, the double-arched, 12-mile bridge connecting Russia to Ukraine's occupied peninsula of Crimea was hit for a third time this week.

A combined missile-and-drone strike on Tuesday destroyed the central road section of the bridge, collapsing part of it into the water and rendering it unusable for road traffic.

But at a press conference after historic talks with his Chinese and US counterparts in Shenzhen, Russian president Putin said Moscow's response would be even more significant.

Putin claimed the bridge was used exclusively for civilian purposes and not to transport military equipment, as Kyiv has alleged, or petroleum products.

Since illegally annexing the Crimean Peninsula in 2014, Moscow has used it as a military base, with airbases, troop concentrations, training grounds and artillery stockpiles.

From there it has also carried out strikes on the rest of the country and resupplied its troops in southern Ukraine.

Commenting on the strikes on the bridge, Kyiv's defence ministry said that for Ukraine, they amounted to to "time gained and lives saved. The less that reaches the occupiers, the less hits our warriors."

The collapse of the Crimean Bridge's arch was the worst damage to be inflicted onto the structure in several years.

The bridge had long been in Ukraine's sights because it represents Moscow's pretensions over sovereign Ukrainian land, and because of its logistical importance in supplying Russian troops in the occupied Ukrainian southern regions.

It was built and unveiled to great fanfare in 2018, four years after Russia illegally annexed Ukraine's Crimea.

Thursday's strike was carried out with Neptune cruise missiles, Ukraine said. Russia's transport ministry said nobody had been hurt in the attack, and that specialists were assessing damage to the bridge. Train services on the bridge were suspended but resumed in the afternoon.

Car traffic, however, will be prohibited for the foreseeable future as a section about 200m (660ft) long of the tarmac was dragged below into the sea when missiles hit the arch on Tuesday.

President Volodymyr Zelensky called the initial strikes on the Crimean Bridge an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making.

The seven-stage operation first required the destruction of air defence systems, radars, electronic warfare assets which protected the bridge. Missiles and drones then dealt the structure the final blow.

World.title: Van Gogh painting sells for record $190.4m after row over its Nazi history
World.content:
It was not immediately clear who purchased the painting. The BBC has contacted Sotheby's for comment.

The oil painting, which was estimated to carry a value of $180m (Â£136m) prior to the sale, was put up for auction as part of a set called the Blaquier-Arrieta Collection.

Sotheby's announced in the hours before the auction that it had resolved a dispute between the Blaquier-Arrieta family and the heirs of the Fischer family - the prior German owners of the work - regarding the sale.

Representatives acting for heirs of the Fischer family had claimed the painting may have been sold under duress during the rise of the Nazis.

A lawyer for the family's heirs reportedly wrote to Sotheby's on their behalf, telling the auction house that the painting was sold in Amsterdam before World War Two because of financial losses the Fischer family's publishing company suffered under the Nazis. The BBC has contacted the lawyer for comment.

"In recognition of the painting's complex Nazi-era history and the suffering endured by the Fischer family during the Holocaust, the two families have reached a mutually satisfactory resolution and the work will be sold pursuant to their agreement," Sotheby's said on Wednesday.

Sotheby's website details the provenance of the oil painting and how it has researched the artwork changing hands since 1890.

It says Samuel Fischer - a famous German publisher - acquired it in 1909 before it was passed down in his family after his death in 1934.

The painting was deposited with Paul Cassirer in Amsterdam in 1932 or 1933 before it went to Henriette and Marcel Kapferer in Paris in 1936, Sotheby's said.

Four other owners then had the painting.

The Blaquier family acquired it in 1975 and owned it for more than half a century before the latest sale, the auction house said.

World.title: Fiona the hippo dies after swallowing a hat at Cincinnati Zoo
World.content:
"We are in shock at the moment," Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike said in a statement. "We did not expect this outcome. She fought until she couldn't anymore."

Michelle Curley, a spokesperson for the zoo, had said that the hat got into Fiona's enclosure by accident, after a visitor tossed it in the air and it caught on a ceiling fan that flung it through a small opening.

"We probably couldn't make [it] happen again if we tried," Curley said.

While she seemed fine at first, her appetite started to decrease a few days later, and the zoo staff tried to encourage Fiona to eat to help push the hat through her digestive system.

An ultrasound before her death showed the hat passing through Fiona's small intestine. A zookeeper said surgery was not an option for full-grown hippos and "our best chance for success with Fiona would be if she could pass this on her own".

"Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn't fight anymore," Jenike said.

Fiona was born premature at the Cincinnati Zoo in 2017 and at first struggled to survive. At birth, she weighed 13 kg (29 lbs), which the zoo said was about half the previous lowest recorded birth weight for her species.

Her story inspired an ice cream flavour as well as a character in Cincinnati's ballet.

World.title: AMR: Pharmacist urges Nigeria to implement policies to curb drug resistance
World.content:
Nigeria needs to translate its antimicrobial resistance (AMR) policies into action to curb the growing threat of drug-resistant infections, a pharmacist has said.

Folashade Lawal, managing director and chief executive officer of Victory Drugs, said the country had developed policies and guidelines to address AMR but faced challenges implementing them across healthcare facilities and communities.

“The challenge now lies not in planning but in implementation,” Ms Lawal said on Thursday while delivering the ninth Ladipo Mobolaji Abisogun-Afodu Annual Lecture in Pharmacy at the College of Medicine, University of Lagos.

The lecture, titled Addressing Antimicrobial Stewardship in Nigeria: Current Perspectives and Future Imperatives, was held during the 2026 World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week, observed from 18 to 24 November.

Policies, implementation gaps

Nigeria’s first National Action Plan on Antimicrobial Resistance covered 2017 to 2022. The plan sought to reduce, prevent and slow the emergence of resistant organisms through awareness, surveillance, infection prevention and control, responsible antimicrobial use, and research.

An assessment of its implementation found that only 44 per cent of the plan’s activities had been completed, highlighting gaps in coordination, funding and implementation across sectors.

Nigeria subsequently launched its second One Health National Action Plan on AMR, covering 2024 to 2028, with six strategic objectives, including stronger governance, surveillance, public awareness, infection prevention and control, responsible antimicrobial use, and research and capacity development.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Ms Lawal said antimicrobial stewardship activities are yet to become routine in many healthcare institutions, despite the country’s policy commitments.

She called for stronger enforcement of regulations governing antimicrobial sales, sustainable funding for stewardship programmes at federal, state and institutional levels, improved access to diagnostic services and laboratory infrastructure, and the establishment of stewardship programmes across healthcare facilities.

She also urged the government to strengthen antimicrobial consumption monitoring, invest in workforce development and research, and expand public awareness of responsible antimicrobial use.

In his welcome remarks, the Dean of the Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Lagos, Sunday Adesegun, said antimicrobial resistance threatened the effective treatment of infectious diseases and could reverse gains made in modern medicine.

He said Nigeria continued to grapple with self-medication, indiscriminate access to antibiotics, inadequate infection prevention and control, and gaps in antimicrobial resistance surveillance.

“Antimicrobial stewardship is not merely a professional responsibility; it is a collective obligation to safeguard public health,” Mr Adesegun said, urging stakeholders to move beyond awareness to concrete action.

Growing threat

Ms Lawal described antimicrobial resistance as a “silent pandemic” that steadily undermines the effectiveness of medicines used to treat infections.

She said bacterial antimicrobial resistance was associated with approximately 4.7 million deaths globally in 2021, including 1.14 million deaths directly attributable to resistant infections.

In Nigeria, she cited estimates that antimicrobial resistance was directly responsible for 50,500 deaths and associated with about 227,000 deaths in 2021.

She warned that resistance threatens not only the treatment of common infections but also modern medical procedures, including surgery, cancer treatment, organ transplantation, neonatal care and intensive care, which depend on effective antimicrobials.

Ms Lawal identified self-medication, inappropriate prescribing and dispensing, unrestricted access to antibiotics, weak regulatory enforcement, inadequate infection prevention and control, and limited diagnostic capacity as major drivers of antimicrobial resistance.

She said inadequate laboratory services often leave healthcare professionals relying on empirical treatment without diagnostic confirmation.

Pharmacists’ role

Ms Lawal urged community pharmacists to refuse inappropriate antibiotic supply without valid prescriptions, source medicines from regulated suppliers, counsel patients on proper use and refer patients for medical care when necessary.

She said hospital pharmacists should support stewardship through prescription reviews, monitoring antimicrobial consumption and collaborating with other healthcare professionals to optimise treatment.

She also called for antimicrobial stewardship to be integrated into pharmacy education and for stronger collaboration among healthcare professionals.

The chairman of the occasion, Olumide Akintayo, a former president of the Pharmaceutical Society of Nigeria, said healthcare professionals, government and other stakeholders had contributed to inappropriate antimicrobial use.

He called for urgent action, including improved regulation, public awareness and responsible professional practice.

He also noted that Nigeria would host the fifth Global High-Level Ministerial Conference on Antimicrobial Resistance in December.

Research grant

At the event, Olusegun Ajala of the Department of Pharmaceutical Chemistry, Faculty of Pharmacy, University of Lagos, won the 2026 Ladipo Mobolaji Abisogun-Afodu Research Grant Award in Pharmacy and received N2.7 million.

His proposal, titled Development of a Psidium guajava-Based Antibiotic Adjuvant for Restoring the Susceptibility of Multidrug-Resistant Bacteria to Conventional Antibiotics, was selected as the winning research proposal.

Deborah Ogundemuren and colleagues from the Department of Pharmaceutics and Pharmaceutical Technology came second with a proposal to develop a bioactive, sprayable hydrogel for postpartum perineal wound care as an antibiotic-sparing strategy.

Osideko Oluwaseun and colleagues from the Department of Pharmaceutical Chemistry came third with a proposal on the chemical standardisation and antibacterial characterisation of fermented maize mash supernatant, known as omidun, produced using different fermentation strategies.

World.title: From Corporate Responsibility to Community Impact: LG Electronics expands clean water initiative
World.content:
LG Electronics is strengthening its Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) commitment through its solar-powered borehole initiative, providing access to clean water for more than 20 communities across Nigeria.

The initiative reflects the company’s dedication to improving everyday living through sustainable technology and community-focused investments. By providing solar-powered water infrastructure, LG Electronics is helping underserved communities address water access challenges while reducing dependence on conventional electricity supply.

Speaking on the company’s commitment to community development, Mr Paul Mba, Head of Corporate Marketing, LG Electronics Nigeria, emphasised that innovation must deliver meaningful benefits beyond consumer products.

Mba explained that the company’s responsibility extends to identifying practical ways its technology and resources can improve lives within the communities it serves.

Recent interventions in Kaduna and Ondo States further demonstrate the national reach of the programme, which combines renewable energy, community participation and social investment to support sustainable development.

Through this growing initiative, LG Electronics continues to demonstrate that corporate responsibility is most meaningful when it translates into tangible benefits for people and communities.

World.title: APC in Ebonyi rejects ‘rainbow coalition’, says state is entirely APC
World.content:
The All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Council in Ebonyi State has rejected the existence of a proposed rainbow coalition in the state, insisting that such a political arrangement does not exist.

The Chairman of the council’s Media Directorate, Emmanuel Onwe, made the declaration on Thursday during a media briefing in Abakaliki.

Mr Onwe said the council would not discuss the coalition while focusing on Governor Francis Nwifuru’s re-election campaign.

He said the council’s director-general had reiterated the governor’s position that no rainbow coalition existed in Ebonyi.

“Ebonyi is entirely APC, as all members of the State Executive Council and the 24 members of the State House of Assembly are members of the party.

“All elected senators, members of the House of Representatives, local government chairmen and appointed officials are APC members,” he said.

However, Mr Onwe acknowledged the right of other political parties and groups to pursue their political interests through lawful democratic activities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Democracy allows individuals and groups to carry out activities in pursuance of their political interests, but such must be done within the confines of the law.

“Our duty, however, is to propagate the good works of the governor and the reasons he should be re-elected for a second term in office,” he said.

He also pledged that the APC and the state government would not condone violence, lawlessness or extra-judicial acts during political activities.

“We would promote the ideals and good works of the government, as I advise those who have grievances to report such to security agencies.

“The state government and the APC would not protect anyone found culpable in any unruly act,” he said.

Mr Onwe, a former commissioner for information and orientation in the state, said the council would conduct its campaign with honour and integrity.

READ ALSO: Court dismisses suit challenging Taraba APC chairmans emergence

The Secretary of the Media Directorate, Uchenna Orji, urged the media to report the council’s activities objectively.

Mr Orji, also a former commissioner for information and orientation, said the council would provide journalists with information about its activities.

He said the council’s statewide campaign would run from 26 November to 18 December.

World.title: BUA Chairman honoured at Silverbird Awards
World.content:
The Founder and Executive Chairman of BUA Group, Abdul Samad Rabiu, was honoured with the 2026 Silverbird Icon of Enterprise and Nation Building Award at the 2026 Silverbird Man of the Year Awards, in recognition of his significant investments across key sectors of Nigeria’s economy.

At the award ceremony, held at the prestigious Eko Hotels & Suites in Lagos, Mr Rabiu was acknowledged for achievements spanning job creation, community support, philanthropy—advancing grants to institutions through ASR Africa—and unlocking remarkable opportunities for domestic production and industrialisation.

Receiving the award on his behalf, Chimaobi Madukwe, Group Chief Operating Officer (GCOO), BUA Group, who represented the BUA Chairman at the ceremonies, commended Silverbird Group for creating the awards platform to recognise and celebrate eminent personalities for their sustainable impact, among whom is the BUA Chairman, Abdul Samad Rabiu, who stood tall, whilst also extending the chairman’s warm wishes.

Speaking further, Mr Madukwe said: “This award is dedicated, on his behalf, to our great and dedicated staff, BUA management, and all BUA loyal customers who have supported BUA over the years, believed in the vision and capacity of our chairman in delivering value to our teeming stakeholders.”

“BUA today has a total market capitalisation in excess of N25 trillion and is renowned for excellent products and services in the Nigerian market and beyond. Under the leadership of our chairman, ASR Africa was established to provide philanthropic intervention in health, education, and social development across Nigeria’s institutions”

Mr Madukwe also said the award is a call to greater impact and an encouragement to continue believing in and investing in Nigeria.

Recently, Abdul Samad Rabiu was also honoured with the 2026 Edge Industrial Leadership Icon of the Year award at the 2026 Edge Awards, while BUA won the Edge Outstanding Industrial Brand of the Year award recognising BUA’s growth under his leadership into one of Africa’s leading industrial groups.

World.title: Resident doctors demand outstanding allowances before Christmas
World.content:
The Nigerian Association of Resident Doctors (NARD) has demanded that the federal government pay 14 months’ outstanding professional allowance arrears and promotion arrears before Christmas.

This was contained in a press statement issued on Thursday following the association’s Extraordinary National Executive Council (E-NEC) meeting, which reviewed the implementation of welfare demands arising from its 46th Annual General Meeting held in Calabar, Cross River State, in September.

The statement was signed by NARD President, Ogar Idoko; Secretary-General, Besongngem Akotanchi; and Publicity and Social Secretary, Ashimom Msughter.

NARD said four months of the 18 months of outstanding Professional Allowance Table (PAT) arrears owed to healthcare workers nationwide had been paid, leaving 14 months outstanding.

It appealed to President Bola Tinubu to authorise the release of funds for payment of the remaining arrears in a single tranche before Christmas.

The association also demanded the payment of Batch 10 promotion arrears before Christmas, expressing concern over delays in their computation, verification and payment despite engagements and assurances.

Government payments

NARD commended the federal government for completing payment of the 2026 Medical Residency Training Fund (MRTF), following the payment of the final supplementary list on Wednesday, 18 November.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Additionally, the upward review and circularisation of the MRTF with adequate budgetary provision for 2027, by the President and the FG, is commendable,” it noted.

It also reported progress on the payment of the 25 and 35 per cent upward review of the Consolidated Medical Salary Structure (CONMESS), with the final supplementary list being processed for payment.

The association said it had been assured, following discussions with the Director of the Integrated Personnel and Payroll Information System (IPPIS), that the January 2026 retroactive payment of PAT arrears would be made alongside November salaries.

It also acknowledged the commencement of payment of the outstanding PAT arrears, describing the first tranche as a relief to healthcare workers and their families.

However, it said the outstanding payments and the delayed conclusion of the Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) remain major concerns.

It called on the Ministries of Labour and Employment and Health and Social Welfare, alongside other government agencies, to accelerate negotiations and ensure the agreement was approved and circularised, with appropriate budgetary provisions and a definite implementation timeline.

Doctors suspend escalation

Following the expiration of its initial two-week ultimatum and subsequent four-week extension, NARD said it had resolved to sustain constructive dialogue and engagement with the federal government rather than immediately escalate its demands.

The association mandated its National Officers’ Committee to intensify engagement with relevant authorities and report measurable progress to the council within four weeks.

It said it would review the government’s response by 20 December and determine further constitutional steps if the outstanding obligations remain unresolved.

“Industrial harmony must be sustained by concrete actions, not assurances alone,” it said.

NARD had in September, issued a two-week ultimatum to the federal government over outstanding welfare demands, warning that failure to address them could trigger industrial action. The ultimatum was subsequently extended.

In August, the association suspended planned nationwide industrial action following engagements with the federal government over outstanding welfare and professional concerns.

World.title: Okuama: Court threatens to jail AGF over disobedience to release order
World.content:
The Federal High Court in Warri, Delta State, has warned the Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, that he risks imprisonment for contempt of court if he fails to comply with an order directing the release of detained Okuama community leaders.

According to a report by Guardian, the warning followed the continued detention of the community leaders despite a 10 June 2026 order by Justice Hyeladzira Nganjiwa directing their immediate release.

The court conveyed the warning through a Form 48, titled ‘Notice of Consequences of Disobedience to Order of Court’, issued on 11 November 2026.

The notice, addressed to Mr Fagbemi at the Federal Ministry of Justice in Abuja, warned that failure to obey the release order would amount to contempt of court and could attract imprisonment.

“Take notice that unless you obey the injunction contained in the court order overleaf for the immediate release of the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 5th and 6th applicants from detention, you will be guilty of contempt of court and will be liable to be committed to prison,” the notice stated.

The case, marked FHC/WR/CS/42/2024, is a fundamental rights enforcement suit instituted by the community leaders on their own behalf and for the people of Okuama community in Ewu Kingdom, Ughelli South Local Government Area of Delta State.

The respondents include the Federal Government, the Attorney-General of the Federation, the Armed Forces of the Federation, the Minister of Defence and the Chief of Defence Staff.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The applicants listed in the proceedings include Arthur Ekpekpo, James Oghoroko, Bernard Esegba, Belvis Adogbo, Dennis Okugbaye and Mabel Owhemu.

The Form 48 specifically identifies the first, second, fourth, fifth and sixth applicants as those covered by the release directive.

The notice is a formal warning to the AGF over the alleged failure to comply with the court’s order. It does not, however, mean that Mr Fagbemi has been convicted of contempt or sentenced to imprisonment.

Background

The detention of the Okuama community leaders followed the killing of 17 Nigerian soldiers on 14 March 2024 in Okuama, during a peace mission to a communal dispute involving Okuama and neighbouring Okoloba community.

The military subsequently launched an operation in Okuama, during which residents were displaced, and homes and other properties were destroyed.

Several community members and leaders were arrested in August 2024 over the incident and detained by the Nigerian Army.

In August 2025, PREMIUM TIMES reported that six community leaders had remained in military custody for a year without trial, raising concerns about violations of their fundamental rights, including their right to personal liberty and fair hearing.

The newspaper reported that the detainees had allegedly been denied access to their doctors, lawyers and family members.

Two of the leaders, Mr Oghoroko, the community’s president-general, and Mr Okugbaye, its treasurer, were reported to have died in military custody in August 2024, a development that prompted the Chief of Defence Staff, Christopher Musa, to order an investigation.

The Defence Headquarters subsequently acknowledged the allegations and said an investigation had been ordered to establish the circumstances surrounding the reported deaths.

The prolonged detention also attracted legislative attention.

In March 2025, the House of Representatives called on the Nigerian Army to release the detained Okuama residents or charge them to court. The lawmakers also urged the military to release its investigation report and rebuild homes destroyed during the military operation.

The latest court warning adds to growing pressure on the federal authorities to comply with judicial directives and address the prolonged detention of the community’s leader.

World.title: Agric Minister dismisses N5trn agricultural loss claim as false, cites increased cereal production
World.content:
The Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Abubakar Kyari, has dismissed claims that Nigeria’s agricultural sector is recording annual losses of ₦2.5 trillion and a projected additional loss of ₦10 trillion, describing them as false and misleading.

Mr Kyari, in a statement issued on Thursday, said the claims were unsupported by credible evidence and were intended to discredit the administration of President Bola Tinubu.

He cited the 2026 Wet Season Agricultural Performance Survey conducted by the National Agricultural Extension and Research Liaison Services (NAERLS), Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria, which put Nigeria’s national cereal production at 29.393 million metric tonnes.

According to the minister, the figure represents a 1.84 per cent increase over the 2025 production level, while rice production alone stood at 9.626 million metric tonnes.

He said the figures contradicted suggestions that Nigeria’s agricultural sector was in total collapse.

Mr Kyari also defended the federal government’s 150-day duty-free food import window introduced in 2024, explaining that it was a temporary intervention designed to bridge supply gaps, improve food availability and stabilise market prices.

He said the policy expired on 31 December 2024 and had neither been renewed nor reintroduced.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

According to him, the measure was a temporary response to supply pressures and was never meant to replace domestic agricultural production.

The minister said the Tinubu administration had continued to support farmers and expand the country’s food production capacity through various interventions, including financing from the Bank of Agriculture, the National Agricultural Development Fund, mechanisation partnerships and Special Agro-Industrial Processing Zones.

He disclosed that the federal government had distributed 2.15 million bags of fertiliser free of charge to farmers across the country, alongside other agricultural inputs and support programmes.

Mr Kyari added that funding had recently been approved to accelerate the production and supply of more than three million bags of NPK fertiliser ahead of the dry season farming period.

He said the initiative would strengthen domestic fertiliser manufacturing capacity, improve the availability of farm inputs and boost agricultural production.

On post-harvest losses, the minister said the government was implementing the National Postharvest Systems Transformation Programme (NiPHaST), which focuses on developing storage warehouses and cold-chain infrastructure for food processing and preservation.

Mr Kyari also dismissed claims that more than 50 per cent of Nigeria’s rice mills had shut down, describing the assertion as inconsistent with the state of the country’s rice-processing industry.

He maintained that several rice mills across the country remained operational, adding that the federal government continued to support local processors through various interventions.

The minister argued that even if some rice mills had suspended production, it would be unfair to attribute such developments to the duty-free food import window, which expired in December 2024.

He said the government’s agricultural policy remained focused on increasing domestic production and reducing dependence on imported food.

“President Tinubu’s charge to us at all times is that we must produce what we consume and consume what we produce,” he said.

Mr Kyari, however, warned that former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar’s promise to reopen Nigeria’s borders could undermine the agricultural sector.

He argued that reopening the borders could expose local farmers to unfair competition through indiscriminate food imports.

The minister reaffirmed the commitment of his ministry to supporting farmers, strengthening local industries, increasing food production, reducing post-harvest losses and making food more affordable.

He accused unnamed individuals of exploiting the agricultural sector for political propaganda, insisting that Nigeria’s agricultural progress should be assessed by evidence rather than political claims.

World.title: Uba Sani urges Northern leaders to unite as Aliyu endorses his second-term bid
World.content:
Kaduna State Governor, Uba Sani, has called on past and present Northern leaders to develop a collective development agenda for the region, lamenting that successive administrations have derailed from the vision of the late Premier of Northern Nigeria, Sir Ahmadu Bello.

Mr Sani made the call on Wednesday at a summit on Good Governance, Inclusivity and Sustainable Development organised by the Sir Ahmadu Bello Memorial Foundation in Kaduna.

He urged the foundation to convene Northern leaders, irrespective of their political affiliations, to develop a common blueprint for addressing the region’s developmental challenges, similar to the vision pursued by the late premier.

The governor said Northern leaders must engage in honest self-assessment and acknowledge their shortcomings, insisting that they had collectively failed the people, himself included.

He also criticised politicians seeking votes ahead of the 2027 general elections by appealing to ethnic and regional sentiments rather than presenting their records in public office and concrete plans for the region.

Mr Sani argued that candidates asking Northerners to support them because of their origins should explain what they achieved for the region while occupying public offices.

The governor attributed some of his administration’s achievements to the support of President Bola Tinubu, whom he thanked for his interventions in Kaduna State over the last three and a half years.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He recalled approaching the president over the completion of the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano highway, describing it as a critical route connecting northern and southern Nigeria.

According to him, the federal government released billions of naira for the project following his intervention, and construction has reached approximately 95 per cent completion.

He also disclosed that he and the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, approached Mr Tinubu over the proposed Kaduna Light Rail Project.

Mr Sani said the president approved $865 million for the project and that the contract had been signed, with a groundbreaking ceremony expected during his planned visit to Kaduna in the next two weeks.

He described the project as a significant development for the state, which would become the second in Nigeria to have a light rail system.

The governor also highlighted his administration’s achievements since assuming office on 29 May2023, particularly in pensions, transportation, security and agriculture.

He said his government inherited pension liabilities of about ₦24 billion but had paid more than ₦21 billion to 9,683 state and local government retirees and families of deceased public servants.

He added that the administration had deployed 100 buses under its free compressed natural gas (CNG) transport scheme, recording 5.2 million passenger trips and savings of more than ₦5 billion for commuters.

On security, Mr Sani said insecurity had previously prevented residents in some communities from accessing schools and farms, but the Kaduna Peace Model had helped farmers reclaim more than 500,000 hectares of previously inaccessible farmland.

He also claimed that no school in the state remained closed because of insecurity, adding that his administration had increased annual agricultural allocations from ₦1.48 billion to more than ₦100 billion.

According to him, more than 69,000 smallholder farmers had received improved agricultural inputs, while over 1,400 truckloads of fertiliser had been distributed to more than 500,000 farmers across the state’s 23 local government areas.

Meanwhile, former Niger State Governor and Chairman of the Foundation’s Board of Trustees, Mu’azu Babangida Aliyu, endorsed Mr Sani for a second term in the 2027 governorship election, citing his performance across key sectors.

Mr Aliyu said the governor had performed creditably in security, education, healthcare, agriculture, infrastructure and human capital development, arguing that Kaduna needed continuity to consolidate the achievements.

He particularly commended Mr Sani for restoring relative peace and harmony to a state previously affected by ethno-religious crises, banditry and communal tensions.

He said farmers had returned to their farms, previously closed schools had reopened, and Muslims and Christians were living together in relative peace.

“Let us not gamble with peace. Let us not abandon progress midway. I call on all indigenes of Kaduna State to come out in 2027 and vote for Governor Uba Sani for a second term, for the sake of continuity, stability and development,” he said.

The Director-General of the foundation, Abubakar Gambo Umar, also commended the governor’s inclusive leadership, saying Kaduna needed leadership that united rather than divided its people, irrespective of ethnic, religious or social backgrounds.

Mr Umar said leadership should be assessed based on character, ideas and measurable results rather than fear, stereotypes or inherited suspicions.

He described Kaduna as the headquarters of Northern Nigeria, arguing that the state’s development had wider implications for the region and that continuity in governance was important for sustaining ongoing development efforts.

In his remarks, the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Tajudeen Abbas, represented by the Deputy Leader of the House, Ado Doguwa, called for accountability, constructive criticism and inclusive governance as essential ingredients for sustainable development.

Mr Abbas commended the foundation for providing a platform for discussions on security, good governance and development, while describing Kaduna as strategically important to Nigeria’s political, economic and social development.

He said good governance should be measured not by government promises but by leadership qualities, institutional integrity, responsible management of public resources and the impact of policies on citizens.

He identified transparency, accountability, responsiveness and respect for the rule of law as fundamental principles of effective governance.

The Speaker also commended Mr Sani for allowing his administration’s programmes and projects to undergo constructive scrutiny, describing the approach as evidence of commitment to democratic accountability and improved service delivery.

On security, he acknowledged continuing challenges in parts of Kaduna State, particularly recent attacks in Southern Kaduna, and sympathised with families affected by the incidents.

He said protecting lives and property remained a fundamental responsibility of government, while recognising the Kaduna Peace Model, inter-agency cooperation, intelligence sharing and community engagement as important components of efforts to restore security.

Mr Abbas also highlighted the establishment of the Disarmament, Demobilisation and Reintegration Peace and Security Committee, collaboration with federal security agencies, the Kaduna Vigilance Service and the State Security Trust Fund as initiatives aimed at strengthening security.

He, however, stressed that lasting peace required more than security operations, calling for sustained dialogue, reconciliation, trust and community participation.

The Speaker urged participants to ensure that the summit went beyond commendations to identify areas requiring improvement and produce practical recommendations.

He also reaffirmed the National Assembly’s commitment to responsible legislation, effective oversight and stronger collaboration among the three tiers of government to translate public resources into tangible benefits for citizens.

The summit brought together government officials, traditional rulers, civil society leaders, development partners and other stakeholders to deliberate on inclusivity, good governance and sustainable development in Kaduna State.
