World.title: Five arrested over disappearance of five-year-old boy in Cross River
World.content:
police badge

By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR

The Cross River State Police Command has arrested five persons in connection with the disappearance of a five-year-old boy in Adim community, Biase Local Government Area of the state.

The boy, a pupil of a nursery and primary school in the community, reportedly left home for school on November 16, 2026, but has not returned since then.

The Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Sunday Eitokpah, disclosed this in a statement on Thursday.

According to the statement, the boy’s father reported the disappearance at about 10:30am on November 18, after efforts by the family to trace his son proved unsuccessful.

Following the report, police operatives visited the community and commenced investigations, which led to the arrest of five suspects.

The suspects have since been transferred to the Violence Crime Response Unit (VCRU) for further investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the boy’s disappearance and determine any possible involvement of the arrested persons.

The police, however, did not disclose the identities of the suspects or the missing child, or the circumstances that led to the arrests.

The Commissioner of Police, CP Ajo Geoffrey Ordue, has directed a thorough investigation into the incident and urged the relevant investigative units to intensify efforts to establish the child’s whereabouts.

The command appealed to residents of Adim and neighbouring communities to provide credible information that could assist in locating the missing boy.

Members of the public with useful information were advised to contact the Police Control Room on 0704 177 7060 or 0705 335 5415, or report to the nearest police station.

The command reassured the family and the public of its commitment to uncovering the circumstances surrounding the disappearance and ensuring that anyone found culpable is brought to justice.

World.title: ‎South-East prosperity central to Tinubu’s agenda — Shettima
World.content:
VP Shettima

‎….Says never before has Nigeria seen top opposition figures defying partisanship to endorse candidate of another party

…I’m still in APC – Ngige

‎

‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

‎

‎ABUJA — THE Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima, has declared that the welfare and prosperity of the South-East region have been at the forefront of President Bola Tinubu’s agenda since his first day in office.

‎

‎He said targeted federal initiatives, critical infrastructure investments and inclusive governance remain central to uplifting the region and fostering lasting prosperity across all five South-Eastern states.

‎

‎Senator Shettima, who spoke on Thursday in Awka, Anambra State, while rallying support for President Bola Tinubu’s re-election at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential campaign rally, noted that he was speaking in his capacity as a titled friend of the region.

‎

‎”So, I am speaking to you today as a titled friend of the Igbo, as the Enyi Ndigbo of Anambra State, as the Enyioma Ndigbo I of Abia State, and as the Aka Ekpuchi Ọnwa I of Ebonyi State.

‎

‎”I am here to assure you that your President, our leader, His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, the Eze Udo of Igboland, has made the welfare and prosperity of the South-East a top priority since the very day he was sworn into office,” he declared.

‎

‎Acknowledging that no part of Nigeria could rival the enterprise of the South-East, VP Shettima said the geopolitical zone has proven again and again that the salvation of Nigeria rests on the promise to make the nation’s economy globally competitive.

‎

‎He pointed out that while the Tinubu administration has answered the “challenge in the most eloquent way possible,” it is proudly returning to the region to share the news that the economy is growing at an unprecedented pace after a series of difficult reforms.

‎

‎Senator Shettima appealed to the people of Anambra State to re-elect President Tinubu, basing his case not only on the effectiveness of the President’s reforms, which have brought higher federal allocations to the state, but also on the argument that the Presidency cannot be won merely by reciting phony statistics about developing nations.

‎

‎His words: “So, we have come to you today to seek your support to renew our mandate. This is not only because our reforms have made more money available to Anambra State, as they have to all South-East states and to all states of the federation.

‎

‎”The road to the Presidency cannot be paved with cramming bogus statistics about Bangladesh, like someone we all know. Anambra Kwenu, we must keep this unbeatable bond alive because there is no party that offers Ndigbo a more promising road to the Presidential Villa than the APC.”

‎

‎Stating that the performance of the Tinubu administration was clearly visible, the Vice President noted that the wave of opposition leaders endorsing the President was unprecedented.

‎

‎”I know you have seen our performance for yourselves, and your Governor has never failed to acknowledge it. Never before have we witnessed, on this scale, leading figures of opposition parties defying partisan conventions to endorse the President of another party for election. This is a remarkable moment in our political history, and we do not take it for granted,” he declared.

‎

‎The VP outlined the administration’s positive impact on the South-East, highlighting the rollout of Operation UDO KA, designed to ensure Mondays are as safe as any other day and to neutralise those destroying businesses in the region.

‎

‎He also noted the rehabilitation of the First Niger Bridge, alongside ongoing work on the Anambra access-road component of the Second Niger Bridge, the Enugu–Onitsha Expressway and the Onitsha–Owerri corridor.

‎

‎Senator Shettima described Anambra State as “the home of the political giants, intellectuals, industrialists and technocrats who have defined” Nigeria’s history, recalling that the first Nigerian President, Dr. Nnamdi Azikiwe, an Igbo man from Anambra, “was an enduring reminder of what happens when we collaborate to form a unified front.”

‎

‎He described the state Governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo, as a quintessential embodiment of the late Azikiwe, saying he readily calls to mind the Zik of Africa.

‎

‎”He (Soludo) is, like Zik of blessed memory, an intellectual of encyclopaedic distinction. He is, like Zik, a pan-Nigerian advocate with practical insights into the nature of power. He is, like Zik, a scholar whose work preceded his entry into elected office.

‎

‎”These two men have shown us the possibility of an enduring bridge between the Igbo and the rest of Nigerians, and we shall honour what they have sacrificed to compel us to think beyond the confines of our ethnicities, our regions, our religions, our languages and our political affiliations,” he added.

‎

‎In his remarks, APC National Chairman, Professor Nentawe Goshwe Yilwatda, while praising Governor Soludo for “making a smart decision to canvass for the winning team,” said he had come to Anambra State to present the best candidate to the people: the man who knows the way in education, the economy and infrastructure, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

‎

‎Urging the people to vote for the President for continued progress, he said President Tinubu cares about education and wants every Nigerian child to be educated. He added that gone are the days when a Nigerian child who aspired to go to school could not do so because there was no money.

‎

‎Also, Deputy Speaker of the House of Representatives, Rt. Hon. Benjamin Kalu, advocated a shift from sentimental politics to strategic cooperation to drive development in Anambra State and the wider South-East.

‎

‎He argued that the success of Igbo people in business and commerce stems from strategic thinking rather than sentiment, just as he suggested that political progress requires moving away from protest-based approaches and focusing instead on strategic alliances.

‎

‎For his part, the Governor of Imo State and Chairman of the Progressive Governors Forum (PGF), Senator Hope Uzodimma, commended Governor Soludo for his wise decision to support the President, noting that the Igbo have been at the forefront of development since the end of the civil war.

‎

‎While asking the people to vote wisely on Election Day, he urged them to visit the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs), describing a vote for President Tinubu as a stand for unity, progress and further development.

‎

‎Former Governor of Anambra State and immediate past Minister of Labour and Employment, Senator Chris Ngige said that people should be free to choose their preferred candidate in 2027 election.

‎

‎Ngige, who said that he still remained a member of the APC but on sabbatical, however, called on the people of the state to vote APC in all positions.

‎

‎Wrapping up, the Director-General of the APC Presidential Campaign Council, Senator Abdulaziz Yari, called for a solid national coalition, urging South-East leaders to support President Tinubu in 2027.

‎

‎He charged the region to embrace the national political coalition and move into the mainstream, emphasising that achieving the Presidency requires broad cross-regional alliances rather than isolated regional efforts.

‎

‎Senator Yari cautioned against political narratives suggesting that a single-term presidency could be achieved without broad national consensus, stressing that sustainable political power is built through partnership and inclusion.

World.title: 2027: I advised Obi to support Atiku, but he refused — Momodu
World.content:
Dele Momodu

A chieftain of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Dele Momodu, has disclosed that he advised the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, to support former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar ahead of the 2027 general election, but the former Anambra State governor rejected the suggestion.

Momodu said Obi insisted on pursuing his presidential ambition independently, adding that he had no objection to the decision.

The publisher of Ovation International disclosed this on Thursday during an appearance on Channels Television’s Politics Today, where he discussed the opposition’s chances in the 2027 presidential election.

Asked whether he considered Atiku ahead of Obi in the presidential race, Momodu expressed confidence in the former vice-president’s political standing, describing him as a politician with national and international appeal.

“There is no question about that. I’ve told Obi to his face. He’s my friend, and I like him,” he said.

He added: “I told him that he should support Atiku, but he said no, he will run it

World.title: Tinubu vows to end export of unprocessed solid minerals
World.content:
…Sector generates over N100bn in 2026 — Alake

By Gabriel Ewepu

ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu on Thursday reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to ending the export of unprocessed solid minerals, saying Nigeria must develop local capacity to add value to its mineral resources.

Tinubu stated this in his presidential keynote address at the Nigeria Now! Investing in Energy, Infrastructure and Mining Summit in Abuja, with the theme, “United Nigeria, New Horizons, One Investment Destination”. The summit ends on November 20, 2026.

The President said the mining sector required improved geological information, transparent licensing, responsible exploration and increased investment in beneficiation and processing to support local industries, create skilled jobs and deliver benefits to host communities.

He said: “In mining, we’re equally determined to move beyond the export of unprocessed resources. Better geological information, transparent licensing, responsible exploration, and greater investment in beneficiation and processing must support Nigerian industries, skilled employment and meaningful benefits for host communities.

“Our mission is to build integrated value chains in which Nigerian enterprises participate and in which domestic capabilities grow.

“We invite investors to bring technology, finance and commercial enterprise while we continue to strengthen the regulatory certainty and institutional support needed for sustainable returns.

“Opportunities are substantial, but they must be converted into well-structured bankable projects rather than remaining prospects on paper. This is why Nigeria now must distinguish itself.”

Tinubu said the government was committed to creating an investment environment that would encourage private-sector participation and support the development of integrated value chains in the mining industry.

Earlier, the Minister of Solid Minerals Development, Dr Dele Alake, said reforms introduced by the Tinubu administration had increased revenue from the solid minerals sector to more than N100 billion in 2026.

Alake said the sector generated about N6 billion annually when he assumed office, but revenue rose to N38 billion in 2024 and N70 billion in 2025.

He said: “When I assumed office, the sector’s total annual revenue stood at just ₦6 billion. However, through reforms, the local value addition policy, the digitisation of mining processes, and efforts to sanitise operations within the sector, that figure increased from ₦6 billion to ₦38 billion by 2024.

“By 2025, it had risen to ₦70 billion. And just about a week ago, the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) informed us that we had crossed the ₦100 billion mark this year.

“All of this has been achieved through reforms, deliberate initiatives, creativity, a sense of responsibility, and the public conscience to do what is right for the people and leave a lasting legacy.”

The minister also said the establishment of the Mining Marshals had strengthened efforts to tackle illegal mining.

According to him, more than 300 suspected illegal mining operators had been apprehended, while over 100 mining sites had been recovered from illegal operators and restored to their legitimate owners.

Alake, however, alleged that some operators affected by the enforcement activities were sponsoring moves to scrap the Mining Marshals.

“As I speak, there have been moves to scrap the Mining Marshals. These moves are sponsored by the operators whom the Mining Marshals have been deployed to bring to justice,” he said.

The minister also defended the removal of fuel subsidy, arguing that the use of savings from the policy had supported infrastructure development across the country’s six geopolitical zones. He criticised calls for the restoration of the subsidy.

Meanwhile, the Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Gboyega Oyetola, said the sector had recorded progress since the ministry was established in 2023.

Oyetola listed improvements in maritime security, port reforms and the approval of Nigeria’s first National Policy on Marine and Blue Economy among the developments recorded.

He disclosed that revenue generated by agencies under the ministry increased from N700.79 billion in 2023 to N1.83 trillion in 2025.

The minister urged investors to explore opportunities in ports, shipping, shipbuilding, fisheries, aquaculture, maritime tourism and logistics.

World.title: 2027: PDP insists on coalition to challenge Nwifuru in Ebonyi
World.content:
Gov Nwifuru

By Jeff Agbodo, Abakaliki

ABAKALIKI — The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Ebonyi State has insisted that a coalition of political parties and interest groups exists to challenge the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led government of Governor Francis Nwifuru in the 2027 governorship election.

The party said the APC’s claim that it was not part of any coalition did not invalidate the existence of political groups working together to challenge the incumbent administration.

The media aide to the PDP governorship candidate, Dr Ifeanyichukwu Odii, Dr Jerry Uhuo, stated this while reacting to comments by the APC campaign spokesman, Senator Emmanuel Onwe, who had alleged that no coalition existed in Ebonyi State.

Uhuo accused Onwe of misunderstanding the concept of political coalition, explaining that it involved political interest groups coming together to pursue common objectives, including electoral victory.

“From all indications, Sen. Onwe appears not to understand what coalition means in the context of the current political engineering.

“Coalition is a coming together of political interest groups to work together for the interest of promoting a common interest and winning election.

“The fact that the Ebonyi APC claims non-membership of such a coalition does not mean that the coalition does not exist in Ebonyi. He admitted that any group could come together to form a coalition. That alone contradicts his original position,” he said.

Uhuo argued that the formation of a political coalition did not require the endorsement of a state government, insisting that political parties and interest groups were free to collaborate.

He added that the PDP and other political groups were already working together to challenge the APC-led administration in the state ahead of the 2027 elections.

“In the case of Ebonyi, the PDP and other political groups are already working together to dislodge the government of Governor Francis Nwifuru,” he stated.

World.title: 14 killed as truck carrying passengers, cattle crashes in Niger
World.content:
FILE IMAGE

NO fewer than 14 persons reportedly lost their lives in a road accident involving a DAF truck conveying 35 cattle and several passengers along Kontagora Road in Niger State.



Zagazola Makama, a counter-insurgency publication, reported that the accident occurred around 11 a.m. on November 17 near Ibeto, as the truck, with registration number Lagos AZL 267 XH, travelled from Koko Local Government Area of Kebbi State to Lagos.



“Police sources said an unidentified vehicle travelling in the same direction reportedly attempted to overtake the truck but brushed against it, causing the driver to lose control before the vehicle fell,” Makama said.



“The truck driver and 13 other occupants reportedly died at the scene.



“Those identified among the deceased included Umar, 45, the driver, from Kaoje; Anas Suleiman, 25, and Sufiyanu Suleiman, 40, both from Koko; Salim Abu Dogo, 30; Abubakar Shehu, 45; Yahaya Abubakar, 30; and Manu, 35, all from Dankigari.

“Others were Rufai Umar, 25, from Bagudo; Faruk Tudu Kaoje, 20, from Kaoje; Umar Abubakar, 30, from Saradosa; Salisu Idry, 35, from Bagodo; and Abubakar Alhaji, 25, from Kaoje.”

Police sources told Makama that relatives identified the bodies, while those claimed by their families were released for burial in accordance with Islamic rites.

The publication added that two unidentified bodies had been deposited at the mortuary of Kontagora General Hospital. “The vehicle allegedly involved in the overtaking manoeuvre was later traced to Kaboji in Magama Local Government Area and taken to the Area Command Office,” Makama said.

“However, the driver of the vehicle reportedly fled and remains at large.”

According to the publication, the Niger State Police Command said investigation was ongoing to establish the full circumstances of the accident and apprehend the fleeing driver.

World.title: FG issues Executive Order to end open defecation by 2030
World.content:
*Once upon a time: Open defecation in Bauchi

By Gabriel Ewepu

ABUJA — The Federal Government has unveiled a new Executive Order to accelerate Nigeria’s efforts to eliminate open defecation by 2030, with state and local governments urged to strengthen sanitation financing, accountability and community mobilisation.

The Open Defecation Free Nigeria by 2030 and Other Related Matters Order, 2025, was unveiled on Thursday during the commemoration of World Toilet Day and the seventh anniversary of the Clean Nigeria campaign in Abuja.

Vice President Kashim Shettima, represented by the Senior Special Assistant to the President on Delivery and Coordination in the Office of the Vice President, Akubo Adegbe, described the Executive Order as a decisive step towards translating government commitments into measurable sanitation outcomes.

Shettima said the order marked a transition from fragmented interventions to stronger coordination, measurable results and sustainable national progress.

He disclosed that since the launch of the Clean Nigeria campaign in 2019, 185 of the country’s 774 local government areas had attained Open Defecation Free (ODF) status, while Jigawa and Katsina remained the only states certified as open defecation-free.

While acknowledging the progress recorded, the Vice President said Nigeria still had considerable ground to cover, urging states yet to achieve ODF status to establish monthly and quarterly targets and make their progress publicly available.

He also warned against a reversal of gains in communities already certified as open defecation-free, stressing the need for sustained monitoring and accountability to protect existing achievements.

According to him, achieving the 2030 target would require sustainable financing, reliable data, stronger institutions, effective implementation and continuous behavioural change.

Shettima called on state and local governments to take ownership of the campaign by allocating adequate resources and strengthening sanitation institutions.

He also urged development partners, the private sector, traditional rulers, community leaders and civil society organisations to sustain their support for the initiative.

The Vice President, who chairs the Steering Committee of the Clean Nigeria Project, reaffirmed the Federal Government’s commitment to working with subnational governments, adding that the National Economic Council would also be deployed to advance and sustain the national sanitation agenda.

Linking the campaign to this year’s World Toilet Day theme, “Sanitation and Gender Equality”, Shettima highlighted the disproportionate burden poor sanitation places on women and girls.

He said inadequate access to safe and private sanitation facilities undermined their health, security, dignity, education and participation in economic and social activities.

He therefore called for inclusive policies and investments that address the sanitation needs of women, girls, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups.

Meanwhile, the Minister of Water Resources and Sanitation, Joseph Utsev, said the Clean Nigeria campaign had evolved beyond public awareness and mobilisation into a national platform for policy coordination, institutional engagement, community participation and performance monitoring.

Utsev highlighted the revised Clean Nigeria Strategy 2025–2030, which is structured around six strategic pillars, as well as the newly introduced Clean Nigeria Real Time Monitoring and Information System, designed to improve data management, track implementation and strengthen accountability.

Reflecting on the campaign’s seven-year journey, the minister identified five critical lessons, including the need to translate political commitment into adequate financing and practical action, prevent communities from relapsing into open defecation, strengthen community ownership, adopt a multi-sectoral approach and ensure reliable data informs planning and resource allocation.

Also speaking, the Minister of Youth Development, Ayodele Olawande, said his ministry was contributing to the campaign through youth mobilisation and community advocacy.

He disclosed that more than 1,000 youth volunteers had been trained to promote sanitation awareness and behavioural change.

Olawande said pilot interventions were ongoing in Bauchi, Kaduna, Benue, Ebonyi and Oyo states, adding that young people had an important role to play in promoting gender-responsive sanitation.

He specifically emphasised menstrual hygiene education, access to safe and private toilet facilities and the need to eliminate the stigma associated with menstruation.

Goodwill messages were also delivered by the former Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, Didi Esther Walson-Jack, alongside representatives of civil society organisations, professional bodies and development partners, who reaffirmed the importance of collective action in achieving Nigeria’s 2030 open defecation elimination target.

World.title: Shettima, Issoufou reflect on Buhari’s legacy at biography launch
World.content:
‎–Late ex-President demonstrated leadership defined by character, not power –VP

‎–As Issoufou urges balanced assessment of Buhari’s achievements, controversies

‎

‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

‎

‎ABUJA — THE Vice President, Senator Kashim Shettima and former President of Niger Republic, Mahamadou Issoufou, yesterday reflected on the legacy of the late former Nigerian leader, Muhammadu Buhari, describing his life and political career as an important chapter in Nigeria’s history that offers enduring lessons on leadership, character and public accountability.

‎

While Shettima said Buhari demonstrated that the true measure of leadership lies in personal character rather than the power and privileges of public office, Issoufou urged Nigerians to assess the former President’s legacy objectively, taking into account his achievements, decisions and controversies.

‎

‎The two leaders spoke at the public presentation of “Muhammadu Buhari: The Authorised Biography”, a three-volume account of the former President’s life and political career, held at the Nigerian Army Conference Centre and Suites, Abuja.

‎

‎The Vice President, who was represented by the Special Adviser to the President on General Duties, Office of the Vice President, Dr Aliyu Modibbo, said Buhari’s modest lifestyle, personal discipline and devotion to national service distinguished him from many political leaders.

‎

‎Speaking on the theme, “The Life We Leave to History”, the Vice President recalled lessons from his personal relationship with the late President, particularly his indifference to material possessions and commitment to Nigeria.

‎

‎”He taught me that the dignity of office depends upon the character of its occupant. He also taught me that a leader’s example continues to speak long after he is out of service,” Shettima said.

‎

‎He described Buhari’s Spartan lifestyle as remarkable in a political environment where public office is sometimes pursued to satisfy private interests.

‎

‎”His Spartan lifestyle distinguished him in a world where too many seek public office to satisfy private appetites. There was something arresting about a man who could command so much and desire so little,” he stated.

‎

‎Shettima noted that Buhari’s political journey, spanning military leadership and democratic governance, attracted both extraordinary public affection and strong criticism over his policies and decisions.

‎

‎He, however, said the former President’s enduring connection with millions of Nigerians reflected a distinctive leadership disposition that defied conventional political calculations.

‎

‎Beyond the tribute, the Vice President described the biography as an important contribution to historical documentation, institutional memory and public accountability.

‎

‎He urged serving public officials to preserve records of their decisions and explain the circumstances surrounding them, warning that failure to do so could leave future generations vulnerable to speculation and distorted accounts of national events.

‎

‎”The privilege of serving a nation includes the obligation of explanation. History becomes poorer whenever those who could have supplied its evidence leave it with unanswered questions,” he said.

‎

‎Shettima commended Buhari for authorising the biographical project during his lifetime and participating in the research, noting that his recollections, alongside interviews and documentary evidence, would enrich the historical record.

‎

‎In his remarks, Issoufou, who chaired the occasion, said the publication provided an opportunity to move beyond mourning and subject Buhari’s life and leadership to objective historical reflection.

‎

‎He described the three-volume work as a significant contribution to Nigeria’s historical record, particularly for younger generations who did not have personal encounters with the former President.

‎

‎”Today, in presenting these volumes, we move from mourning to historical reflection. Mourning belongs first to the family, friends and contemporaries. History belongs to everyone, including generations that never knew the man,” he said.

‎

‎Issoufou cautioned against presenting Buhari’s legacy in absolute terms, insisting that a fair historical assessment must accommodate both his accomplishments and shortcomings.

‎

‎”None of us can claim to have the final word on Muhammadu Buhari. Nor should any biography pretend to do so,” he added.

‎

‎Former Senate President Anyim Pius Anyim, who represented former President Goodluck Jonathan, also recalled Buhari’s commitment to personal relationships, describing it as an important aspect of his character that deserved recognition.

‎

‎Earlier, the author, Dr Udu Yakubu, said the three-volume biography was the culmination of more than two and a half years of research, interviews and documentation.

‎

‎He acknowledged Buhari’s cooperation throughout the process, noting that the former President granted him access to relevant information without compromising his independence as a researcher.

‎

‎”He gave the work the legitimacy of access without taking away my independence of judgement. I regret that he did not live to see these works completed, but the record now carries his voice,” Yakubu said.

‎

‎Reviewing the first volume, “Buhari: The Phenomenon”, Ambassador Dr Chijioke Wigwe described it as an authoritative account of the former President’s life, containing some of his final substantial recorded reflections.

‎

‎He traced Buhari’s journey from his upbringing in Daura, Katsina State, through his military career and appointment as Federal Commissioner for Petroleum Resources to his emergence as Head of State and eventual return to farming after leaving office.

‎

‎Wigwe observed that Buhari’s firm and uncompromising disposition shaped his leadership and influenced the circumstances surrounding his removal from power.

‎

‎He said the biography offered an opportunity to examine Buhari’s character and place in Nigeria’s history without sentiment or prejudice.

‎

‎”History must neither flatter nor condemn blindly but must examine dispassionately the human being whose life became part of the Nigerian story,” he said.

‎

‎Also reviewing the second and third volumes, The Presidency and “The Reckoning”, Ambassador Professor Tijjani Muhammad-Bande identified institutional discipline, accountability and national unity as defining features of Buhari’s leadership.

‎

‎He recalled the former President’s insistence that public funds spent on government projects must translate into tangible results, as well as his respect for institutional procedures and the constitutional tenure of public officeholders.

‎

‎Muhammad-Bande further described Buhari as a committed believer in Nigeria’s unity who opposed violent attempts to undermine the country’s territorial integrity.

‎

‎He said Buhari recognised the constitutional right to peaceful protest but maintained a firm position against taking up arms against the Nigerian state, regarding national unity as a responsibility that transcended ethnic, religious and political divisions.

‎

‎The three-volume biography examines Buhari’s personal background, military career, political journey and eight-year presidency, providing a historical account of a leader whose legacy continues to attract debate across Nigeria.

World.title: Forex Experts Seek Stronger Collaboration to Boost Responsible Trading
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Oluchi Chibuzor

Forex Trading Experts have called for stronger collaboration between regulators, brokers and other players in the financial technology ecosystem to address misinformation, build trust and promote responsible participation in the foreign exchange market worth about $9.5trillion daily.

Speaking at the second edition of the Africa Forex Trading Expo in Lagos, the Director of Azelia Expo, Zach Kiratu, said the absence of a central platform for stakeholders to interact, alongside widespread misinformation about the industry, informed the establishment of the expo.

He explained that the platform brings together forex brokers, cryptocurrency exchanges, payment service providers, fintech companies, educators, regulators, affiliates and introducing brokers to encourage engagement and collaboration.

According to him, “One of the reasons we started the expo was that there was a lack of a central point where all the players could meet. We also observed that there is a lot of misinformation out there about forex trading, with people painting it as gambling, which it is not.

“It is a viable business, but the kind of information that has been channelled out there is painting forex trading as gambling, which it is not. So that was also one of the reasons we started the expo, to demystify forex trading and even crypto and all these, what you are calling, digital assets. So we want to demystify them, we want people to understand, because when we talk about the forex market, this is a very big market that has about $9.6 trillion daily.”

Similarly, the Business Development Manager, FXTM, Inahoro Rachel, called for greater efforts to demystify financial markets and encourage more women to embrace forex trading professionally.

She said “misconceptions portraying trading as gambling or quick-money-making schemes could discourage women from exploring opportunities in the market. So they need a mentor to professionally learn the rudimentary skills to trade.”

Founder Spark FX Academy, Citadel Egigba, emphasised the importance of education before entering the forex market, advising prospective traders to understand its operations and risks before committing funds.

“The first thing to do is not to begin to trade. The first thing is to understand the system. You need to go through the learning phase,” Egigba said.

World.title: Aké Festival 2026 Opens in Lagos with Call to Protect ‘Native Intelligence’
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Yinka Olatunbosun

Writers, poets, filmmakers and cultural thinkers from across Africa and the diaspora converged on the Silkwood Hotel in Ikeja GRA on Thursday, November 19, for the opening ceremony of the 14th Aké Arts and Book Festival.

Running from November 19 to 21 under the thought-provoking theme ‘Native Intelligence,’ the 2026 edition of Africa’s premier literary gathering interrogates the intersection of ancestral African knowledge, indigenous languages and emerging technologies in an era increasingly dominated by artificial intelligence (AI).

Organised by the Book Buzz Foundation, the three-day festival features 24 curated events—including 11 book chats, six panel discussions, film screenings, and the signature Palmwine and Poetry Night.

Literary heavyweights and emerging voices on this year’s roster include Nnedi Okorafor, Chika Unigwe, A. Igoni Barrett, Wole Talabi, and Wana Udobang, alongside key institutional partnerships with Sterling Bank, the Open Society Foundations, Granta magazine, and the Caine Prize for African Writing.

Speaking at the kick-off of the festival, Founder and Festival Director Lola Shoneyin emphasized that the 2026 theme was designed to challenge how society defines and values knowledge, warning against allowing indigenous wisdom to be sidelined by algorithms.

“There’s the intelligence that comes from education. Then there’s the intelligence from the people,” Shoneyin said. “This gives us an opportunity to talk about that kind of intelligence. As you know, with the Aké Festival, we’re not shy. We will have important conversations. We are constantly in pursuit of the unsayable. And that means we want to talk about the matters that are important to us, the things that we want people to take away and remember for months and years after leaving that festival.”

Shoneyin also reiterated her commitment to strengthening local publishing ecosystems, noting that African writers should not rely on Western validation to define literary excellence.

She commended the host state for stepping up its institutional support for the literary arts, highlighting a new Lagos State Government initiative providing N20,000 book grants and festival access to 100 young residents under the age of 25.

Representing the Lagos State Government—which partnered with the festival through the Office of the Special Adviser on Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture—officials reaffirmed Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu’s commitment to positioning Lagos as the creative capital of the continent.

“Lagos remains the city where every heritage finds its place, and where creativity does not simply exist—it thrives,” the state government representative stated. “By partnering with the Aké Arts and Book Festival and investing directly in book grants for our youth, we are ensuring that the next generation of Lagosians remains deeply connected to our indigenous stories, critical thinking and cultural identity.”

As discussions get underway in Ikeja, attendees are set to explore topics ranging from speculative fiction and Nigerian animation to the ethics of AI in creative writing, cementing Aké’s reputation as a vital forum for shaping Africa’s intellectual future.

World.title: Atiku Demands Independent Audit of INEC’s AI System Ahead of 2027 Elections
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has demanded that the Independent National Electoral Commission immediately disclose and submit to independent scrutiny any artificial intelligence system it intends to use in processing polling unit results for the 2027 general elections. Nigerians must know whether a machine will be allowed to delay, reject or interfere with the transmission of their votes before the first ballot is cast.

Atiku, in a statement issued by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, said he had written to the INEC Chairman on behalf of the African Democratic Congress and allied democratic stakeholders to demand algorithmic transparency, an independent audit and clear rules for human oversight. The petition follows INEC’s announced integration of AI and intelligent document processing into the route between its Data Verification and Authentication System, DIVAS, and the INEC Result Viewing portal, IReV.

“INEC cannot ask Nigerians to trust a system whose rules they are forbidden to see. If an algorithm can flag a polling unit result sheet, the public deserves to know what triggers that flag, who set the threshold, who can change it and what happens to the result afterward.

“The danger is plain. A valid result sheet photographed in poor light, bearing unfamiliar handwriting or produced on worn paper must not be held back because a machine fails to recognise it. Nor can INEC leave room for a system that treats errors in one area as harmless while treating similar errors elsewhere as grounds to delay results. Such decisions would affect real votes, cast by real people, whose rights cannot be made dependent on secret software settings.”

Atiku said INEC must publish the system’s technical and operational framework, including the sources of its training data, the criteria used to flag discrepancies and the identities of its developers and third party vendors. He demanded that independent cybersecurity experts, political party technology representatives and civil society technologists be given access to the source code, training data and decision logs for a meaningful audit before the nationwide mock accreditation scheduled for 28 November 2026.

He also called on INEC to publish a clear procedure for every result sheet flagged by the system: who reviews it, how the decision is recorded, how political parties are notified and how an error can be challenged promptly. AI, he said, must remain an administrative aid under human supervision. It must have no automated power to delete, alter or permanently block a result.

“The polling unit result sheet, Form EC8A, records what happened where the people voted. INEC must publicly reaffirm the legal status of the physical form completed and signed at the polling unit, and explain how it will resolve any conflict between that document and an AI assessment. A machine’s verdict cannot be allowed to quietly displace the evidence witnessed by voters and party agents.”

Atiku further demanded real time monitoring access for political parties, through a dedicated dashboard or suitable observer interface, so they can detect unusual patterns of flagging, delays or blocked uploads while an election is under way. He called on the National Assembly to summon INEC’s leadership and ICT Directorate for public answers about the system’s design, safeguards and audit arrangements.

He urged election observers and international partners to pay attention to the digital handling of results alongside events at polling units. Voters, he added, should lawfully document results as announced and displayed at their polling units so there is a public record against which uploaded results can be checked.

“Our Affordable Life campaign is a promise to bring down the crushing cost of living, restore opportunity and make government answer to the people it serves. Nigerians must be free to accept or reject that promise at the ballot box. No hidden algorithm should stand between a struggling family’s vote and the change that family hopes to see.

“INEC has an opportunity to answer these questions before mistrust hardens into a crisis. Open the system. Let independent experts test it. Publish the rules for correcting its mistakes. Guarantee that no valid vote will disappear behind a screen marked ‘flagged’.

“Nigerians will not accept an election in which they can watch the counting at their polling unit but cannot see what happens when their result enters INEC’s digital system. Families facing the daily struggle to afford food, fuel and basic necessities deserve the power to choose a better life. Their votes belong to them. INEC must prove, in public and before election day, that its technology will protect those votes.”

World.title: South-East Leaders Converge on Enugu to Chart Part for Prosperity
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

From Tony Icheku in Owerri

Nigeria’s former Minister of Finance and Economic Planning, Dr. Kalu Idika Kalu will on Thursday, November 26, 2026 in Enugu, present a keynote address on economic transformation and the future of South-East geo-political zone to flag off the ‘South-East Policy and Impact Conference 2026’

The conference, which will declared open by Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah with the theme “From Policy and Investment to Shared Prosperity and Impact” is organised by the Policy and Impact Forum (PIF), a governmental organisation and holds at the Presidential Hotel, Enugu.

The Executive Director of PIF, Agwu Amogu in a statement said the conference whose objectives is aimed at moving conversations beyond policy announcements to practical actions that will strengthen enterprises, create jobs and improve livelihoods across the five South-East states will attract policymakers, investors, business leaders and development stakeholders to examine how ongoing economic reforms can translate into shared prosperity for the region.

“The real test of economic reforms and publimc investments is their impact on people’s lives. We must ask how policies translate into opportunities for businesses, jobs for our young people, stronger institutions and prosperity for our communities,” Amogu said.

He added that the conference would provide an opportunity to identify practical pathways to action and ensure that the South-East positions itself to benefit from emerging opportunities as Nigeria implements significant economic reforms.

The programme will feature a presentation by Professor Okey Ikechukwu, a Governance and certified Management Consultant on the Federal Investments and Development Scorecard, 2023 to 2026.

He added that a high-level panel discussion will explore how public policies, government investments and private capital can drive inclusive economic growth and measurable development outcomes. Discussions will cover infrastructure and connectivity, agriculture and value chains, manufacturing, MSMEs, trade and export, investment mobilisation, public-private partnerships, education, skills development, research and innovation.

There will also be an interactive stakeholder session bringing together government, businesses, investors, professional bodies, community leaders, civil society and young people to discuss regional priorities and opportunities.

Amogu said the organisers expect the engagement to generate actionable recommendations, partnership opportunities and priority actions for sustained development across the region.

“Our objective is to move beyond policy conversations and investment announcements to focus on implementation, collaboration and results,” he affirmed

World.title: NOIPOLLS: 76% of Nigerians Dissatisfied with Working of Democracy in 27 Years
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

* Only 37% expect 2027 elections to be free and fair

* Economic Society: Slower inflation, not sign of lower prices, lists pathways to national rebirth

*Presidency: Worst is over, thumbs up economic trajectory

Ndubuisi Francis in Abuja

Nigeria’s foremost public opinion polling and market research firm, NOIPolls Limited, has revealed that 76 per cent of Nigerians were dissatisfied with the working of democracy since the country returned to civil rule.

Also, only about 37 per cent of Nigerians expect the 2027 elections to be free and fair.

NOIPOLL’s Chief Executive Officer, Dr. Chike Nwangwu, presented the figures in Abuja at the National Growth and Development Forum 2026, organised by MoneyLine with Nancy on AIT.

The event themed, ‘The Nigeria We Want: The Economy, Your Money, Our Future,’ drew participation from leading stakeholders in the public and private sectors, the academia, and development finance institutions (DFIs), among others.

Nwangwu, who presented perception polls on the society, stated that 76 per cent of the citizens submitted that democracy had not fared better 27 years after, while 55 per cent of Nigerians believe that democracy was preferable to other forms of government.

Similarly, 57 per cent of Nigerians claimed that Nigeria was moving in the wrong direction as a nation.

However, Nwangwu disclosed that inspite of the their disappoinments in many spheres of national life, 79 per cent were still proud to be Nigerians, with another 79 per cent hopeful about the future.

In his goodwill message, President of the Nigerian Economic Society (NES), Dr. Baba Yusuf Musa, argued that the theme of the event was a reminder that economic policy was never merely a contest of statistics, “but the mother calculating what she can afford in the market; the graduate in search of the dignity of work; the farmer hoping to harvest in safety; the entrepreneur weighing the cost of power and credit”.

According to him, “The Nigeria we want must be built upon the Nigeria we have, and the Nigeria we have was shaped by those who came before us.

“Let me therefore begin, as economists must, with the evidence, including the evidence of history.

“History first offers credit. In the era of our National Development Plans, Nigeria thought in decades, not in budget cycles. The First Plan of 1962 to 1968 gave us the Kainji Dam, the Niger Bridge at Onitsha and our first refinery at Port Harcourt.

“Later plans gave us the Warri and Kaduna refineries, new federal universities, the unity colleges and great arterial highways. Some 60 years on, many remain the backbone of our national infrastructure. History also demands candour.

“Somewhere along the way, we lost vital links between plan and performance. We built, but did not always maintain. The oil windfall of the 1970s drew us away from the agriculture and non-oil exports that had sustained us.”

Musa regretted that strategic projects such as the Ajaokuta Steel Complex, begun with great promise, have yet to be fulfilled after several decades, adding that when formal planning gave way in the mid-1980s, long-term strategy too often yielded to visions that changed with administrations.

The NES President noted that while he was not indicting any generation or government, a nation that does not learn from its past was condemned to pay for it twice.

He offered five pathways towards attaining a country of Nigerians’ dream.

The NES President underscored the need for growth that creates jobs and reaches the poor, adding that over half of poor Nigerians earn their living in agriculture.

“Raising farm productivity, through storage, rural roads, irrigation, security and finance, is therefore not merely agricultural policy. It is poverty policy, food-price policy and security policy.”

Second, he called for predictable prices, savings that hold their value, and credit within reach, stressing that slower inflation does not mean lower prices as the price level is still some 12 per cent above last December.

“The easing of the policy rate must find its way to the lending rates faced by small businesses, the true engine of employment. That requires fiscal and monetary policies that are credible, coordinated and clearly communicated.

“Third, an economy that produces what it consumes and sells to the world. No nation has built enduring prosperity on imports alone. Reliable power, efficient ports, secure trade routes and enforceable contracts together form the architecture of competitiveness.

“And may I gently suggest that we stop celebrating projects because they are launched, and judge them by the services they deliver. Under the African Continental Free Trade Area, Nigeria should become the factory floor and services hub of a market of 1.4 billion people.

“Fourth, investment in people above all else. Our youthful population is either our greatest dividend or our gravest risk, and it is policy, not providence, that will decide which. Foundational learning, primary healthcare, digital skills and the full economic participation of women are among the highest-return investments any economist can recommend.

“Social protection must be a bridge to opportunity, not a destination. Inclusion is not charity; it is a condition for national productivity,” Musa argued, and called for disciplined public finance and credible public institutions.

According to him, “Our deeper challenge is the gap between announcement and implementation. Debt is a financing instrument, not a development strategy. And every naira of public spending should answer three questions: What problem will it solve? Who will benefit? And how will we know it worked?Permit me a word of counsel.”

Also, in his goodwill message, President of the Capital Market Academics of Nigeria (CMAN), Prof. Uche Uwaleke, said the theme spoke to a fundamental question that should underpin every economic policy conversation, vis-a-vis how to

translate economic reforms, policy interventions and improvements in macroeconomic indicators into tangible improvements in the living conditions of ordinary Nigerians.

By and large, he said the success of any economic reform must be measured not merely by improvements in gross domestic product (GDP), foreign exchange stability, government revenue or external reserves, but by its capacity to create jobs, improve purchasing power, reduce poverty, expand opportunities and enhance the overall quality of life of citizens.

He maintained that while macroeconomic stabilisation is an important foundation for sustainable growth, it must be complemented by policies that stimulate productive investment, support small and medium-scale enterprises, strengthen domestic production, promote financial inclusion and ensure that economic opportunities reach households and businesses across the country.

The Special Adviser to the President, Dr. Tope Fasua, noted that inspite of some of the adverse fallouts of the economic reforms, the worst was over, admonishing against perpetual despondency.

He explained that the country was better with the reforms despite the temporary hardship faced by Nigerians, adding that macroeconomic fundamentals remain the fulcrum for microeconomic well-being to kick in.

Earlier in her welcome address, the convener of the event, Nancy Illoh-Nnaji, underscored the necessity of the public form, saying Moneyline with Nancy on AIT had deliberately positioned its platforms as a bridge between government, policymakers, institutions and the public.

“We don’t just report what institutions are doing; we want people to understand why it matters and what it means for their lives,” she said.

World.title: Ebonyi APC-CC Warns Against Political Violence, Flags of Campaigns Nov. 26
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

Benjamin Nworie in Abakaliki

The All Progressives Congress (APC) Campaign Council (APC-CC) in Ebonyi State said the party would flag off its campaigns on November 26, in Afikpo council area, warning against political violence and any form of lawlessness during the 2027 general elections.

The Director of the Directorate of Communications of the APC Divine Mandate Campaign Organisation for 2027, Senator Emmanuel Onwe, stated this on Thursday during the inaugural press briefing of the campaign organisation at the party’s secretariat in Abakaliki.

Senator Onwe maintained that the party’s commitment to democratic competition would be demonstrated through issue-based engagement, constructive political discourse and the presentation of its administration’s record in governance.

He further denied that the ruling party had no policy or directive authorising the destruction of opposition campaign materials, stressing that political competition must be conducted within the confines of democratic principles and the rule of law.

“It is not possible for a ruling government to have a policy of destruction, whether it is the destruction of posters, billboards or the commission of violence against the opposition. No,” he declared.

He categorically stated that the APC in Ebonyi State did not support acts of violence, lawlessness or extrajudicial conduct, adding that the party would pursue its political engagements through legitimate and issue-based campaigns.

“APC in Ebonyi State does not support acts of violence. It does not support lawlessness. It does not support actions that are extrajudicial,” Onwe said.

He said that the party would concentrate on showcasing the achievements of the Governor Francis Nwifuru-led administration rather than engaging in activities capable of undermining the democratic rights of opposition parties.

“APC in Ebonyi State will campaign with integrity, with honour, and will only project the positive achievements of the APC government in Ebonyi State. No more, no less,” he added.

The campaign director advised individuals and political parties who felt aggrieved by the alleged removal or destruction of their campaign materials to seek redress through the appropriate security agencies rather than resorting to self-help.

“I would advise those who feel aggrieved in any shape, in any way, in any form, to take the matter to the police,” he stated.

Onwe also assured that neither the state government, the APC State Working Committee nor any party official would shield individuals found to have engaged in unlawful conduct, irrespective of their political affiliations.

World.title: Soyinka, Others Task PR Professionals on Rebuilding Public Trust
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

* At WPRF, Nobel Laureate stresses strategic role of communication in strengthening institutions, democracy

* Dandaura cites survey showing only 46% of Africans trust their presidents

* Okonkwo warns irresponsible communication can cost lives, cites Rwanda genocide

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

Nobel Laureate, Professor Wole Soyinka, on Thursday challenged public relations professionals to embrace greater responsibility in shaping public perceptions, rebuilding confidence in institutions and strengthening relationships across society.

He warned against the dangers of irresponsible communication amid technological disruption and growing demands for transparency and accountability.

Soyinka, whose goodwill message was read at the Africa Day activities of the 13th World Public Relations Forum (WPRF) 2026 in Abuja, said public relations had assumed a strategic role in determining the credibility and survival of democratic institutions, organisations and societies.

The literary icon, who won the 1986 Nobel Prize in Literature, said the international gathering provided an important opportunity to reaffirm the relevance of public relations in shaping perceptions, building trust, strengthening institutions and fostering meaningful relationships.

He noted that the profession carried an even greater responsibility at a time when technological advancements were transforming communication and increasing public expectations for transparency and accountability.

Soyinka commended the Global Alliance for Public Relations and Communication Management, the African Public Relations Association (APRA), the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR) and other partners for bringing the international conversation to Africa.

He expressed optimism that the deliberations would strengthen professional collaboration and advance the relevance of public relations globally.

The forum brought together communication experts, policymakers and industry leaders to examine the challenges of misinformation, declining institutional credibility and the responsibility of communication professionals in strengthening democracy and Africa’s position in global affairs.

Speaking at the event, NIPR Vice-President, Prof. Emmanuel Dandaura, described Africa’s declining public confidence in political leadership and public institutions as a fundamental crisis of trust that required urgent attention from communication professionals.

Citing an Afrobarometer survey conducted across 39 African countries, Dandaura disclosed that only 46 per cent of respondents expressed trust in their presidents, while confidence in national parliaments stood at 37 per cent.

He described the findings as a wake-up call, arguing that public relations practitioners must move beyond the conventional responsibility of disseminating information to helping institutions establish credibility and sustain public confidence.

According to him, four major initiatives emerged from the Abuja forum: Nigeria’s proposed definition of public relations, the Abuja Declaration on Responsible Communication, an evaluation framework for measuring its implementation and an African communication framework.

He, however, cautioned that the success of the initiatives would depend not on their presentation at the forum but on their practical implementation.

“The Abuja Declaration should not be regarded as an achievement merely because it has been presented. Its real value will be determined by the extent to which its principles translate into measurable action and professional conduct,” he said.

Dandaura urged communication professionals across Africa to support the domestication of the proposed framework, encourage cross-border collaboration and strengthen ethical standards within the profession.

Also speaking, APRA President, Mr. Arik Karani, called for a more effective response to misinformation, stressing that communication practitioners must combine speed with accuracy, particularly in the rapidly evolving digital environment.

“Speed is essential, but accuracy matters more than any other thing in the digital era that we live with,” he said.

Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of United Nigeria Airlines, Prof. Obiora Okonkwo, warned that irresponsible communication could undermine democratic stability, threaten public health and, in extreme circumstances, cost human lives.

Citing the 1994 Rwandan genocide, he recalled how a radio station, Radio Télévision Libre des Mille Collines (RTLM), became an instrument for propagating ethnic hatred and inciting violence.

“The lesson is clear: communication is not always an innocent exercise. In the hands of irresponsible actors, the microphone can become as destructive as a very dangerous weapon,” he warned.

Okonkwo also referenced Nigeria’s 2023 general election and the misinformation that characterised the COVID-19 pandemic as examples of how unverified information could deepen divisions, undermine public confidence and encourage dangerous behaviour.

Drawing from his experience in the aviation industry, he maintained that transparency and truthfulness remained the most sustainable foundations of corporate reputation.

“Truthfulness is not the enemy of reputation management. It is its most sustainable foundation,” he declared.

He advocated stronger professional self-regulation, information literacy and media literacy, warning that artificial intelligence had made it increasingly easy to produce convincing fabricated images, videos and voices capable of misleading unsuspecting members of the public.

In his contribution, Director-General of the National Orientation Agency (NOA), Lanre Issa-Onilu, called for a fundamental change in national character, arguing that communication professionals could not successfully promote an institution or country whose actual conduct contradicted the image being projected.

He questioned the rationale behind marketing Nigeria as an attractive investment destination when prospective investors continued to encounter unnecessary bureaucratic bottlenecks.

He also challenged the country’s ability to promote national unity while discrimination, prejudice and other divisive tendencies persisted.

Issa-Onilu identified the Nigerian National Ethics Policy and National Value Charter as critical instruments for sustainable national development, arguing that institutional and economic reforms would achieve limited results without corresponding improvements in citizens’ values and conduct.

“Policies do not implement themselves. People implement them, and their values influence the results,” he said.

The NOA director-general stressed that national character could not be transformed through occasional appeals and public campaigns but through consistent demonstration of ethical values in everyday conduct.

He urged stakeholders, particularly communication professionals, to make responsible communication and ethical behaviour integral to Nigeria’s national development agenda.

World.title: Tinubu Okays Plan By World’s Lagest Bus Manufacturer, Yutong, To Establish CNG Assembly Plant In Nigeria
World.content:
Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google 

.Global firm to supply initial 300 CNG-powered buses with first 100 arriving Lagos by Dec

Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has welcomed plans by the world’s largest bus manufacturer and a global leader in electric and CNG-powered buses, Yutong, to establish a CNG bus assembly plant in Nigeria, following his invitation to the Chinese automotive giant to support the expansion of affordable mass transportation across the country.



Presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, in a release issued on Thursday, stated that

the investment will support the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme (NACTP) in collaboration with State Governments, which targets transport fare reductions of approximately 40 per cent on participating routes, in line with the President’s Renewed Hope Agenda 2.0 for 2027–2031.

Under the agreement, which is scheduled to be signed in Lagos on Thursday, November 19, 2026, with the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles (Pi-CNG & EV), Yutong will supply an initial 300 CNG-powered buses, with the first 100 expected to arrive in Lagos by the end of December, 2026.



Subsequent buses will be assembled in Nigeria through YP Automobiles Bus Assembly at the former Leyland Automotive plant in Ibadan, Oyo State, reviving local industrial capacity, reducing dependence on imported vehicles and creating employment opportunities for Nigerian engineers, technicians and other workers.



Yutong, which sold 49,518 buses globally in 2025, brings extensive experience in mass transit manufacturing, with operations across international markets and a track record of supporting local assembly and public transportation projects in several countries.



The President noted that the investment comes as CNG adoption continues to increase nationwide, supported by the expansion of refuelling infrastructure through Pi-CNG & EV, the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF) and private sector investors.



These interventions include deploying Mobile Refuelling Units (MRUs) and the President’s directive for 2,000 additional CNG refuelling infrastructure units nationwide, laying the foundation for a wider rollout of affordable commercial buses.



Tinubu emphasised that reducing the daily cost of transportation for Nigerians remains the central objective of these investments.



He noted that millions of Nigerians depend on commercial transportation to get to work, take their children to school, travel to markets and move goods between communities. For many households, transportation consumes a significant portion of their daily earnings.



The President stressed that the lower operating costs of CNG-powered vehicles must translate into lower fares for passengers, allowing workers, traders and families to retain more of their income for food, education and other essential needs.



He pointed to the approximately 40 per cent fare-reduction target under the NACTP, as outlined in his Renewed Hope Agenda 2.0, and reiterates his administration’s determination to work with state governments and transport operators to extend affordable CNG transportation to more routes nationwide.



He welcomed Yutong’s decision to establish local assembly capacity in Nigeria, noting that the investment will help sustain the supply of affordable commercial buses while facilitating technology transfer, creating skilled employment and strengthening the country’s automotive industry.



Tinubu reiterated that the success of the CNG programme must ultimately be measured by how much Nigerians save on transportation, and assures citizens of his administration’s continued commitment to reducing living costs through practical investments in infrastructure, manufacturing and affordable mass transit.

World.title: Rachel Kolisi: ‘Met the love of my life’
World.content:
Rachel Kolisi is in London to promote her Falling Forward project. Images via IG

Rachel Kolisi has set tongues wagging with a social media post about meeting he “love of my life”. The former Springbok WAG and ex-wife of Siya Kolisi is currently in London to promote her book, Falling Forward.

In 2024, Rachel and Siya shared news of their shock marriage split.

Since then, the rugby player has been linked to 25-year-old influencer Rachel John



RACHEL KOLISI SPARKS RUMOURS WITH LATEST POST

On her social media platforms, Rachel Kolisi posted a picture of her enjoying a night out in London.

“Met the love of my life on the underground yesterday”, she captioned the post.

Rachel’s mention of finding love again set tongues wagging in the comments section.

Dozens of followers were convinced Rachel had moved on from her e-husband, Siya Kolisi…

“Only the right person can give you this glow. Love it for you”

“Lucky guy!”



Others were convinced that Rachel was referring to something and not someone…

“She fetched her printed books, which are literally a physical reminder of who she is underneath it all…..she’s reminding herself she is her own love of her life”

“She met herself. She found Rachel”.

Rachel Kolisi is currently in London as part of her international Falling Forward project.

She is booked for a book signing and to host a screening of her personal documentary, followed by a live Q&A session about resilience, faith, motherhood, and rebuilding her life after her high-profile divorce.

NO PLANS TO MOVE ON, YET

Rachel Kolisi has revealed that she has no plans to find love again just yet.

Speaking in an interview on 947 in March, the mom of two said: “I find it so interesting that that’s what’s considered moving on. I’m good by myself. I don’t think I’ve ever been better by myself.”

Rachel has also repeatedly shared that she would not be dropping her last name.

Speaking at a recent book event, Rachel Kolisi responded to a question about why she chose to keep her marital surname, despite her divorce.

She mentioned a time when she was approached by a woman in a supermarket who called her “Siya Kolis’s wife”.

She said of the encounter: “‘I was like ‘Nope’. Then I stopped and said ‘My name is Rachel, it’s nice to meet you’”.

Rachel reflected on why she did not revert to her maiden name, which is Smith.

She continued: “What is really important for me is to create stability for my children in two years, after they have moved five times, three times in schools and twice overseas. It was the most unstable, insane years of their lives, plus their parents got divorced on top of that.

“Stability not just for my children, but for myself and for the people around me. Was a surname change desperately needed at the time? No. Will I do it eventually? I don’t know. Why is the public so intrigued about this? I have no idea. But for now, I’m Rachel Kolisi, and I’m very proud to be Rachel Kolisi”.

World.title: Love Is Blind SA’s ‘messy’ male cast make international headlines
World.content:
Love Is Blind SA's male cast have made headlines around the world, weeks before its premiere. Images via IG

The male cast of Love Is Blind South Africa have made headlines abroad after Netflix posted, and then deleted, their images – twice!

Interestingly, the men’s job titles also changed overnight.

The dating reality TV show is hosted by married couple Dineo Langa and Solo Langa, and will premiere with its first 6 episodes on Friday, 4 November.



The show brings together 27 singles – 14 women and 13 men – aged between 24 and 3, who will find love behind a wall.

LOVE IS BLIND SOUTH AFRICA’S MALE CAST MAKE INTERNATIONAL HEADLINES

On social media, Netflix’s decision to post and delete images of the male cast members on Love Is Blind SA’s debut season has become a trending topic.

Many South Africans commented on the supposed disparity in appearances and career choices between the men and women cast members.



Others dug up the dirt on a few individuals.

US reality TV podcaster, Rikki Wise, of Storytime with Rikki, picked up on Netflix’s faux pas, adding: “It’s crazy that they changed all these people’s photos and job titles and thought we wouldn’t notice…I cannot believe they did this”.

Rikki expressed her concern that “None of these men has real jobs… it just means unemployed!”



She added: “The women are scientists and attorneys and doctors, and this is what you gave them? This is a sh*tshow. Get it together!”

Fellow US podcaster, Jessie Woo, commented under a Love Is Blind SA post: “Why did y’all delete this the first time?”.



UK reality TV podcaster, Anthony Gilet, agreed, adding that Netflix was “messy” over the move.

Referring to rumours about the cast’s questioning paths, he added in an IG post: “We’re talking secret baby mamas, drowning in debt, down-low estcourt trade!”

WHEN DOES FIRST SEASON PREMIERE?

Love Is Blind SA, which follows the US franchise, will air its first six episodes on Friday, 4 December.

Episodes 7 and 8 will air on 11 December, with the grand finale taking place on 18 December.

South Africa has adapted several popular international TV dating shows for local audiences. These also include Netflix’s The Ultimatum: South Africa, and Love Never Lies: South Africa. Other local adaptations include Love Island South Africa and Married at First Sight: Mzansi.

World.title: ‘Weddings and funerals to eat’: Pensioner’s grim survival plan has South Africans talking
World.content:
Older South Africans who depend on their SASSA pension say the money no longer covers the month, and one commenter has a bleak suggestion for getting by.

The comments appeared under a post on The South African’s Facebook page, where pensioners and their families discussed how they survive on the grant.

Surviving on a pension FOR PENSIONERS

Daniel Lebatie addressed his fellow pensioners directly, and offered a plan that mixed humour with hardship.



“Hi senior citizen of SA, to survive on your monthly pension, we should go to parties, weddings, and funerals to eat at weekends; maybe just maybe we’ll survive with the little money we get,” Lebatie wrote.

His comment drew laughing and heart reactions, but it touched on a real worry for many households where the old age grant is the main income.

A shortfall that hits home

One commenter shared The South African’s earlier report on a grant shortfall. In that story, a pensioner’s money dropped from R1 300 to R633.

Stories like that one strike a nerve because many older grant recipients do not spend their pension on themselves alone. They often spend it on grandchildren, unemployed adult children and other relatives who share the same roof.

Palesa Rose Motsôane said older recipients also face judgement over how they spend the grant. “Even the elderly buy alcohol with their grants, even gambling with it. Am I wrong, or just because they are older that we are not to say anything?” she wrote.

‘Half for ministers’

Some commenters directed their anger at government rather than at recipients.



Others echoed calls made in SASSA comment threads for the government to create jobs so that grandparents do not have to support whole families on a single grant.

For now, many pensioners say they have no option but to stretch every rand until payday.
