Rep. Bennie Thompson: “While Americans were stranded in airports across the country, with many sleeping on the floor at their gates, the secretary boarded a luxury jet, flew to a college football game and visited the private suite of a company that DHS had awarded a $2.2 billion contract.”

DHS Secretary Mullin Questioned over Deaths of Immigrants in ICE Custody

Nov 19, 2026

Homeland Security Secretary Mullin also faced questions about the deaths of immigrants in ICE custody and the killing of activists at the hands of federal agents, including Renee Good and Alex Pretti. New Jersey Democratic Congressmember LaMonica McIver questioned Mullin after New Jersey this week sued DHS in federal court seeking records for a civil rights investigation. The complaint found at least three people died at the Delaney Hall ICE jail in Newark while in the custody of the for-profit prison company GEO Group.

Rep. LaMonica McIver: “Someday extremely soon, history is going to judge you for what you are doing, your collaboration with Stephen Miller, all of these deaths. Do you have any regrets or reservations for the leading role you are playing in this administration’s immigration agenda?”

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin: “I’ll never apologize about enforcing our nation’s laws.”

Rep. LaMonica McIver: “Not about even killing people?”

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin: “We’re not killing people.”

Rep. LaMonica McIver: “No apologies for that? That” —

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin: “We’re not killing people.”

Rep. LaMonica McIver: “You are killing people. You are killing people.”

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin: “No, ma’am. That’s your opinion.”

Rep. LaMonica McIver: “No, no, you are killing people, with” —

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin: “Have you investigated what your state penitentiary looks like?”

Rep. LaMonica McIver: “The whole entire country watches you kill people, literally.”

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin: “I got the numbers right here, what it looks like.”

Rep. LaMonica McIver: “I’m reclaiming my time. This is my time. I’m reclaiming it.”

Congressmember McIver faces what she’s calling politically motivated federal charges after she was accused of assaulting an immigration officer during a congressional oversight visit to Delaney Hall last year. She faces up to 17 years in prison.

World.title: Mexican Journalist Eduardo Flores Killed in Acapulco
World.content:
Flores, a reporter for local news website Enfoque Informativo Guerrero, was found dead on Saturday, November 14, in Acapulco, a coastal resort city in the southern Mexican state of Guerrero.(Photo: Enfoque Informativo Guerrero/Facebook)

By Committee to Protect Journalists

HAVANA TIMES – Mexican authorities must immediately, credibly and transparently investigate the killing of journalist Eduardo Flores Salado, the Committee to Protect Journalists said Wednesday.

Flores, a reporter for local news website Enfoque Informativo Guerrero, was found dead on Saturday, November 14, in Acapulco, a coastal resort city in the southern Mexican state of Guerrero.

According to a statement by the Guerrero state prosecutor’s office (FGE), published Sunday on X, the remains of Flores were found in the evening of the previous day. Authorities opened a murder investigation, but the statement did not provide any further details about the circumstances of the reporter’s death, whether his work as reporter is considered as a motive or whether the FGE has identified any possible suspects.

In an interview with Mexico City broadcaster Grupo Fórmula on November 15, Héctor Nájera, the president of Enfoque Informativo’s parent company Grupo Nájera, said that Flores had been strangled.

“The brutal killing of Eduardo Flores highlights the ongoing relentless violence against journalists in Mexico and the impunity that fuels the deadly attacks against the press that have already claimed seven victims earlier this year,” said Jan-Albert Hootsen, CPJ’s Mexico representative. “Even as the government of President Claudia Sheinbaum touts a significant drop in homicides in the country, deadly violence against the press continues unabated, as does the almost complete impunity in press killing.”

Flores, 42, was a reporter for several local outlets. He contributed for over a decade to Enfoque Informativo. He previously contributed to Novedades, a now defunct local newspaper, and Flores was also a co-founder of Prensa Rosa, a local LGBTQ+ press collective.

For Enfoque Informativo, Flores reported on local politics, crime and security, human rights and the disappearance crisis in the greater Acapulco metropolitan area, according to a statement by Grupo Nájera owner Hector Nájera the website published on its Facebook page on November 15. He most recently covered press conferences and events organized by the Acapulco municipal government.

CPJ made several phone calls to Enfoque Informativo and the Guerrero FGE for comment, but the calls were not answered.

World.title: Trump’s Secretary of War Signs Military Pact with Delcy in Caracas
World.content:
Pete Hegseth: “January 3rd Was the Day of Venezuela’s Liberation”

US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth speaks at a press conference this Wednesday November 18 at the US Embassy in Caracas, Venezuela. Photo: EFE/ Miguel Gutierrez

Trump’s Secretary of War said Venezuela has gone from being “the most aggressive regional threat” to a cooperative partner.

By Efecto Cocuyo

HAVANA TIMES – US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth signed a military cooperation agreement on Wednesday, November 18, with the interim administration of Delcy Rodríguez during a previously unannounced visit to Miraflores Palace in Caracas. The meeting marks the highest-level visit by an official of Donald Trump’s administration to the country since the US military operation on January 3, which culminated in the capture of Nicolas Maduro.

According to reports from state media, Hegseth was received with honors after landing at Maiquetía Airport and holding meetings at the presidential palace with Defense Minister Gustavo Gonzalez Lopez and Foreign Minister Oliver Blanco.

A New Alliance and Historical References

In remarks broadcast on Venezuelan state television, the Pentagon chief said the two countries were resuming a defense alliance after more than two decades of interruption under the government of Hugo Chavez. According to Hegseth, the central objective of the agreement is to “ensure that the Venezuelan people are not threatened by foreign actors, narco-terrorists, or criminals, and that they are safe and protected within their sovereign borders.”

“We are signing a military alliance again after many years. We have the opportunity to fight terrorism and criminals who affect both countries,” the US official said. Hegseth also stated that they hope to “deepen our defense cooperation and partnership in ways that draw on the experience of the United States Armed Forces.”

During his remarks, Hegseth invoked the Monroe Doctrine and bilateral cooperation during World War II — including the joint protection of oil refineries against German submarines — describing them as precedents for “the natural military and strategic partnership between Venezuelans and US Americans.”

January 3rd and the Liberation

The visit comes more than ten months after the events of January 3, 2026. Following the official ceremonies at Miraflores, Hegseth spoke to reporters at the US Embassy in Caracas, where he emphasized the Trump administration’s three-phase plan for Venezuela and the renewed military agreement.

Hegseth said his country had resolved “a 27-year problem for the hemisphere” in Venezuela.

“Venezuela is better today than it was yesterday, and it will be better tomorrow than it is today,” he stated. He also described January 3 as “a day of liberation for Venezuela.”

Hegseth asserted Wednesday that, less than a year after the capture of Nicolas Maduro, Venezuela had gone from being “the most aggressive regional threat” to becoming “a cooperative security partner.”

“Venezuela has gone from being our most aggressive regional threat to becoming a cooperative security partner. In the process of rebuilding its Armed Forces alongside the United States, we are reestablishing our military alliance, which is natural and historic,” he said.

“All of this is thanks to close cooperation with President Delcy Rodriguez to stabilize Venezuela and rid it, once and for all, of narco-terrorists,” Hegseth continued.

He noted that the Department of War had brought Maduro and his wife, Cilia Flores, before the US justice system, which “put an end to the war that narco-terrorists had waged in Venezuela for decades against the US American and Venezuelan peoples.”

“We achieved this through the most sophisticated military operation in Latin American history, without a single United States casualty. The operation lasted just 48 minutes,” he said.

The result, he asserted, was “peace achieved through strength, by bringing narco-terrorists to justice and opening a new chapter for the United States, for Venezuela, for the Venezuelan Armed Forces, and for the entire Western Hemisphere.”

Hegseth said he was aware of the significance of the moment and noted that he was the first Secretary of War this century to set foot on Venezuelan soil.

“Just a year ago, my presence here, our presence here, would have been practically unimaginable. But this was possible for one simple reason: President Donald Trump had the courage to do what no previous president was willing to do: defend the United States through actions, not just words,” he said.

Interim Government Accepts the Agreement

For her part, Delcy Rodriguez expressed her administration’s interest in expanding training programs, equipment supplies, and access to new technologies for the Bolivarian National Armed Forces under the agreement.

The stop in Caracas is part of a regional tour by the US secretary, who is expected to continue on to Colombia — where he will deliver C-130 Hercules military transport aircraft — as well as Ecuador and possibly Honduras.

First published in Spanish by Efecto Cocuyo and translated and posted in English by Havana Times.

World.title: A Letter from Havana Times
World.content:
18 years, seven days a week, from Cuba despite everything

Photo por Nester Nuñez

By Circles Robinson

Dear Readers,

In October we reached our 18th anniversary of nonstop daily reporting, commentary, diaries, and photography centered on Cuba, while also covering Nicaragua, Venezuela, and other Latin American countries.

Most of our contributing writers and photographers are in Cuba, documenting the extraordinarily difficult times they are living through. From Pinar del Río, Havana, Mayabeque, Matanzas, Camagüey, and Holguín they tell us of their days spent juggling scarcities of every kind. Yet these talented writers choose to take the time to be part of this online media project. In the coming weeks, some of them will tell you in their own words why.

The Havana Times family also includes others who help make the publication possible with their writing, editing, and technical support from Venezuela, Panama, Nicaragua, Brazil, Chile, Canada, Switzerland, Spain, and the United States.

We are not a large publication, with no salaried staff, but the reader survey we conducted in May, in which many of you participated, showed us that you have a high regard for the credibility of our work. That means a great deal to us. The results also told us that most of you feel Havana Times gives you a good picture of life on the ground in Cuba and a better understanding of the complexities of the country’s politics and the challenges it faces. That is exactly what our combined effort sets out to do.

I continue editing and publishing Havana Times out of a personal commitment to our writers and photographers as well as a love for both Cuba and Nicaragua, where I lived for many years. In this increasingly polarized world, I remain committed to a kind of journalism that emphasizes empathy and ethics while avoiding extremism.

I’m also happy to know that people from different countries who read Havana Times before traveling to Cuba have written to us after returning home to say the publication gave them an introduction to the country; this helped them better understand what they encountered and, thus, get more out of their trip. Many continue reading afterwards. Knowing that our work can serve readers in this way is deeply gratifying.

Our hope is to continue providing this service in the coming year and beyond. Later this month, we will launch our all-important annual reader fundraising campaign. If you also believe in the importance of independent journalism and care about the people and countries we cover, I hope to have your support.

World.title: Financing an Apartment in Brazil
World.content:
A condominium in Curitiba, Brazil

By Osmel Almaguer

HAVANA TIMES – I have a Cuban friend who managed to finance a place of his own through Brazil’s Minha Casa Minha Vida [“My house, my life”] Program. I remember writing about that while trying to explain the different ways an immigrant can purchase a property.

That was a more or less a year ago. My friend’s success inspired me to try it as well. He’s in the middle of his financing, which ends in 2028, and I just received an email offering us our own financing.

That doesn’t mean it’s going to work out. We’ve agreed to move forward with the process and learn more about the proposal, and now we’re waiting for a response from the real estate agency, to find out if there are any available units based on our ranking.

If the answer is yes, we’ll begin a series of in-person meetings with the real estate agency to work out the details before signing the contract.

First, they’d give us a full presentation of the project, including the projected construction timeline. After that, we’d discuss the contract details and payment terms.

We don’t yet know the total price of the apartment, but we do know that the condominium project is located in the Cajuru neighborhood, just a few minutes from downtown. I did some research, and it’s a residential area with excellent prospects for continued growth, so from a financial standpoint, it could be a good investment.

I’ve already mentioned that I firmly believe in this approach to managing our finances because, after all, if we spend our whole lives moving from one rental to another, we’ll never own a home of our own – but will still end up paying hundreds of thousands of Brazilian riais [note: 5.87 riais = $1 US].

Just to give an example, in the four years I’ve been in Brazil, I’ve already spent about 60,000 reais (approximately $12,000) on rent, which is equivalent to one-fifth of the value of a small apartment.

Minha Casa Minha Vida is a government program that subsidizes affordable housing for low-income families. Through this program, in combination with another program called Casa Curitibana, we could receive a subsidy of up to 30,000 reais ($6,000) to cover part of the down payment, with the remainder divided into monthly installments until the condo is completed.

A project of this kind raises several concerns. For example, having to pay the monthly loan installments alongside our current rent for two or three years. Construction interest accrues over the waiting period, causing the monthly down payment installments to rise from an initial 600 reais ($120) to as much as 2,000 reais ($400).

The size of the apartment is also a bit discouraging—only 34 square meters.

As an asylum seeker, I don’t have legal status that would allow me to finance an apartment; however, a driver’s license serves as legal identification, and it is possible to obtain one easily by paying between 1,500 and 2,000 reais (between $300 and $400).

For a family that lives paycheck to paycheck, all these expenses—even though they’re only possible thanks to programs like Minha Casa Minha Vida—mean it’s important to carefully calculate and manage every decision, because even the slightest slip-up could leave us in a bind.

Read more from the diary of Osmel Almaguer here on Havana Times.

World.title: Trump, Putin and Xi hold their first three-way summit, rich in symbolism but short on announcements
World.content:
Trump, Putin and Xi hold their first three-way summit, rich in symbolism but short on announcements

19th Thursday, November 2026 - 18:38 UTC Full article

Putin, Xi and Trump arrive together for their first trilateral summit on Thursday in Shenzhen.

US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping held the first three-way meeting between the leaders of the three powers in Shenzhen on Thursday, an encounter rich in symbolism that ended with a commitment to dialogue on reducing nuclear risks but no concrete measures.

US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping held the first three-way meeting between the leaders of the three powers in Shenzhen on Thursday, an encounter rich in symbolism that ended with a commitment to dialogue on reducing nuclear risks but no concrete measures.

“We are truly making history,” Trump said during the nearly hour-and-a-half meeting, held on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. “The United States, Russia and China are uniquely positioned to discuss how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons on Earth and also to lower the risk of those weapons being used,” he added. “Everything possible must be done to prevent a nuclear war,” Xi said, adding that “the seeds sown at today's trilateral meeting will surely take root”. Putin recalled that the three countries were “the victors of World War II” and share “responsibility for maintaining international peace and security”.

According to the declaration issued after the meeting, the three leaders committed to “engage in dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing nuclear proliferation”, and agreed to increase production and supply of refined petroleum products. The text also states that “the International Criminal Court and other similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction”, upholds respect for the immunity of state officials and calls for reform of the United Nations. The International Criminal Court has an outstanding arrest warrant for Putin.

The New START treaty, which limited the US and Russian nuclear arsenals, expired in February 2026. Trump has proposed replacing it with an agreement that includes China, which in turn demands that Washington and Moscow first reduce their arsenals. “We need more than diplomatic theatre and photo opportunities,” Daryl Kimball, executive director of the Arms Control Association, told AP.

The summit marked a new step in Putin's return to the international stage. Trump, who had not met him since their Alaska summit in August 2025, called him a “friend”. “God protect us from friends like that,” Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk responded on X. European governments and Ukraine had feared the three leaders would discuss the country's future without Kyiv at the table.

Trump and Xi will meet again at the G20 summit on December 14 and 15 at the Trump National Doral resort in Florida. Putin has not decided whether he will attend. “I will think about it. We will see,” he said.

World.title: UK Parliament briefing details London's response to Argentina's offensive against Sea Lion
World.content:
UK Parliament briefing details London's response to Argentina's offensive against Sea Lion

19th Thursday, November 2026 - 18:35 UTC Full article

Flags of Britain's Overseas Territories fly near the Houses of Parliament in Westminster, London.

The House of Commons Library has published a research briefing setting out the response of Andy Burnham's government to Argentina's legal, economic and diplomatic offensive against the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falklands, nine days before the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea decides whether to order a halt.

The House of Commons Library has published a research briefing setting out the response of Andy Burnham's government to Argentina's legal, economic and diplomatic offensive against the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falklands, nine days before the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea decides whether to order a halt.

The document, prepared by researchers Patrick Butchard, John Curtis and Philip Loft, is not a government statement but an analysis intended to inform lawmakers, Infobae reported. It reviews four fronts of Argentina's offensive this year: the reaffirmation of sovereignty at the UN General Assembly, sanctions against some 60 individuals and companies linked to exploration, the revival of construction at the Ushuaia naval base, and the case before the Hamburg tribunal. “The UK government has said it will contest the legal case and introduce protections for businesses operating” in the islands, it summarises.

Those responses include the business guidance published in September by Overseas Territories Minister Uma Kumaran, which states that the islanders “have the right to develop their natural resources as they see fit”, with the government's “full support” for companies. In October, London announced measures under its Protection of Trading Interests legislation so that British companies “can continue to make commercial decisions in accordance with UK law” despite Argentine sanctions.

The briefing devotes a section to the United States. It recalls that Donald Trump said in August his administration was reviewing its traditional neutrality on sovereignty over the islands, and that Burnham subsequently raised with him “the economic consequences of Argentina's coercive measures for the UK and the US”. Citing Argentine media, it says Washington's concern over possible sanctions on US companies may have led Buenos Aires to slow down its sovereignty defence bill.

That bill suffered a fresh setback on Wednesday: the Chamber of Deputies session called to debate it collapsed for lack of quorum, with 126 deputies present, three short of the 129 needed, after the Provincias Unidas and MID blocs refused to take their seats over objections to the articles on foreign interference and freedom of expression.

Argentine Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno defended the legal route the same day. “This arbitration focuses on the exploitation of natural resources while the underlying issue has not been decided,” he told a legal forum in Buenos Aires. “Once a drop of oil is extracted, that drop cannot be recovered.” Quirno said that, whatever the decision on November 28, “the arbitration continues”.

Sea Lion, operated by Britain's Rockhopper Exploration and Israel's Navitas Petroleum about 220 kilometres north of the islands, has estimated reserves of 1.7 billion barrels and is expected to begin drilling in January 2027.

World.title: Ueno Bank collapse claims Paraguay’s attorney general and the head of Itaipú
World.content:
Ueno Bank collapse claims Paraguay’s attorney general and the head of Itaipú

19th Thursday, November 2026 - 18:27 UTC Full article

In the case against the businessmen, ten executives of the Vázquez Group, which owned Ueno, are in custody

Paraguay’s Attorney General Emiliano Rolón resigned on Tuesday in the face of imminent impeachment, and the Paraguayan director of the binational Itaipú dam, Justo Zacarías Irún, was dismissed on Wednesday, in the latest wave of departures triggered by the collapse of Ueno Bank. At least a dozen senior officials have left their posts since the bank was taken over on November 3, among them President Santiago Peña, who was removed from office and is in prison.

Rolón submitted his resignation to President Pedro Alliana after the Chamber of Deputies opened impeachment proceedings against him for alleged misconduct in office. He had been criticised for delaying raids and stalling investigations linked to the bank and to Peña. Deputy prosecutor Alba Rocío Cantero has taken over on an interim basis.

Zacarías Irún, dismissed by Alliana along with the Paraguayan members of Itaipú’s board, is accused of depositing US$163.8 million of the entity’s funds in Ueno Bank in breach of internal rules. The dam, shared with Brazil, is one of the Paraguayan state’s largest sources of revenue.

Peña, charged with breach of trust, self-serving administration and now also criminal association, was moved to a barracks on the outskirts of Asunción, to an ordinary room, after it emerged that at the Presidential Escort Regiment he had occupied a luxury room with a gym. Alliana dismissed the unit’s commander, José David Daiub Fatecha. Prosecutors also raided the homes of the former president’s brothers and seized documents on a company set up in Luxembourg in 2024.

The list of departures includes former Central Bank president Carlos Carvallo, in pre-trial detention; his interim successor, Liana Caballero Krause, who lasted a week in the post and is in custody; the Superintendent of Banks, Holger Insfrán, charged with breach of trust; and Interior Minister Enrique Riera. Opposition lawmakers are also demanding the departure of Comptroller General Camilo Benítez for failing to flag the irregularities.

The string of removals is unsettling the ruling Colorado Party. “Where does this end? And where do we begin a process of institutional reconstruction?” asked the speaker of the Chamber of Deputies, Raúl Latorre, who called for dialogue with the opposition ahead of the 2028 general election.

In the case against the businessmen, ten executives of the Vázquez Group, which owned Ueno, are in custody, among them chief executive Federico Miguel Vázquez and the bank’s president, Juan Manuel Gustale. Prosecutors have seized 27 vehicles, including several Rolls-Royces and a Lamborghini, three aircraft and a yacht.

World.title: IMF warns global debt will soon reach 100% of GDP, the highest since World War II
World.content:
IMF warns global debt will soon reach 100% of GDP, the highest since World War II

19th Thursday, November 2026 - 03:51 UTC Full article

“The level of global debt will soon reach 100% of GDP, the highest since World War II. This requires urgent attention,” Georgieva said

International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva warned on Thursday that global public debt will soon reach 100% of world gross domestic product, the highest level since World War II, and called for “urgent attention” to government finances.

International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva warned on Thursday that global public debt will soon reach 100% of world gross domestic product, the highest level since World War II, and called for “urgent attention” to government finances.

“The level of global debt will soon reach 100% of GDP, the highest since World War II. This requires urgent attention,” Georgieva said at the plenary session of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders' summit in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.

The warning comes amid a rebound in global inflation, which the IMF chief attributed both to the energy crisis caused by the war in the Middle East and to rising technology demand linked to the construction of artificial intelligence infrastructure. That rebound, she said, has led to tighter monetary policy through interest rate rises in many countries, making debt more expensive to service.

In the same speech, Georgieva highlighted that 2026 has been the first year in which artificial intelligence has had a tangible impact on global growth, and called on countries to prepare quickly for the changes it will bring.

World.title: IMF’s Georgieva at APEC: countries must “quickly prepare” for artificial intelligence
World.content:
IMF’s Georgieva at APEC: countries must “quickly prepare” for artificial intelligence

19th Thursday, November 2026 - 03:36 UTC Full article

“We are facing the fastest transformation in the history of humanity,” the Bulgarian economist said

International Monetary Fund (IMF) Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva on Thursday urged countries to “quickly prepare” their digital infrastructure, labour markets and workers for the rise of artificial intelligence, speaking at the plenary session of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders’ summit in the Chinese city of Shenzhen.

“We are facing the fastest transformation in the history of humanity,” the Bulgarian economist said. “Countries must quickly prepare their digital infrastructure, their labour markets and their workers for AI, and prevent risks, especially in ensuring financial stability and cybersecurity,” she added.

According to Georgieva, 2026 has been “the first year in which AI has had a tangible impact on global growth”, acting as a counterweight to the effect of the war in the Middle East on energy supplies. “While the energy crisis will eventually dissipate, AI is here to stay. It will be the most significant factor for competitiveness, productivity and growth in the medium term,” she said.

Artificial intelligence is among the priorities of the agenda promoted by China at the summit, alongside the defence of free trade and regional connectivity. The Shenzhen meeting culminates on Thursday with the first three-way encounter between the presidents of China, the United States and Russia.

World.title: US and Venezuela restore military cooperation with Hegseth’s surprise visit
World.content:
US and Venezuela restore military cooperation with Hegseth’s surprise visit

19th Thursday, November 2026 - 03:26 UTC Full article

Hegseth met acting President Delcy Rodríguez at the Miraflores Palace and signed the agreement with Venezuelan Defence Minister Gustavo González López

US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth signed a military cooperation agreement with Venezuela in Caracas on Wednesday during an unannounced visit, the first by a Pentagon chief since the January 3 US military operation that removed Nicolás Maduro from power. The agreement restores cooperation that Hugo Chávez broke off in 2005.

Hegseth met acting President Delcy Rodríguez at the Miraflores Palace and signed the agreement with Venezuelan Defence Minister Gustavo González López. He said it includes joint training, strategic cooperation, intelligence sharing and the supply of defence equipment and capabilities, so that the Venezuelan people are “not threatened by foreign actors, narco-terrorists or criminals”. “In the process of rebuilding its armed forces alongside the United States, we are restoring our military alliance, which is natural and historic,” he said.

At a later event at the US embassy, Hegseth said Venezuela had gone from being “the most aggressive regional threat” to a “reliable partner”, and issued a warning to criminal groups: “To the narco-terrorists who have used this as a safe haven, your time is up. We will hunt you down, we will find you and we will kill you.”

Minister González López issued a statement, his first since taking office, setting limits on the agreement. The resumption of technical and military cooperation, he stressed, will be carried out in strict adherence to the Constitution and with full respect for “sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity, preserving the leadership, command and competence of the Bolivarian National Armed Forces”. The text notes that the new relations stem from the “harsh and painful events of January 3”. Rodríguez, who had just returned from a tour of Turkey, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, said Hegseth “has a great responsibility on his shoulders”.

According to El País, cooperation had already been working in practice for months. At least two operations on Venezuelan territory received US support in equipment and intelligence: a June attack on the hideout of the leader of the Tren de Aragua gang in Bolívar state and the drone destruction of a National Liberation Army (ELN) operations centre in Apure, both with doubts about the number and identity of those killed. After the June earthquakes in La Guaira and Caracas, some 2,000 US troops were deployed to help with the emergency.

In 2005 Venezuela replaced cooperation with Washington with Russia, Iran and China, which became its main arms suppliers. Hegseth continued his regional tour in Colombia and Ecuador, focused on security and the fight against drug trafficking.

World.title: Anthropic, maker of Claude, debuts on Nasdaq after the largest IPO in history
World.content:
Anthropic, maker of Claude, debuts on Nasdaq after the largest IPO in history

19th Thursday, November 2026 - 03:14 UTC Full article

Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI employees led by siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, now chief executive and president, Anthropic has focused its growth on business customers

US artificial intelligence company Anthropic, maker of the Claude assistant, begins trading on Nasdaq on Thursday after pricing its initial public offering at US$83 a share, above the expected range, in what the US financial press describes as the largest offering in history. The deal values the company at around US$1.5 trillion.

Anthropic is selling 980 million shares, up from the 825 million initially planned, raising about US$81.3 billion, according to CNBC and CNN. The company had set a range of US$70 to US$78 a share, and demand reached almost seven times the shares on offer, according to Bloomberg. On top of that comes a private placement of US$26 billion in shares to major technology companies. The offering surpasses that of SpaceX, Elon Musk’s space company, which went public in June. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are leading the deal, and the stock will trade under the ticker ANT.

Founded in 2021 by former OpenAI employees led by siblings Dario and Daniela Amodei, now chief executive and president, Anthropic has focused its growth on business customers. According to the prospectus cited by the press, its revenue rose from US$41 million in 2023 to US$386 million in 2024, US$4.6 billion in 2025 and US$16.3 billion in the first half of 2026 alone, and in the second quarter it posted its first operating profit, of US$974 million.

After the deal, Amazon and Google, which are at once suppliers, competitors and investors, will hold about 15% and 14% of the capital, respectively. The seven co-founders will retain shares giving them 50.1% of voting rights, although an independent body elects the majority of the board.

The IPO comes after weeks of sharp volatility in technology stocks, which fell heavily earlier this month, and is seen as a test of market confidence in artificial intelligence. In its prospectus, the company itself warns that the technology it develops could cause catastrophic harm, one of the risks it sets out for investors.

World.title: Xi and Putin reaffirm their alliance on the eve of the first three-way summit with Trump
World.content:
Xi and Putin reaffirm their alliance on the eve of the first three-way summit with Trump

18th Wednesday, November 2026 - 17:25 UTC Full article

Before the opening banquet, Trump and Putin greeted each other in Xi’s presence, their first encounter since the Alaska summit in August 2025.

Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin reaffirmed their strategic alliance in Shenzhen on Wednesday, hours before Xi personally greeted Donald Trump at the airport, on the eve of the first three-way meeting between the heads of state of China, Russia and the United States, to be held on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.

At their bilateral meeting, Xi described relations between the two countries as “as firm as a mountain in the face of any adversity or storm” and called for continued work towards a multipolar world order. “Coordination between Russia and China in foreign policy remains firm and produces good results. In a complex geopolitical situation, we continue to pursue constructive paths to forge a fairer multipolar world order,” Putin replied, referring to Europe’s “humiliating decline” and arguing that the sanctions imposed on Russia over the invasion of Ukraine have backfired.

Hours later, Xi went to the airport to greet Trump, an unprecedented gesture in his 14 years in power which, according to international media, had not occurred since Mao Zedong welcomed Soviet leader Nikita Khrushchev in 1959. “China is a country of courtesy with a long tradition of reciprocity,” Xi told him, according to the official Xinhua news agency, referring to the welcome Trump gave him in Washington in September. Before the opening banquet, Trump and Putin greeted each other in Xi’s presence, their first encounter since the Alaska summit in August 2025.

Opening the summit’s business forum, Xi warned that “unilateralism and protectionism are gaining strength” and called for global supply chains to be kept open. “Openness brings progress and isolation inevitably leads to backwardness,” he said.

According to China’s Foreign Ministry, Thursday’s three-way meeting will address how to “preserve world peace and promote strategic stability in relations between major powers”. Trump has said he wants to discuss reducing nuclear arsenals and, according to press reports, also the wars in Ukraine and Iran, although the White House had said Ukraine was not on the trilateral agenda. No agreements are expected.

Trade will also be on the table at the bilateral meeting between Xi and Trump. The tariff truce between the two countries expires on January 10, and China holds a dominant position in rare earths: in 2024 it mined about 60% of those used in magnets and accounted for 91% of their refining, according to the International Energy Agency. During his earlier stop in Manila, Trump promoted critical minerals agreements with Asian partners and approved arms sales to the Philippines worth more than US$5 billion.

World.title: Congress approves Animal Welfare Law, spelling out pet owners’ legal responsibilities
World.content:
Congress has approved a new General Law on Animal Welfare, Care and Protection, establishing new obligations to ensure the care and protection of pets in Mexico.

The new law recognizes animals as sentient beings and subjects of care, and establishes that abandonment, mistreatment and cruelty may lead to penalties and the requirement to make amends for the harm caused

The legislation also includes amendments to five other laws related to animal health, environmental protection, wildlife, civil protection and film production.

What are the new obligations and sanctions?

According to the bill, pet owners must provide their animals with suitable food and constant access to drinking water. Owners must also keep their pets in a clean and safe environment, protected from harsh weather.

The bill also regulates the sale of animals, which can only take place in authorized shops — not public markets or online platforms like Facebook. Sales must meet the criteria for traceability and include a mandatory veterinary inspection.

Failure to meet the new legal obligations may result in fines, administrative detention of up to 36 hours, business closures and revocation of permits, among other penalties.

What is considered animal abuse under the new law?

The law defines acts of mistreatment or cruelty as behaviors that may lead to death with prolonged suffering; killing healthy animals without a legal justification; administering harmful substances such as alcohol or drugs and performing mutilations for aesthetic purposes, such as ear and tail docking.

Other prohibited acts include tethering animals in a way that could cause them injury or strangulation; denying them access to food, water or rest; and using them as targets for attacks during the training of other animals for shows, sporting activities or security work.

Expanding on last year’s dolphin show ban, the bill also prohibits the use of wild animals in circuses, dog fighting, and the use of animals in demonstrations or television contests. It also prohibits using animals for political or commercial advertising, school festivities, or as contest prizes.

Finally, the law says that euthanasia may only be justified in cases of injury, serious or incurable illness, suffering, or other conditions that compromise the animal’s well-being.

The bill has been forwarded to the presidential office (Presidencia) for publication in Mexico’s Official Gazette (DOF) and immediate entry into force.

With reports from Grupo Animal and El Financiero

World.title: Mexican security forces dismantle 3 drug labs in Sinaloa and Michoacán
World.content:
Federal authorities dismantled three narco labs, seizing drugs and chemicals worth an estimated US $74.6 million in two separate joint operations carried out earlier this month.

In a Nov. 17 press release, the Security Cabinet said that intelligence work allowed Navy personnel — in coordination with the Security Ministry, the Attorney General’s Office (FGR) and state police officials — to identify and locate clandestine laboratories in the states of Sinaloa and Michoacán.

En #Sinaloa y #Michoacán, autoridades federales localizan e inhabilitan tres laboratorios para la elaboración de metanfetamina. https://t.co/HYVXaSot2u https://t.co/WYilOHxC0y — Secretaría de Seguridad y Protección Ciudadana (@SSPCMexico) November 17, 2026

In total, authorities seized 2.4 metric tonnes and 1,000 liters of methamphetamine, 11,630 liters of chemical precursors and 2,210 kilos of dual-use substances. No arrests were reported.

“With these actions, the institutions of the Security Cabinet weaken the capacity of criminal organizations to produce synthetic drugs by disabling facilities, chemical precursors and equipment used for their production,” the press release said.

The first operation took place in Sinaloa near the town of Tanques, in the coastal municipality of Elota, halfway between Culiacán and Mazatlán.

There, authorities found a clandestine laboratory with approximately 1,000 liters and 800 kilos of methamphetamine, 800 liters of chemical precursors, 210 kilos of dual-use substances, as well as various materials used for the production of synthetic drugs.

In a second operation in the remote village of Zirúcuaro, Michoacán, about 145 kilometers south of the state capital Morelia, two clandestine laboratories were located.

Marines seized approximately 1,600 kilos of methamphetamine, 10,830 liters of chemical precursors and nearly 2,000 kilos of dual-use substances. They also seized tanks, makeshift reactors, improvised equipment and material used for the production of synthetic drugs, as well as two vehicles.

All materials from the three laboratories were seized and turned over to the appropriate authorities, while the hardware and machinery used to manufacture synthetic drugs found at the three locations were destroyed.

These operations followed an action carried out on Nov. 6 in the municipality of Atempan, Puebla, where Navy personnel, in coordination with federal, state, and municipal authorities, dismantled another clandestine laboratory and arrested two men.

The Security Cabinet said that federal authorities have dismantled more than 2,800 clandestine labs and methamphetamine production and storage sites since President Claudia Sheinbaum took office on Oct. 1, 2024.

With reports from Milenio, El Financiero and Zeta

World.title: Misifú, the crime-fighting cat, thwarts a would-be robber in Puebla
World.content:
Streaky the Supercat now has a crime-fighting colleague in Puebla after a night-time hold-up was foiled by a heroic kitty earlier this month.

The feisty feline protected his home turf valiantly, forcing the aspiring attacker to retreat from the premises, in a manner that would have made Captain Americat proud.

The attempted robbery took place on the evening of Saturday, Nov. 7, at a family grocery store in the San Ramón neighborhood in the southern outskirts of Puebla city.

🐱🐾 ¡El michi se puso la capa de héroe! Un gatito fue parte de la defensa de una tienda durante un intento de asalto en una tienda en la primera sección de San Ramón, ubicada en la calle Bugambilias, #Puebla. Las dueñas se enfrentaron al ladrón el pasado 7 de noviembre y ahora el sujeto es buscado por las autoridades. 🚨 #Noticias #Entérate #Viral #TráficoPuebla — TraficoPuebla (@Trafico_Puebla) November 18, 2026

A man wearing a black hoodie sweatshirt and a baseball cap entered the establishment and asked the shop assistant, Lidia, for some information about an over-the-counter medication.

Shortly thereafter, he returned wearing a mask, the hood pulled up over his head, and, while menacing the attendant, threatened to use a weapon he claimed to have concealed in a backpack unless they opened the cash register.

As he approached Lidia, her daughter came rushing out from behind the counter with a weapon of her own — her kitten Misifú.

The young woman held the cat by the back of its neck and thrust it toward the thief’s face while he had yet to brandish the unidentified weapon. Misifú lashed out, its claws extended and began hissing and scratching the would-be thief on his raised hands, causing him to back away and eventually retreat from the store.

The owner of the store then emerged from behind the counter and followed the suspect out the door, after which the wannabe crook can be seen walking down the sidewalk in the video from the security cameras that captured the entire cat-astrophic incident.

Thus far, there has been no official report on the identity of the alleged purr-petrator and police are still searching for the suspect. However, since the video has been circulated widely on social media his cronies are no doubt mocking him mercilessly for being hiss-terically thwarted by a 10-pound ball of fur.

Following the incident, the victims requested increased police presence in the area to prevent further crimes that could endanger business owners and residents.

With reports from TV Azteca, Milenio and MegaNoticia

World.title: MND Local CDMX: From folklórico and Santa runs to little devils, Christmas is here
World.content:
From Christmas pageantry at Chapultepec Castle to mischievous devils in Coyoacán and hundreds of Santas racing through Santa Fe, Mexico City has plenty of festive ways to celebrate the holiday season. Whether you’re looking for traditional Mexican posadas, folkloric performances, family-friendly theater or a chance to don a Santa suit and hit the pavement, here are some seasonal events worth adding to your December calendar.

Oh, and don’t forget about the medieval Christmas fair we shared a couple of weeks ago.

Okay … Let’s get into it.

Ballet Folklórico brings Mexican Christmas traditions to Chapultepec Castle

Mexico City’s historic Chapultepec Castle will once again provide the backdrop for “Navidades en México,” a unique Christmas-themed performance by the Ballet Folklórico de México de Amalia Hernández, with seven shows scheduled in December.

The production celebrates Mexico’s Christmas traditions through folkloric dance, music and theatrical performances, exploring the blend of Indigenous and Spanish influences that shaped the country’s holiday celebrations.

According to the organizers, the show is divided into three acts. The first recreates the Annunciation and a live Nativity scene, complete with farm animals brought in especially for the performance. The second celebrates the gifts brought by the Three Wise Men through regional dances inspired by traditions from Oaxaca, Yucatán, Chihuahua and Tamaulipas, as well as Tlaxcala, Michoacán and Veracruz. The final act recreates a traditional Mexican posada, featuring folkloric dances and Christmas carols performed by a choir of more than 50 people.

The event takes place outdoors, so organizers recommend dressing warmly and arriving at least 45 minutes before the show. General admission seating is available, and late arrivals will not be permitted once the performance begins.

The production is recommended for children aged 6 and older. Chapultepec Castle, for those who don’t know, sits on top of a hill. As such, free transportation vans will be available for visitors with disabilities and older adults, while other attendees can use a paid shuttle service to reach the castle.

Dates : Dec. 17, 22, 23, 25, 26, 27 and 30. Every show begins at 7 p.m.

Location: Av. Heroico Colegio Militar 172, Bosque de Chapultepec I Secc, Miguel Hidalgo, 11580 Ciudad de México

Cost: 1,180-1,708 pesos

Tickets and additional information are available through Ticketmaster Mexico. Meanwhile, if you can’t make the show but want to see a folkloric ballet performance, check out Ballet Folklórico de México de Amalia Hernández on Instagram.

Mischievous devils and posada traditions take over Coyoacán

A traditional Mexican Christmas pastorela returns to Coyoacán for its 37th year, combining live theater, music, fireworks and an interactive celebration of the country’s holiday traditions.

“Diablos Revolucionarios: Pastorela Tradicional de Coyoacán” will run from Dec. 18–27 at the Casa de Cultura Jesús Reyes Heroles in the southern Mexico City borough. Written by Luz María Meza and directed by Jorge Sandoval, the production features a cast of more than 20 performers.

For nearly four decades, the family-friendly performance has chronicled the journey of several shepherds as they make their way to witness the birth of Jesus. There’s just one problem: A group of mischievous devils continuously try to derail their plans.

The production combines Mexican humor with live music and fireworks, culminating in a Nativity scene accompanied by performances from folkloric group D’Santos.

But the experience extends beyond the stage. Following the performance, visitors can walk through the cultural center’s gardens alongside a procession of pilgrims, singing traditional posada songs and taking part in a recreation of the customary request for lodging. The evening also includes piñata raffles and a snack of tamales and atole.

Admission includes a candle, a welcome serving of ponche and post-performance refreshments.

Unfortunately, we can’t tell you how much tickets cost, as they don’t go on sale until Nov. 20, at which point they can be purchased via Boletia or the venue’s box office.

Dates: Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays from Dec. 18-27, with two performances beginning at 6 p.m. and 8 p.m.

Location: Av. Francisco Sosa 202, Santa Catarina, Coyoacán, 04010 Ciudad de México

Tickets go on sale Nov. 20. In the meantime, though, you can learn more about the event at Cartelera de Teatro.

The Santa Run brings a sea of Santas to Mexico City’s Parque La Mexicana

Hundreds of Santa Clauses are expected to take over Mexico City’s Parque La Mexicana on Dec. 13 for The Santa Run, an annual Christmas-themed sporting event that combines running, family activities and holiday festivities.

The 2026 edition will offer three distances: a 10-kilometer race, a 5-kilometer race and a 1-kilometer walk. The event is open to participants of all ages, with children, people using wheelchairs and even furry four-legged companions welcome to join the shorter route.

There is one important requirement: participants must wear the event’s official Santa Claus costume throughout the race. The outfit, which comes with registration, includes a jacket, trousers, belt and hat. Special costumes are also available for dogs.

The 5K and 10K races will begin at 7 a.m., while the 1K walk is scheduled to start at 7:15 a.m.

In addition to the outfit, registration includes a commemorative medal, a race number, hydration along the route and access to a post-race Christmas celebration featuring a concert and prize raffle. Participants will also receive breakfast provided by Fisher’s restaurant, while part of the registration proceeds will go toward purchasing gifts for children with cancer.

Date: Sunday, Dec. 13 at 7 a.m.

Location: Av. Luis Barragán 505, Santa Fe, Contadero, Cuajimalpa de Morelos, 05348 Ciudad de México

Cost: 690-950 pesos

Registration is available through the event’s official website, The Santa Run México, or check them out on Instagram for more information.

Drew Pittock serves as Mexico News Daily’s features director. He is based in Mexico City. Have an idea for a feature story or unique event in CDMX? Send an email to drew.pittock@mexiconewsdaily.com.

World.title: Mexico in Numbers: Just how big is Mexico’s tourism economy?
World.content:
Incredible food. Beautiful beaches. Friendly people. Archeological wonders. Cool cities. Pueblos mágicos. And much, much more.

It’s no wonder that Mexico is one of the world’s most popular tourism destinations.

Mexico welcomed a record-high 47.8 million international tourists in 2025, making it the world’s sixth most-visited country.

With such a high number of international tourists, it’s no surprise that tourism is a major contributor to the Mexican economy. Holidaying Mexicans also inject large amounts of money into the economy.

So, exactly how big is Mexico’s tourism GDP? What contribution does it make to Mexico’s overall GDP? Which states are most and least dependent on tourism?

Find the answers in this “Mexico in Numbers” article!

Mexico’s tourism GDP exceeded 2.7 trillion pesos in 2024

Federal Tourism Minister Josefina Rodríguez Zamora reported last December that Mexico’s tourism GDP in 2024 was 2.71 trillion pesos, representing a year-over-year increase of 2.5% in real terms.

Based on the Bank of Mexico’s closing USD:MXN rate on Monday (18.53), that amount is equivalent to US $146.25 billion.

Rodríguez also reported that tourism’s share of Mexico’s overall GDP in 2024 was 8.7%.

Mexico leads OECD in tourism’s share of GDP

Among countries that belong to the Organization for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), Mexico ranks equal first with Iceland for tourism’s share of GDP, according to data published in the report “OECD Tourism Trends and Policies 2026.”

Published in August, the report includes data from either 2023 or 2024 for 33 OECD countries.

In Mexico and Iceland, tourism contributed to 8.7% of GDP.

The only other OECD country where tourism contributed more than 8% of GDP was Portugal.

What are Mexico’s most and least tourism-dependent states?

According to federal Tourism Ministry (Sectur) data, the Caribbean coast state of Quintana Roo — home to tourism destinations such as Cancún, Playa del Carmen, Tulum and Cozumel — is easily Mexico’s most tourism-dependent state.

Data published by Sectur in a 2024 report shows that tourism-related activities generated 49.2% of Quintana Roo’s GDP in 2022.

Baja California Sur and Yucatán had the next-highest shares, with tourism accounting for 17.3% and 16.1% of their GDP, respectively. The former state’s tourism destinations include Los Cabos and La Paz, while among the latter’s are Mérida and the ancient Maya city of Chichén Itzá.

Campeche had the smallest tourism share of any state economy in 2022, with tourism accounting for just 2.8% of its GDP. The Gulf coast state’s economy is heavily dependent on offshore oil production, although it does have two UNESCO World Heritage sites: the “Historic Fortified Town of Campeche” and the “Ancient Maya City and Protected Tropical Forests of Calakmul.”

After Campeche, Coahuila and Durango had the smallest tourism shares of state GDP in 2022, at 3% and 3.2%, respectively. The graph below shows data for all of Mexico’s 32 federal entities.

By Mexico News Daily chief staff writer Peter Davies (peter.davies@mexiconewsdaily.com)

World.title: Interior minister praises Sheinbaum’s composure and confidence in China: Thursday’s mañanera recapped
World.content:
Listen to this article

Sheinbaum’s mañanera in 60 seconds

🎤 Sheinbaum concludes APEC participation, Rodríguez gives overview of China trip: Interior Minister Rosa Icela Rodríguez, who is leading the mañanera press conferences in Sheinbaum’s absence, said the president had concluded her participation in the 33rd APEC Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen and would arrive in Mexico City late Thursday or early Friday.

Interior Minister Rosa Icela Rodríguez, who is leading the mañanera press conferences in Sheinbaum’s absence, said the president had concluded her participation in the 33rd APEC Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen and would arrive in Mexico City late Thursday or early Friday. 🇲🇽 🇦🇺 Sheinbaum meets Australian prime minister: Rodríguez said the president held a bilateral meeting on Thursday with Anthony Albanese that “will help strengthen trade relations [and] promote investment.”

Rodríguez said the president held a bilateral meeting on Thursday with Anthony Albanese that “will help strengthen trade relations [and] promote investment.” 👏 Rodríguez praises Sheinbaum’s “composure”: She said the president handled herself with “composure” and “firmness, without confrontation or subservience.”

She said the president handled herself with “composure” and “firmness, without confrontation or subservience.” 🚨 Rodríguez: Mexico will keep arresting people smugglers: Responding to U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin’s comments on migrant caravans, she said Mexico “will continue detaining people who are involved in these kinds of crimes.”

Why today’s mañanera matters

President Sheinbaum’s participation in this week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen, China, was a key focus of the government’s Thursday morning press conference, helmed once again by Interior Minister Rosa Icela Rodríguez.

Unlike the two previous days, Sheinbaum didn’t join the mañanera by video link, but Rodríguez provided an overview of the president’s four-day visit to China.

Also of note at today’s mañanera was the interior minister’s response to the U.S. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin’s remarks on Wednesday about migrant caravans.

Members of a migrant caravan are currently walking northward through the state of Chiapas, reaching the municipality of Pijijiapan on Wednesday.

Last Thursday, U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to double tariffs on Mexican goods if Mexico didn’t stop the caravan.

Sheinbaum concludes her participation in the APEC summit

Rodríguez told reporters that Sheinbaum had concluded her participation in the 33rd APEC Leaders’ Meeting.

Encuentro muy productivo con el primer ministro de Australia, Anthony Albanese, y su gabinete. https://t.co/OhEykRioMK — Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo (@Claudiashein) November 19, 2026

She noted that the president attended “multiple” bilateral meetings with other leaders during her time in Shenzhen, including one on Thursday with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese.

“We know that this meeting will help strengthen trade relations [and] promote investment,” Rodríguez said.

She said that Sheinbaum was at the airport in Shenzhen and would arrive in Mexico City late Thursday or early Friday.

“Tomorrow she will lead the parade for the 116th anniversary of the Mexican Revolution,” Rodríguez said.

Later in the press conference, the interior minister announced that the government’s communications team had put together a video of Sheinbaum’s trip to Shenzhen.

The video showed the president arriving in Shenzhen, meeting with members of the Mexican community in China, addressing the APEC CEO Summit, engaging with Chinese President Xi Jinping in a bilateral meeting, meeting with other leaders, including Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and U.S. President Donald Trump, and speaking at the APEC Leaders’ Meeting.

Rodríguez praises Sheinbaum’s ‘composure’ on the world stage

Rodríguez said that Sheinbaum displayed “composure” and “confidence” during her participation in the APEC summit and other meetings in Shenzhen.

“She is a well-qualified woman who approaches these kinds of meetings with great composure and confidence,” she said.

Rodríguez said that Sheinbaum will provide her own account of her trip to China “in due course.”

“… We were particularly struck by how she handles herself with great composure and firmness, without confrontation or subservience, as befits a head of state,” she said.

“In the cabinet, we’re very proud [of her],” Rodríguez said.

Rodríguez: Mexico will continue to arrest people smugglers

A reporter asked Rodríguez about Mullin’s comments on Wednesday about migrant caravans.

In an appearance before a U.S. House of Representatives committee, he said:

“Under the previous Biden administration the cartels turned human trafficking into a multi-billion-dollar industry. And they’re selling, unfortunately, very vulnerable people a bill of goods that they can’t deliver. They will not be allowed to enter the United States underneath President Trump’s watch. Our border is secure and will remain secure. Fortunately, we have pretty good cooperation with Mexico right now and Mexico has assured us that [migrant caravans] will not make it to our southern border, their northern border. … For anyone who’s thinking about joining one of these caravans and allowing the cartels to extort dollars from you, you’re wasting your money, it’s not going to happen, you’re not coming into the United States unless you do it the proper way and that’s following our immigration policy that Congress set.”

Live: Homeland Security head Markwayne Mullin testifies at House hearing on national security

Watch this video on YouTube

Rodríguez said that some migrant caravans “have a kind of organization in which it has been detected that leaders … are owners of bus companies, for example.”

She said she didn’t have details on organized crime’s alleged involvement in migrant caravans, but added that the government is aware of the “business” of people smuggling, “which is obviously a crime.”

“We sometimes see it with another kind of facade,” she added, apparently suggesting that migrant caravans can be used as a front for people smuggling.

Rodríguez said that “Mexico has arrested” people smugglers and human traffickers in the past and “will continue detaining people who are involved in these kinds of crimes.”

“The Security Cabinet is very vigilant in ensuring there is no impunity,” she said.

Rodríguez said on Tuesday that National Migration Institute officials are trying to persuade migrants who are part of the caravan in Chiapas to return to their countries of origin, among which are Honduras, Guatemala and El Salvador. She said that the caravan was made up of 781 people, down from around 1,500 when it set off from Tapachula last week.

By Mexico News Daily chief staff writer Peter Davies (peter.davies@mexiconewsdaily.com)

World.title: Breaking: Peso surpasses 19 to the dollar, its weakest point in 17 months
World.content: Listen to this article The Mexican peso depreciated past 19 to the US dollar on Thursday morning, its weakest position in over a year. The peso sank to as low as 19.04, according to Bloomberg, a depreciation of just over 1% compared to the Bank of Mexico’s USD:MXN closing rate on Wednesday, which was 18.84. ﻿ The last time the peso traded above 19 to the greenback was in June 2025. Bloomberg reported that the depreciation of the peso on Thursday morning came “as the prospect of further [U.S.] Federal Reserve tightening intensified a selloff fueled by Mexico’s dovish monetary stance.” The Bank of Mexico (Banxico) lowered its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points earlier this month to 6.25%, and minutes released on Thursday from the central bank’s most recent monetary policy meeting “reaffirmed the majority of policymakers’ dovish stance,” according to Bloomberg. In contrast, the U.S. Federal Reserve increased its key interest rate to a target range of 3.75%-4% in September and is widely expected to raise it by another 25 basis points in December. The gap between Mexican and U.S. interest rates has helped support the peso by making the carry trade —borrowing in dollars to invest in higher-yielding peso assets — more attractive. But a hike by the Fed in early December would narrow that gap and reduce the carry trade’s appeal. The Fed could increase its interest rate again in January, which would make the gap even narrower, provided the Bank of Mexico doesn’t lift its key rate after its Dec. 17 monetary policy meeting. A Banxico hike appears unlikely as the central bank has signaled it will hold its rate steady after its November cut. In brief At a rate of 19.04 to the dollar, the Mexican peso has depreciated around 5.5% this year. The peso closed at 18.00 to the greenback on the final day of 2025, according to the Bank of Mexico. The peso has depreciated more than 11% since trading at 16.86 to the dollar in early September. The most recent MND Peso Index™ determined that the peso was 4.2% undervalued at a rate of 18.67 to the dollar. determined that the peso was 4.2% undervalued at a rate of 18.67 to the dollar. The Bank of Mexico looks set to hold its key rate steady next month even as inflation trends upward. Mexico’s annual headline rate was 3.75% in October, slightly higher than the 3.7% rate in the United States in September. Mexico News Daily

World.title: Opinion: Tulum will recover, but it won’t look the same
World.content:
Lately, almost every conversation I have about Tulum starts with the same question: Is it over? Buyers ask me, friends ask me, people who visited five years ago and read the headlines ask me.

I understand why. This has been a hard year, and anyone who lives and works here has felt it.

The numbers are not pretty, and I don’t want to pretend they are. In September 2025, hotel occupancy in Tulum fell to 49.2%, when a year earlier it was 66.7%. This summer, the Tulum Hotel Association reported occupancy down over 20% between May and July, and some hotels on the coast were running at around 15%. Between January and July, about a third fewer tourists arrived than in the same months last year.

Restaurants were quiet, some hotels closed for the season, and a few airlines dropped their routes.

So yes, something happened. But I see it differently from the collapse story, and I want to explain why. In my view, what Tulum lost was a moment, and what it keeps is a place.

More than a beach

When people talk about Tulum falling, they usually talk about the beach: the sargassum, the fees, the prices. The beach matters, of course. But Tulum was never only a beach.

The cenotes are still there, and seaweed never reaches them. The ruins have been standing on that cliff for centuries. Sian Ka’an, which UNESCO declared a World Heritage site in 1987, is still one of the largest protected coastlines in Mexico. And the food, the wellness culture and the architecture that made people around the world copy the “Tulum style” did not disappear in one bad summer.

A place that depends on one thing is fragile. Tulum has many things, and most of them have nothing to do with what the sea brings in.

The sargassum is a serious issue, and this year was the worst we have seen. By the end of July, around 96,000 metric tons had been collected along the Mexican Caribbean. But it is a condition of the whole region, it returns every year, and the destinations that handle it well are the ones that invest in handling it. That investment is now happening. In July, the federal government announced a plan of 2.64 billion pesos, led by the navy, with collection boats at sea, 35 kilometers of barriers and an early warning system, and Tulum is one of the five priority zones.

Some of the damage, let’s be fair, Tulum did to itself. Visitors felt they paid too much and were not welcome on beaches. That is changing, too. With Plan Tulum Renace, which started in November 2025 and was expanded this July, there are now 10 free public accesses to the beach, entry to the Parque del Jaguar is free, the fees for the archaeological zone were cut by up to half and prices are being monitored. For me, this matters as much as the sargassum boats, because reputation is what brings people back.

An identity money cannot build

There is one more reason I believe in Tulum, and you will not find it in any occupancy report. Cancún was designed. In 1969, a team from the central bank studied hundreds of sites and chose an empty sandbar, and the hotels came after the roads and the airport. It is a success, and it will keep working.

Tulum happened in a completely different way. It grew slowly: a road, some cabañas, a certain kind of traveler, a certain kind of architecture. Over the years, that turned into an identity, and an identity is something money cannot build. You can put up thousands of rooms in a year and a half. You cannot create the reason people want to be in them.

I also want to be clear about what recovery means, because I think this is where many people get it wrong. Tulum will not go back to 2021, and I don’t think it should. That period was a distortion, with too much construction, prices that made no sense and infrastructure that could not keep up. Some of the businesses closing now should close. The market is correcting its own excess, and that is healthy.

There are already signs of the next stage. The high season last November opened with occupancy of 75.8%. This winter, United, Air Canada, Air Transat and WestJet are bringing back eight international routes, and Mexicana is adding 24 flights. And new construction has almost stopped, as the state developers’ association reported no new housing projects registered in Tulum as of August.

A selective recovery

What I expect is a recovery that chooses. People will come back to a town that can no longer support everything the boom created, and they will choose what is well-located, well-built, fairly priced and well-designed. In my work, I see the same with property. The homes that have something real to offer will come back first, and stronger, because there is less noise around them.

In the meantime, Tulum is doing what a place should do in a quiet period. It is cleaning its coast, opening its beaches, controlling its prices and trying to deliver what it promised. I don’t see that as a town in decline. I see a town getting ready to deserve its premium again.

The spirit was always the hard part, and Tulum has it. The rest is maintenance.

Jana Mihalikova is the founder and managing director of Heron Real Estate, a buyer-side real estate advisory in the Riviera Maya.

World.title: Arcor Shuts La Campagnola Tuna Plant
World.content:
Arcor says tuna is no longer caught in Argentina and local mackerel has run short, so cans will now come ready-made from abroad.

The halt did not come out of nowhere. In October 2026 La Campagnola stopped production at the plant and suspended about 60 workers, citing a stock of unsold tuna and a shortage of mackerel, according to the Mar del Plata daily La Capital.

Mackerel, known locally as caballa, was the fish the plant processed from Argentine waters. La Nación says the plant had been idle for months before the closure was announced.

La Nación reports that Arcor bought the plant about 20 years ago. The daily El Día notes that Mar del Plata once had about 35 factories canning mackerel, anchovy and tuna.

Some employees questioned the lack of advance information, according to Mar del Plata media summarised by iProfesional. They also voiced uncertainty about moving to plants in other provinces.

Arcor has not published how many of the 75 will accept a transfer or what separation terms apply to those who stay. The company says its other La Campagnola sites, in Villa Mercedes in San Luis province, in San Juan and in Recreo in Catamarca, will keep supplying the shelves.

The brand stays on sale in the usual shops, according to the company statement reported by El Día. For Mar del Plata, one of Argentina’s main fishing ports, the closure removes another employer from the waterfront.

Arcor says it will offer all of them a transfer to other plants in its group. It has not said how many will accept.

Why did Arcor close the plant?

The company says the global tuna trade moved to finished cans and that Argentine mackerel has run short, which made local canning unsustainable.

World.title: YPF Offers Loans to Small Suppliers
World.content:
YPF will not lend the money itself; it only guarantees that its purchase orders will be paid, which cuts the banks' risk.

Business: Argentina

YPF, Argentina’s state-controlled oil company, will start a pilot in December that lets small suppliers borrow against the company’s own purchase orders, according to iProfesional on Thursday 19 November 2026. Chief executive Horacio Marín says the first half of a contract can be advanced at about 32%, against 45% to 50% elsewhere.

The aim, Marín says, is to stop fast-growing suppliers from going bust while they wait to be paid. He says growth can ruin a firm that must fund the work before it is paid.

Marín first outlined the problem on Liderologías, a streaming programme. Growth can break a small or medium-sized company (SME) “because of financial problems, not economic ones”, he said, and a supplier whose workload triples “has to have capital”.

YPF pays at 30 days, he said, but certifying the work, a technical sign-off that it was done, can take up to 30 more. iProfesional puts the gap between that review and payment at up to 60 days. In the first stage, a supplier holding an awarded purchase order can ask a bank for an advance of 50% of the contract.

The loans run through Finova, a digital finance platform that links companies with banks, and at least three lenders are involved: the private banks Macro and Galicia and the Neuquén provincial bank, BPN.

YPF acts only as the guarantor, Marín said. “If YPF gives you a purchase order it is binding, it is an obligation I have, and so the certainty of YPF paying is so high that it lowers the risk, and that lowers the rate.”

Marín gave a worked example: on a US$1 million contract the firm would receive the peso equivalent of US$500,000 up front. After the work is certified, the second half can also be discounted instead of waiting up to 60 days.

The scheme follows a month of pressure from local suppliers. On 22 October, Neuquén daily Noticias NQN reported that the provincial business chamber CEIPA said YPF had promised to pay at 30 days and that the provincial bank would offer financing to local small firms.

Around the same time, at the AOG Patagonia 2026 oil and gas fair in Neuquén, chambers grouped in Fecene, the province’s energy-sector federation, asked Marín for a bigger share of tenders under the province’s “Buy from Neuquén” law. Marín asked them for a list of suppliers by trade, according to iProfesional.

The plan deals with cash flow, a separate issue from the tender demand, and Marín insisted it is no subsidy. “Helping does not mean subsidising,” he said, adding that using the line is the supplier’s choice.

The loans are in pesos, and Marín says the same advance elsewhere costs 12 to 15 percentage points more. YPF has not published the pilot’s rules or any cap per firm.

The suppliers work mainly in Vaca Muerta, Argentina’s main shale oil and gas basin, in Neuquén province. YPF has not said how much money the pilot will cover.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is YPF lending money to suppliers?

No. Banks lend through Finova; YPF only guarantees that its purchase orders will be paid, according to Marín.

Who can use the scheme?

Small and medium-sized suppliers holding a YPF purchase order, on a voluntary basis. The pilot starts in December 2026.

World.title: Tesla Opens Orders in Argentina Friday
World.content:
A higher tariff-free price ceiling for electric imports cleared the way, and Tesla is in talks with YPF, Argentina's state-controlled oil company, on charging.

Business: Argentina

Tesla will start taking orders for the Model 3 and Model Y in Argentina on Friday 20 November 2026, its first sales in the country, the company confirmed to Bloomberg Línea, a Latin American business news outlet, according to Dolarhoy, an Argentine personal-finance news site. Official prices will be published on launch day, so none is confirmed yet.

A government change made the launch more workable. Dolarhoy reports that Argentina raised the maximum factory value of fully electric cars that can enter without the 35% tariff on cars from outside the regional trade bloc from US$16,000 to US$35,000, within an annual quota.

The ceiling applies to the car’s value at origin, not to the shipping, insurance and local sales costs on top. So the tariff relief does not mean a Tesla will sell for US$35,000, Dolarhoy notes.

Sector estimates quoted by the same site put prices above US$50,000, depending on version and import conditions. Contexto Tucumán, citing estimates, says a Tesla could start around US$60,000.

Tesla will use its direct model: digital orders plus physical spaces to see the cars and take test drives. Contexto Tucumán reports that the first point is planned for the Unicenter shopping mall, on level 1, showing two vehicles, and that Tesla Argentina SRL, a local company, has been set up.

The Cybertruck will not be part of the first offer, which is limited to the two high-volume models, according to Dolarhoy. Dolarhoy says the aim is to start with the two highest-volume models.

The partnership with YPF is still at the exploratory stage. Dolarhoy says the two companies are discussing cooperation on fast-charging infrastructure and energy storage, after the June letter of intent.

Dolarhoy says the arrival will also test the development of Argentina’s charging infrastructure. The clearest signal will come on Friday, when Tesla publishes its Argentine prices and opens the order books.

Fani Titi, the group chief executive, said the result showed “disciplined strategic execution” against “persistent macroeconomic uncertainty”. Adjusted earnings per share rose 7.4% to 43.5 pence, and the interim dividend rose to 18.5 pence, a payout of 42.5% of adjusted earnings.

Lending grew faster than deposits. The weaker side of the ledger was cost. Operating costs rose 9.7% to £623.8 million (about US$817 million), or 4.8% at constant currency, pushing the cost-to-income ratio to 53.3% from 51.9%, while the credit loss ratio improved to 0.28% from 0.35%.

Titi pointed to a new “Alliance Banking” partnership with the Shoprite Group in Southern Africa, which our 10 November report covers. The group says it also keeps investing in technology and client-facing staff.

The group is also reorganising into three global segments: Private Client, Corporate and Investment Banking, and Corporate Mid-Market. Investec said the spending to build them is expected to peak this financial year and should lift earnings growth from the year to March 2028.

On capital, the core equity ratio, a measure of loss-absorbing capital, was 13.8% at Investec Limited and 13.1% at Investec plc. A tighter regulatory limit on how far banks can rely on their own risk models, effective 1 January 2027, is expected to cut Investec Limited’s ratio by about 0.85 to 1.00 percentage points, the company said.

The company guides to a group return on equity (profit as a share of shareholders’ funds) of 13.0% to 14.0% for the year to March 2027, with Southern Africa at 18.0% to 19.0%. It puts the UK arm’s return on tangible equity at 12.0% to 13.0%.
