World.title: GTA VI Launch Week Comes With Special Food Menus Across Prague
World.content:
With Grand Theft Auto VI arriving on November 19, Bolt Food has teamed up with Prague restaurants to offer exclusive gaming menus, discounts and a competition to win PlayStation 5 consoles and copies of the game.

After years of anticipation and two delays, Grand Theft Auto VI finally arrives on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S on Thursday, November 19. For many players, the launch is likely to mean long gaming sessions and late nights. In Prague, there will also be plenty of food options to go with them.



From November 9 to 22, Bolt Food is running a special Gaming Campaign, bringing together local restaurants that have created menus inspired by the new game. The selection includes burgers, pizzas, sushi, chicken dishes and larger sharing meals, available exclusively through the delivery platform.

The campaign also includes discounts on selected offers and a competition featuring PlayStation 5 consoles and copies of GTA VI.

Win a PlayStation 5 or GTA VI

Bolt Food is giving away three PlayStation 5 consoles and 36 copies of Grand Theft Auto VI as part of the campaign.

To enter, customers need to order one of the participating gaming menus or place an order worth at least CZK 350 from a participating restaurant. Each qualifying order automatically counts as one entry, with no additional registration required.

Some orders may also include surprise gifts from Niceboy.

The competition runs in Prague until November 22. Full terms and conditions are available through Bolt Food’s Czech Instagram account, @boltfood_cz.

What Prague Restaurants Are Offering

Several restaurants have put together special dishes and combinations for the campaign. Here are some of the options available through Bolt Food.

Burgers and Comfort Food

Hoxton Burgers – Chorizo Smash

The burger restaurant has prepared a special smash burger featuring chorizo.

Želva – Trevor Burger

A substantial combination of a 170-gram beef patty, double cheddar, bacon chutney, blue cheese, maple syrup, crispy onions, jalapeños and chipotle mayonnaise, finished with a poutine topping.

Master Burger – Sunrise Burger

Beef, cheddar, bacon and a fried egg make up this burger, which takes inspiration from a classic breakfast combination.

Amici – Gaming Pizza and Burger Menus

Customers can choose between special gaming-themed pizza and burger menus.

Pizza for Sharing

Three Prague pizzerias have also joined the campaign with exclusive combinations.

Davinci offers three options: Street Hustler, Five Star Chase and Million Dollar Slice.

Presto Italiano has created three pizzas named after GTA-inspired characters: Jason’s Pizza, with chicken, pepperoni, bacon and red onion; Lucia’s Pizza, featuring pepperoni, bacon, chilli and Parmesan; and Raul’s Pizza, with a cream base, chicken, bacon, Gorgonzola and garlic.

Caruso is serving a Gaming Pizza topped with ham, bacon, spicy salami, smoked scamorza and onion.

Sushi and Japanese Food

Sushi fans can choose from several campaign-specific options.

Doebikokota – Respect +

The combination includes Philadelphia Classic rolls, crispy chicken gyoza and Coca-Cola.

Aurum Sushi has introduced three gaming options: Hot Pursuit, The Big Score and Wanted.

Imperial Sushi is offering several dishes, including Geisha Roll, Salmon & Tuna Snack, Office Snack, Baked Chicken on Iceberg Roll and Baked Chicken Tamago Roll.

Hasu Sushi – Hasu Gaming Challenge Set**

The special 18-piece set includes salmon nigiri, salmon maki and Sunshine Roll.

Chicken and Wraps

For those looking for something easy to eat during a gaming session, two restaurants are offering chicken-based options.

Chickin has introduced the GTA Power Griller and GTA Quesadilla, both available in double-bacon versions.

Louisiana Chicken is serving the Six Stars Sandwich, featuring crispy chicken strips with bacon-chilli sauce, tomato and iceberg lettuce, as well as the Wanted Wrap, which combines chicken nuggets with the same sauce.

Wraps, Kebabs and Sharing Combos

Other participating restaurants have opted for larger combinations and meals designed for different group sizes.

Burrito Loco – Crunchy Wrap Gaming Menu

The menu includes a drink and a choice of churros with chocolate dip or chips and salsa.

Mahir Kebab offers three combinations: Solo Mission, Duo Heist and Full Crew Combo, with portions designed for one, two or three people.

Matoka – I’m The Gamer Set

A special menu created for the campaign.

Something for the End of the Night

For those looking for a more substantial meal or something sweet, two more restaurants have joined the line-up.

Lasagneria – Spicy Lasagna and Oreo Tiramisu Combo

The main course combines Italian salsiccia sausage, chilli, béchamel and Grana Padano. Dessert comes in the form of Oreo tiramisu with mascarpone cream and espresso.

Na Květnici – Jason Duval Menu

A special menu named after one of the two main characters in GTA VI.

How to Order

All campaign menus are available through the Bolt Food app. Customers can browse the participating restaurants, select their preferred dishes and order directly for delivery.

The Gaming Campaign runs until November 22, meaning the special menus will only be available for a limited period.

Whether you’re planning a gaming night with friends or simply looking for something different to order this week, Prague’s restaurant line-up has plenty of options.

World.title: Prague Christmas Markets 2026 – Dates, Locations and Opening Hours
World.content:
Prague’s Christmas market season will begin on November 20, with the first stalls opening at Náměstí Míru.

The main markets in the city centre will follow on November 28, when the Christmas tree in Old Town Square will also be illuminated for the first time.

Markets and Advent events will take place across the Czech capital, from the historic centre to neighbourhoods such as Vinohrady, Smíchov and Karlín. While some will close on Christmas Eve, others will remain open until January 6, 2027.



Prague Christmas Markets 2026 – Full Schedule

Náměstí Míru | Nov 20 – Dec 24 |

Náměstí Republiky | Nov 25 – Dec 24 |

Tylovo náměstí | Nov 26 – Dec 24 |

Anděl, Smíchov | Nov 27 – Dec 31 |

Mariánské náměstí | Nov 27 – Jan 6 |

Old Town | Nov 28 – Jan 6 |

Wenceslas Square | Nov 28 – Jan 6 |

Jiří z Poděbrad Square | Nov 28 – Dec 23 |

Karlínske náměstí | Dec 6 |

When Will the Christmas Tree in Prague Be Lit?

The Christmas tree in Old Town Square will be illuminated for the first time on Saturday, November 28, marking the opening of Prague’s main Christmas market.

According to organiser Taiko, the tree will be installed on November 23 and 24. This year’s Norway spruce comes from Šimonovice in the Liberec Region. It is approximately 60 years old, stands 23 metres tall and has a trunk circumference of more than two metres.

After the Christmas season, apprentices from Jarov Secondary Vocational School will process its wood into products for social organisations in Prague.

Where to Find the Main Christmas Markets

Old Town Square

November 28, 2026 – January 6, 2027

Daily, 10:00–22:00

Prague’s largest Christmas market will feature wooden stalls selling decorations, handicrafts, gifts and traditional seasonal food. The Christmas tree and its lighting ceremony will once again be the main attraction.

Wenceslas Square

November 28, 2026 – January 6, 2027

Daily, 10:00–22:00

Located a short walk from Old Town Square, the market will offer Christmas decorations, gifts, handicrafts and refreshments.

Náměstí Míru

November 20 – December 24, 2026

Daily, 10:00–20:00

The first Christmas market of the season will open around the Church of St Ludmila. Stalls will sell Advent wreaths, candles, decorations, sweets and seasonal refreshments.

Anděl

November 27 – December 31, 2026

Daily, 8:00–20:00

The market in Smíchov’s pedestrian zone will remain open until New Year’s Eve, making it one of the few locations operating after Christmas.

Other Christmas Events in Prague

Several additional events will take place during Advent.

– Bavarian-Czech Advent Market: November 27–29 at Chotek Palace, with regional food, nativity scenes, woodcarving demonstrations and workshops.

– Christmas Craft Markets: December 5–6 at Výstaviště Praha, featuring around 150 artisans. Admission is free.

– Lemarket: December 11–13 at Galerie Mánes, showcasing Czech designers, independent brands, fashion and handmade gifts.

– New Town Advent: December 13 at the New Town Hall, with craft stalls, workshops, performances and free admission.

World.title: Chinese National Circus to Make Czech Debut in February 2027
World.content:
The National Circus of China will perform in the Czech Republic for the first time in February 2027, bringing its production ZENSATION: Grandmasters of Balance to Prague, Brno and Ostrava.

The show combines traditional Chinese acrobatics with contemporary stage production, drawing on an artistic tradition that dates back more than 2,000 years.



Titled ZENSATION: Grandmasters of Balance, the production brings together some of the circus’s best-known acts in a programme featuring performers trained at China’s leading circus academies.

Many have spent most of their lives mastering acrobatic disciplines, with years of intensive training behind the precision and control required for each performance.

The programme is designed as a retrospective of the Chinese circus, revisiting celebrated routines that have received awards at international festivals and attracted audiences around the world.

Rather than relying on elaborate visual effects, the production puts the emphasis on the performers themselves, highlighting balance, coordination, physical strength and precision.

Its approach combines established acrobatic techniques with a contemporary presentation, placing the human body and its capabilities at the centre of the show.

The production is directed by Raoul Schoregge, artistic director of the Chinese National Circus in Europe. Under his direction, the show brings together highlights from the circus’s long history in a format intended to appeal to both established fans of acrobatics and audiences encountering the tradition for the first time.

The February 2027 tour will visit three cities:

– Ostrava – February 2027

– Brno – February 2027

– Prague – February 2027

Tickets are available here.

World.title: Could You Crack the Case? English-Language Detective Game Comes to Prague
World.content:
On November 29, The Globe Bookstore & Café will host The Edenmoor Case, an interactive detective game that challenges teams to solve a fictional crime by examining evidence, questioning witnesses and putting their theories to the test.

Set in 1928 in the fictional town of Edenmoor, Louisiana, the game invites participants to step into the role of investigators.

Armed with an initial case file, players must uncover what happened, determine who can be trusted and build a convincing case before their time runs out.



Unlike traditional escape rooms, The Edenmoor Case does not rely on elaborate physical sets or theatrical performances. Instead, teams gather around a table and conduct their investigation through a digital platform, accessible from a laptop, tablet or smartphone.

The platform allows players to explore different locations, question witnesses, examine documents and uncover new leads. But the information they encounter is not always straightforward. Witness accounts may contradict one another, seemingly important details can lead nowhere, and a single overlooked clue could change the direction of an investigation.

Much of the experience unfolds through discussion between team members. Players compare their findings, challenge one another’s assumptions and decide which leads are worth pursuing.

With limited time and multiple possible interpretations of the evidence, reaching a shared conclusion becomes part of the challenge.

View this post on Instagram A post shared by The Edenmoor Case | Detective Game Prague (@edenmoor.case)

The game also introduces a competitive element. Several teams investigate the same crime simultaneously, working with identical evidence and under the same two-hour time limit. Each team must submit its conclusions, with the challenge focusing on the strength of the investigation rather than simply who finishes first.

Designed for groups of two to eight people, the English-language experience offers an alternative to traditional group activities in Prague. Friends, couples and colleagues can take part together, while individual participants are also welcome to register.

The next session takes place on Sunday, November 29, at The Globe Bookstore & Café, Pštrossova 6, Prague 1. Doors open at 4:00 PM, and the investigation begins at 5:00 PM.

Tickets cost 300 CZK per person in advance or 330 CZK at the door.

Registration and further information are available at www.edenmoor.eu/prague. Updates and a closer look at the game can also be found on Instagram at @edenmoor.case.

For private group bookings and enquiries, contact [email protected].

World.title: Samosas, Biryanis and Tandoori: Three Reasons to Visit Ekant in Prague
World.content:
Karlovo náměstí is not usually the first place people think of when planning a dinner out in Prague.

It is central, but it lacks the restaurant scene of neighbourhoods such as Vinohrady or Karlín. There are plenty of reasons to pass through, but perhaps fewer to stay for dinner.

Ekant Indian Restaurant is one of them.



The restaurant serves a broad menu of North Indian dishes, from curries and tandoori specialities to biryanis, samosas and freshly baked naan.

If there are two things worth ordering, they are the samosas and the biryanis. The latter are a particularly good alternative to the usual curry-and-rice combination, while the samosas make an easy choice to start a meal.

The menu also covers chicken, lamb and seafood dishes, alongside a sizeable vegetarian selection. Vegan options are available, too, and the restaurant can accommodate certain dietary requirements on request.

There is plenty of choice, whether you are visiting for a quick lunch, a relaxed dinner or a meal with friends. The restaurant has a casual dining room, with table service, takeaway and delivery available.

World.title: Need a Plumber or Electrician in Prague? This App Can Help
World.content:
Finding a reliable plumber, electrician, cleaner or handyman can be time-consuming, particularly for foreigners living in the Czech Republic who may not know where to look or whom to contact.

A Czech platform called Helplii aims to make the process easier by bringing customers and local service providers together through a single online marketplace.



Instead of searching through multiple websites, social media groups or personal recommendations, users can describe the job they need done and post a request through the Helplii app. Local professionals can then respond with offers, allowing customers to compare prices, availability and reviews before deciding whom to hire.

The process is designed to cover everything in one place. Once an offer has been accepted, customers can communicate directly with the provider through the app, share details and photos, and arrange the work. Payments are also handled through the platform.

Helplii covers a wide range of everyday services, including plumbing, electrical work, home repairs, cleaning, furniture assembly, gardening, moving assistance and pet sitting.

The platform also lists services such as IT support, accounting, tutoring, photography and translation.

According to the company, its marketplace currently covers more than 25 service categories and 16 cities and towns across the Czech Republic.

The platform focuses primarily on freelancers and small businesses, although larger service companies can also register. To offer services in the Czech Republic, providers must have a registered business identification number (IČO).

Helplii also includes several features intended to make transactions more transparent. Providers submit their own prices, customers can review ratings and feedback from previous jobs, and communication takes place within the app. Phone numbers remain hidden until an offer is accepted.

For service providers, the platform offers another way to find customers without having to rely entirely on advertising or personal contacts. They can receive requests matching their skills and availability, submit their prices and build a reputation through customer reviews.

Helplii is available for both iOS and Android devices.

World.title: West Ham Star Tomáš Souček Launches English Autobiography in Prague
World.content:
Tomáš Souček has presented the English edition of his autobiography at the British Embassy in Prague, with the book set to reach UK readers ahead of Christmas.

British Ambassador Matt Field welcomed the West Ham United midfielder to Thunovský Palace on Monday, November 16, for the launch. The event marked the next step for the autobiography, which was first published in the Czech Republic a year ago.

The English edition will be titled Tomáš Souček – My Story and will initially be available through West Ham’s official fan shop. Souček said the decision to translate the book had been made from the beginning, with the aim of making it accessible to supporters in England.



“I’m living a second life in England. My children are growing up there, and I feel right at home. That’s why I’m so happy we can bring this book to West Ham fans. I have an incredible connection with them, and they deserve it,” Souček said to Prague Morning.

The launch also featured an unusual alternative to the traditional champagne toast. Instead of pouring sparkling wine over the book, Souček and Field blew bubbles above its cover, referencing West Ham’s pre-match tradition and the club anthem I’m Forever Blowing Bubbles.

“In England, seeing a bubble blower means seeing West Ham. Besides, I’m not really a fan of being doused in alcohol. Bubbles are a much better fit for this book,” Souček said.

Field, meanwhile, recalled watching the Czech midfielder lift the UEFA Europa Conference League trophy in Prague in 2023.

“I’ve been a fan ever since. I know he’s scored more goals in the Premier League than any other Czech footballer. But apparently, that wasn’t enough for him, so he decided to write a book, too. As a diplomat, I can only hope he doesn’t decide to try his hand at my job as well. That would start to look like a hat-trick,” the ambassador joked.

The autobiography was written by Souček together with football journalists David Čermák and Jan Palička. It covers both his professional career and personal life, including his struggles with insomnia and depression at different stages of his football journey.

The English edition includes an additional chapter covering West Ham’s relegation season, the disappointing World Cup campaign in the United States and Souček’s return to football after a serious ankle injury.

World.title: Furiant Is Back: Prague’s Czech Sweets Pop-Up Reopens November 27
World.content:
Furiant, the Czech pastry pop-up that attracted long queues and sold out daily during its first run, will reopen on November 27 at its original location inside the Parnas restaurant.

The project brings together Jiří Matějka, former head pastry chef at Karlín’s Eska and Café Slavia, and Jozef Onderka, owner of Café Slavia, SmetanaQ and the Forbína cocktail bar.



Their idea was to create a modern Czech confectionery focused on traditional sweet dishes rather than the croissants and French-style pastries found in many of Prague’s newer bakeries.

When Furiant first opened in October 2025, the response exceeded expectations. Operating from Thursday to Sunday, the pop-up sold out every day, sometimes closing earlier than scheduled.

The team initially struggled to keep up with demand, choosing not to increase production at the expense of quality.

Matějka developed the concept after several years working in Berlin, where he began to miss traditional Czech sweets. His experience at Eska and abroad helped shape an approach that combines familiar dishes with contemporary pastry techniques and carefully selected ingredients.

The menu puts the spotlight on Czech sweet meals, including semolina porridge, rice pudding, plum dumplings, pancakes and buchtičky se šodó (small sweet yeast buns served with vanilla custard).

View this post on Instagram A post shared by Furiant (@furiant_prague)

One of Furiant’s defining characteristics is its deliberately limited menu, which changes regularly according to the season and availability of ingredients.

The kitchen works with Czech flour, dairy products from the Struhy farm, chocolate from the Herůfek family and locally sourced poppy seeds, which are ground on-site.

The reopening will give Prague residents another opportunity to visit the pop-up at Parnas, overlooking the Vltava River and Prague Castle.

World.title: Budapest’s City Park Ice Rink celebrates 100 years with season opening this Friday
World.content:
Budapest’s City Park Ice Rink, Városligeti Műjégpálya, kicks off its 2026/2027 winter season this Friday, 20th November, marking an unusual milestone. Exactly 100 years ago to the day, workers switched on the first artificial cooling system beneath the lake, transforming how the Hungarian capital spent its winters. For expats, international students, and visitors in town this week, Friday night offers a rare chance to skate on a genuine piece of local history.

Author: Tselmeg Khosbayar

A century of artificial ice beside Vajdahunyad Castle

People have been skating in City Park since January 1870, when the Pest Skating Association first opened the lake to the public. Back then, skaters were completely at the mercy of the weather, if the water did not freeze solid, the season simply did not happen. That changed on 20th November 1926 with the installation of underground cooling pipes, making Budapest one of the earliest cities in Europe to run an outdoor artificial rink and guaranteeing a reliable winter season.

A century later, the City Park Ice Rink Budapest spans more than 12,000 square metres, ranking among Europe’s largest open-air rinks. Framed by the Neo-Baroque Skating Hall and the towers of Vajdahunyad Castle, it remains a winter fixture for locals and newcomers alike.

What to expect at Friday’s centenary opening

To mark the 100-year anniversary, gates open on Friday, 20th November from 5:00 PM to 9:00 PM. Organisers have lined up live music, figure-skating and ice-sport demonstrations, and family-friendly anniversary activities throughout the evening. Because the rink sits completely outdoors, final opening times always depend on weather conditions and last-minute ice preparation. Anyone heading over on Friday should check the official website (mujegpalya.hu) or the rink’s Facebook and Instagram pages beforehand for confirmed ticket releases and session hours.

Practical tips for first-time visitors

Getting to the rink at Olof Palme sétány 5, right behind Heroes’ Square, takes only a few minutes from central Budapest. Hop on the historic yellow M1 metro line from Deák Ferenc tér or Oktogon to Hősök tere, and walk two minutes across the square. Buying tickets online in advance is strongly recommended, especially for Friday nights and weekends when queues at the ticket window build up quickly. Keep in mind that daily skating is divided into morning (9:00 AM–1:00 PM) and afternoon/evening (5:00 PM–9:00 PM) sessions, with a break in between to resurface the ice.

Because the rink is wide open to the winter air, temperatures drop noticeably once the sun sets. Dress in warm layers, bring gloves both for warmth and to protect your hands if you take a tumble, and pack thick socks if you plan to rent skates at the entrance (you will need a valid ID or a small cash deposit). For quieter ice and room to practice, go on a weekday morning; for floodlights, music, and a livelier crowd, aim for Friday or Saturday evening.

Student discounts and on-site facilities

International students living in Budapest can take advantage of reduced entry prices by showing a valid student ID at the ticket desk. Inside the main Skating Hall, visitors have access to heated changing rooms, a guarded cloakroom for shoes and backpacks, and warm lounge areas to thaw out between laps.

Once open, the City Park Ice Rink Budapest typically stays active until late February, weather permitting. Paired with a hot drink from the on-site café or an evening soak at the neighbouring Széchenyi Thermal Bath, it remains one of the best ways to spend a winter day in the Hungarian capital.

World.title: Hungary lifts veto on Ukraine’s progress towards EU membership
World.content:
Hungary has withdrawn its objection to Ukraine and Moldova opening the final two negotiating clusters in their European Union accession processes, removing a significant obstacle to their membership bids.

Hungary lifts block on Ukraine’s EU plans

EU diplomats told the Kyiv Independent on 18 November that Budapest had dropped its opposition to the remaining steps needed to advance the two candidate countries’ negotiations. Hungary had previously withheld the final approval without publicly providing a formal explanation.

The decision concerns the clusters covering agriculture and the green agenda, the last two of six groups of policy areas to be opened in the accession process.

Further EU approval is still required

Hungary’s change of position does not mean the two clusters will open immediately. Ambassadors representing all 27 EU member states must first agree on a common position, followed by approval from national ministers. Only after these steps can an intergovernmental conference formally declare the clusters open.

All six clusters are currently expected to be opened by December. The focus will then shift increasingly towards the rule of law and anti-corruption requirements. Both Ukraine and Moldova must formally meet a series of interim benchmarks covering these areas before individual elements of their accession negotiations can be considered complete.

The European Commission’s annual enlargement assessments suggest that Moldova has largely completed the necessary work. EU and national diplomats reportedly expect the Commission to circulate a report confirming Chisinau’s progress during the week beginning 23 November.

Ukraine still faces additional challenges, particularly in implementing rule-of-law reforms. However, a joint EU-Ukraine task force has been established to accelerate the process. One EU diplomat told the Kyiv Independent that the cooperation could triple the pace of Ukraine’s progress.

Ukraine faces a longer reform process

EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos and Lithuanian Foreign Minister Kęstutis Budrys have expressed hope that Ukraine will complete the required reforms by the end of Lithuania’s presidency of the Council of the EU in June 2027.

The political background to Hungary’s reversal remains subject to interpretation. The previous government of Viktor Orbán consistently adopted a critical position towards Ukraine’s EU ambitions. According to EU diplomats cited by the Kyiv Independent, the new Hungarian administration was also keen to avoid appearing too accommodating towards Kyiv.

The withdrawal of the objection therefore represents an important breakthrough for both Ukraine and Moldova, but it does not guarantee their eventual membership.

Opening the final negotiating clusters is only another stage in a lengthy process. Both countries will still need to demonstrate progress on democratic standards, the rule of law, anti-corruption measures and the adoption of EU legislation before accession talks can be concluded.

World.title: Hungarian expert helps Montenegro move closer to EU membership, foreign minister says
World.content:
Hungary has sent an integration expert to Montenegro to work directly with the country’s government on its European Union accession process, Foreign Minister Anita Orbán has announced. During talks in Budapest on Thursday, she and Montenegrin Deputy Prime Minister Filip Ivanović discussed how Hungary could help the Balkan country conclude its accession negotiations this year and become a full EU member in 2028.

Hungary provides practical support for Montenegro’s EU ambitions

In a Facebook post following their meeting, Orbán said Hungary was providing more than political backing for Montenegro’s EU ambitions. Hungarian integration experts have been sent to every Western Balkan country, with one now working directly alongside the Montenegrin government on its accession process.

The Foreign Ministry has also appointed a dedicated official to deal with Western Balkan affairs, aiming to make Hungary’s support for the region’s European integration more effective.

Orbán stressed that Montenegro had made significant progress over the past two decades and fulfilled most of the conditions required for EU membership.

She also highlighted the longstanding ties between the two countries. Hungary was among the first states to recognise Montenegro’s independence in 2006 and opened its embassy in Podgorica that same year. The two countries are celebrating the 20th anniversary of their diplomatic relations in 2026.

Hungarian companies also play an important role in the Montenegrin economy, while an increasing number of Hungarians are choosing the Balkan country as a holiday destination.

Filip Ivanović and Anita Orbán. Photo: Facebook/Orbán Anita

Hungary promises to push for faster EU enlargement

According to Orbán, Montenegro’s EU membership would send an important message to the entire Western Balkans: countries that meet the necessary conditions should have a place in the European Union.

She added that enlargement would strengthen both regional stability and Europe’s security.

The Hungarian foreign minister also congratulated Montenegro on the expected closure of two additional EU accession negotiating chapters in Brussels on Thursday, marking another step towards membership.

Prime Minister Péter Magyar has likewise pledged strong Hungarian support for Western Balkan enlargement. Speaking at a joint press conference with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Berlin last week, he said Hungary maintained good relations with every Western Balkan country, without exception.

“Serbia and the Western Balkans can count on us,” Magyar said, adding that he would strongly advocate in Brussels for accelerating the region’s EU accession process.

Montenegro is currently among the frontrunners in the Western Balkans’ EU integration process, with 2028 identified as its target year for full membership.

World.title: Viktor Orbán’s brother invoked family ties to seek visa help from ambassador, email reveals
World.content:
Áron Orbán, the younger brother of former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, explicitly identified himself as the prime minister’s brother when asking Hungary’s ambassador to Iraq for help arranging visas for 16 people in 2023. The email, recently made public by György Velkey, Parliamentary State Secretary at the Foreign Ministry, adds to growing scrutiny of the former prime minister’s brother, who was arrested last week on suspicion of human trafficking and influence peddling.

“Áron Orbán (Prime Minister’s brother)” – the email to the Iraqi ambassador

The email, dated 21 August 2023, was addressed to Attila Tar, Hungary’s ambassador to Baghdad at the time. In it, Áron Orbán asked for assistance in arranging visa appointments for 16 people, adding that his local business partner was ready to receive them and put them to work. He also suggested that three more groups might follow.

“Could I kindly ask for a little help with suggesting appointments for the 16 people in the attachment?” he wrote, thanking the ambassador in advance.

According to the attached document, Orbán was seeking short-stay Schengen C visas for all 16 applicants through the Hungarian embassy in Iraq.

A C-type visa allows its holder to stay in the Schengen Area for up to 90 days. Such visas are generally issued for tourism, business trips and other short-term purposes.

However, Velkey questioned the way the request was presented, pointing out that the email referred to the visas as tourist visas despite mentioning that the applicants were expected to start working for a local partner.

Most notably, the email was signed “Áron Orbán (Prime Minister’s brother)”.

Further revelations about the former prime minister’s brother

Velkey has published several documents in recent days concerning Áron Orbán’s business activities and alleged access to Hungarian diplomatic services.

Earlier, he revealed a September 2023 letter in which the former prime minister’s brother offered cooperation to then Foreign Minister Péter Szijjártó and recommended a new chief adviser, who also managed his investment portfolio. In July 2023, Orbán had also requested a personal meeting with Eszter Gyarmati, then the Foreign Ministry’s administrative state secretary, regarding a proposed strategic partnership covering education, IT and security technology services.

Another email published by Velkey reportedly showed that the Foreign Ministry had instructed its diplomatic missions in Vietnam to give special attention to two companies linked to Áron Orbán: Multi Shoot Zrt. and HR Capital Kft. The instructions also called for priority appointments, with the only explanation being that this was a “senior management expectation” of the ministry.

Viktor Orbán’s office previously described the allegations surrounding the emails as an attempt at defamation. It insisted that personal or family connections could not be used to influence government decisions during the previous administration. It also said that authorities had always taken the necessary steps whenever concerns arose over visa or residence permit applications, including those connected to the former prime minister’s brother and the Vietnamese visa cases.

Áron Orbán arrested on suspicion of human trafficking

On 11 November, a court ordered Áron Orbán and his partner to be held in pre-trial detention for one month. They are suspected of helping Vietnamese nationals travel to Western Europe through Hungary over several months in 2024.

According to investigators, the suspects allegedly assisted with visa applications at Hungarian diplomatic missions and charged recruitment fees per person, subsequently sharing the proceeds. Authorities believe that more than 100 Vietnamese citizens may have benefited from the scheme.

The National Office for Asset Recovery and Protection (NVVH) suspects Áron Orbán of influence peddling, while the National Bureau of Investigation suspects him and his associates of human smuggling committed commercially and as part of a criminal organisation. These remain allegations, and the investigation is ongoing.

Áron Orbán in a police vehicle after being detained. Photo: MTI

Telex investigation first exposed the visa business

Telex first investigated Áron Orbán’s business associates and alleged visa-related activities in 2025, publishing an extensive investigation into the network and its operations.

The investigation followed the leak of an audio recording in October 2024, in which Áron Orbán could be heard discussing visa-related matters with Dávid Héjj, an associate of Viktor Orbán working at the Prime Minister’s Cabinet Office.

The recording suggested that Áron Orbán and his associates had an interest in arranging visas, while some of their applications were reportedly being blocked by the authorities.

World.title: Hungary gets green light for EUR 5.4 billion EU defence loan – Motorway projects could also benefit
World.content:
Hungary’s revised application for a EUR 5.4 billion (approximately HUF 2,000 billion) loan under the European Union’s SAFE defence financing programme has been approved by the EU Council. The funding could support military developments as well as civilian infrastructure projects, including the planned M49 motorway, while an advance payment of nearly EUR 800 million could reach the Hungarian budget relatively soon.

Hungary’s revised defence loan application approved

The Council of the European Union approved Hungary’s revised SAFE plan on Thursday, according to the Hungarian Permanent Representation to the EU.

The programme, proposed by the European Commission last year, provides EUR 150 billion in joint loans to help EU member states strengthen their defence capabilities.

The previous Hungarian government initially requested EUR 20 billion from the scheme, although the country was allocated EUR 16.2 billion. It subsequently submitted an even larger, EUR 17.4 billion investment plan.

However, the European Commission was unable to approve Hungary’s original application, citing its complexity and the excessive amount requested. By March 2026, Hungary was the only member state whose plan had not received the Commission’s approval.

The new government revised the application in September, reducing the requested amount to EUR 5.4 billion. The European Commission approved the revised plan in October, paving the way for Thursday’s final approval by the Council.

Air defence, anti-drone systems and motorway development

The detailed investment plans remain confidential due to their national security implications. However, a report published by Népszabadság last week suggested that the funding could cover several major projects.

These reportedly include air defence systems, anti-drone capabilities and the development of the M49 motorway. The financing could also accelerate previously planned military equipment purchases and help integrate Hungary’s defence industry into European supply chains.

András Bíró-Nagy, State Secretary for EU Affairs at the Prime Minister’s Office, welcomed the Council’s decision, saying that the investments would contribute to both Hungary’s security and economic development.

He highlighted that the programme would also make it possible to finance infrastructure projects suitable for civilian use alongside defence-related developments.

Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendi also addressed the revised plan in a Facebook post on Friday. He said it had been prepared in line with Hungary’s reassessed defence needs and financial capacity. He also referred to NATO members’ commitment under the previous government to increase defence spending to 5% of GDP, although he did not disclose further details of the planned investments.

Nearly EUR 300 million could arrive as an advance payment

Thursday’s approval means that the Hungarian government and the European Commission can now sign the loan agreement.

One important issue was the EU’s conditionality mechanism, which also applies to SAFE financing. The mechanism was introduced to protect the EU budget against breaches of the rule of law, and Hungary was the only member state against which the Council launched proceedings in 2022. The procedure was closed in October 2026 after the necessary conditions were met.

Under the SAFE programme, participating countries are entitled to a 15% advance payment. In Hungary’s case, this would amount to approximately EUR 810 million, or close to HUF 300 billion at current exchange rates.

World.title: Trump, Putin and Xi issue joint statement after historic meeting: ‘A nuclear war cannot be won’
World.content:
Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping have issued a joint declaration following their first official three-way summit in Shenzhen, China. The three leaders pledged to uphold strategic stability and international security, discussed energy cooperation and reaffirmed that a nuclear war must never be fought. However, their meeting has also raised concerns about a possible new division of global spheres of influence, with Europe once again left out of discussions on Ukraine.

The 90-minute meeting took place on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen. It ended at 11 am Hungarian time, after which the three presidents released a joint statement outlining the main areas of agreement.

According to the BBC, the declaration focuses on maintaining strategic stability and international security, improving energy security and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons. The leaders also addressed the immunity of state officials and the role of international institutions.

Four key points of the joint declaration

The statement sets out four main areas of cooperation:

UN reform: As permanent members of the UN Security Council, China, Russia and the United States pledged to promote reforms that would enable the organisation to respond more effectively to global challenges and fulfil its central mission of maintaining international peace and security. Energy security: The three countries intend to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products, while stressing the importance of maintaining stable energy flows. International legal institutions: The leaders recognised the importance of the principle of national consent and respect for the immunity of state officials. They agreed that the International Criminal Court (ICC) and similar institutions must not abuse their jurisdiction. Nuclear weapons: The three presidents reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. They also confirmed that dialogue is underway to reduce nuclear risks and prevent the proliferation of nuclear weapons.

Xi Jinping reportedly described nuclear weapons as a sword of Damocles hanging over humanity, according to Chinese state media. He also called for their complete prohibition and destruction.

Photo: Anadolu Agency

Leaders praise the meeting, but Ukraine remains a sensitive issue

The three presidents all appeared satisfied with the outcome of the meeting. According to China’s state broadcaster CCTV, Xi described the talks as “positive, constructive and highly productive”, stressing the importance of protecting the hard-won peace.

The Chinese president said the major powers must respect one another’s legitimate security concerns and work together to address global challenges.

“As long as dialogue continues and the doors remain open, there is hope for peace,” Xi said, according to Chinese state media.

Putin also expressed satisfaction. In a video released by the Kremlin after the meeting, the Russian president can be seen saying goodbye to Xi as he leaves the summit venue.

“Thank you for organising this. I don’t think anyone expected everything to go so well,” Putin said.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov described the atmosphere as positive, while Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov claimed that Ukraine had not been the central topic of the discussions.

However, Trump made clear that he would welcome discussions on the war. At the beginning of the meeting, he said that dialogue was essential to achieving peace and expressed his wish to see the conflict come to an end.

“I would like to see this war end,” the US president said.

Trump also described the summit as an honour and thanked Xi for the warm welcome. He argued that previous leaders had too often avoided talking to countries with which they disagreed.

“We think differently. (…) Peace has never been achieved without the possibility of dialogue,” he said.

Photo: Anadolu Agency

Fears of a new division of global influence

Despite the positive tone of the meeting, the summit has raised concerns that the three leaders could be laying the groundwork for a new division of the world into spheres of influence, sometimes described as a possible “Yalta 2.0”.

The comparison refers to the 1945 Yalta Conference, where the leaders of the United States, the Soviet Union and the United Kingdom discussed the post-war order in Europe.

One of the main concerns is that Trump and Putin once again discussed the war in Ukraine without European leaders at the table. The meeting also took place against the backdrop of growing tensions over Taiwan, which Beijing considers part of its territory.

According to Chinese sources, Xi told Trump that Washington must handle the Taiwan issue appropriately if it wants to avoid damaging relations with Beijing, HVG reported. Although the United States does not recognise Taiwan as an independent state, it remains an important arms supplier to the island.

China has rejected comparisons between the summit and the Yalta Conference, arguing that such interpretations reflect outdated Cold War thinking. Beijing says it supports a multipolar international order rather than a world divided between a handful of dominant powers.

Nevertheless, concerns about the emergence of competing spheres of influence persist. Trump’s approach to the Americas, sometimes referred to as the “Donroe Doctrine”, reflects Washington’s ambition to maintain a dominant position in North and South America. Russia, meanwhile, continues to seek influence in Ukraine and other former Soviet republics, while China is expanding its position in Asia and Africa.

The situation is not identical to that of 1945, however. The European Union remains a major economic power, and several middle powers continue to support an international order based on international law.

Photo: Anadolu Agency

Australia calls on Putin to end the war

Not everyone at the APEC summit shared the conciliatory tone of the three leaders.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese directly called on Putin to end Russia’s war against Ukraine during the organisation’s plenary session.

“The two main causes of disruptions to trade are the conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East, and we must do everything we can to bring them to an end,” Albanese said.

He then addressed the Russian president directly: “And I say this very clearly to President Putin: end the war, end it now.”

World.title: Hungary’s Ministry of Defence signed contract with fugitive businessman wanted by the government
World.content:
Hungary’s Ministry of Defence has come under scrutiny after one of its offices signed a HUF 661 million (approximately EUR 1.79 million) furniture procurement contract with a company overwhelmingly owned by businessman György Stofa, just five days after police issued an arrest warrant for him in connection with the scandal surrounding the National Bank of Hungary.

Company of businessman linked to the Matolcsy scandal earns government contract

The agreement with Gyulai “Fafém” Bútor Zrt. was signed on 26 October by the Defence Economy Office, a background institution of the Ministry of Defence. Stofa owns 99 per cent of the company indirectly through another business, Fur-Real Kft., according to corporate records cited by 24.hu.

The businessman was declared wanted on 21 October in an investigation into alleged financial fraud involving the central bank. An international and a European arrest warrant were subsequently issued against him.

Furniture contracts worth hundreds of millions

According to documents obtained by 24.hu, Gyulai “Fafém” Bútor won the procurement in a consortium with Miskolc-based Iroda 2000 Kft. The companies were contracted to supply office chairs worth HUF 503 million (EUR 1.36 million) and manufacture built-in cabinets for a further HUF 157 million (EUR 425,400). The furniture is intended for the military’s Logistics Support Command and the Hungarian Defence Forces’ Materials Supply Depot.

The procurement was carried out under a framework agreement established last year, during the previous Orbán government. The Public Procurement and Supply Directorate had organised a wider tender worth up to HUF 50 billion (EUR 135.5 million) for office furniture for state institutions. Under the framework, suppliers compete again when individual orders are placed.

The arrangement has raised questions about how a company linked to a wanted businessman was selected after an arrest warrant had been issued against its owner. The Public Procurement and Supply Directorate confirmed to 24.hu that the contracts had been signed on 26 October, but said no fulfilment had yet been recorded on its procurement portal. The Ministry of Defence was also sent questions about the deal.

Links to former central bank leader Matolcsy

Stofa is closely associated with Ádám Matolcsy, the son of former National Bank of Hungary governor György Matolcsy. Prosecutors suspect the two businessmen of economic fraud in a case involving the central bank. Neither has reported to the authorities, and their whereabouts remain unknown.

György Matolcsy, who led the central bank from 2013 to 2025, has also been detained in connection with the investigation. Stofa previously held management positions in several companies linked to the central bank and was involved in business activities surrounding Villa Nicole in Mykonos, associated with Ádám Matolcsy. His name has also emerged in connection with the Kégl Castle property in Székesfehérvár-Csalapuszta.

The Ministry of Defence also awarded a separate HUF 731 million (EUR 1.98 million) furniture contract to IMG Office Kft. and Garzon Novum Kft. IMG Office is linked to Gábor Szentgyörgyi, a former wrestling partner of Győző Orbán Jr, the brother of former prime minister Viktor Orbán.

The contracts have prompted questions about due diligence in state procurement, particularly when companies are linked to individuals wanted in a major financial investigation. The Ministry of Defence so far has not answered to questions.

World.title: Official: Budapest’s Buda Castle district to ban Airbnb-style rentals
World.content:
Budapest’s District I council has approved new regulations on short-term accommodation, introducing a complete ban on such rentals in the Buda Castle District from 1 January 2028. Other parts of the district will face different restrictions, depending on the type of building in which the accommodation is located.

The local council adopted the regulation on Thursday, introducing a differentiated approach to short-term accommodation services across the district.

Complete ban on short-term rentals in the Buda Castle District

Privately operated and other types of accommodation establishments registered in the Castle District by 31 December 2026 will be allowed to continue operating until 31 December 2027.

Once this transitional period ends, a complete ban on short-term accommodation services will come into force in the area from 1 January 2028.

Different rules for apartment buildings outside the Castle District

In areas outside the Castle District, the regulation distinguishes between accommodation establishments operating in condominium-style residential buildings and those located in other types of properties.

For establishments in condominium-style buildings, a transitional period will also apply. Those registered by 31 December 2026 will be allowed to continue providing accommodation until 31 December 2027 without having to prove that they have obtained the consent of the condominium.

From 1 January 2028, however, such approval will become mandatory.

The regulation covers not only traditional condominiums but also housing cooperatives and jointly owned residential buildings that have not been legally converted into condominiums but contain at least three flats.

By contrast, accommodation establishments located in buildings that do not fall into the condominium-style category will be allowed to operate throughout the year, without any such restrictions.

Buda Castle District. Budapest, Hungary. Photo: Unsplash

Fines of up to HUF 2 million for violations

The district notary will be responsible for monitoring compliance with the new rules. In cases of violations, they will be authorised to impose fines and order the temporary closure of an accommodation establishment for up to 45 days.

The maximum fines will be:

HUF 200,000 for private individuals and sole traders.

for private individuals and sole traders. HUF 2 million for legal entities and other organisations.

According to the preliminary impact assessment, there are currently 420 registered private and other accommodation establishments operating in District I, of which 19 are located in the Castle District.

The new regulation will enter into force on 1 January 2027.

World.title: ‘Dignity’ Promised as Serbia’s Parliament Elects New Speaker From Student List
World.content:
Aleksandar Cupic, an MP from the Student List, was elected Speaker of Serbia’s National Assembly on Thursday as the power handover continued following last month’s momentous elections in Serbia.

Members of the Student List applauded Cupic, whilst the majority of the now opposition United Serbia parliamentary group, led by former President Aleksandar Vucic of the Serbian Progressive Party, was absent.

Of the 239 MPs who took part in the vote, 97 voted for Stojan Radenovic, while 140 voted for Cupic.

In his first address as Speaker, Cupic spoke of his honour on taking the post.

“I call on all of you to do everything in our power to restore dignity to the country’s highest legislative body and state institution through lawful means, while also respecting the dignity of every individual MP,” he said.

Hew added that voters who had elected them expect all of them to be mindful of every word spoken in the chamber. “That is why dialogue and tolerance must become the foundation of the political culture of each and every one of us,” he said.

He added that parliament would foster constructive criticism and oversight, citing Voltaire’s words that “to cease criticism is to be dead”, and stressing that scrutiny makes public officials more serious and accountable.

“I promise all of you, as well as all the citizens of this country, that in this role, as in everything I have done in my life, I will be strict and fair. Strict with myself and fair to you,” he added.

Cupic addressed the earlier physical attack on the MP Lidija Vukicevic, calling it “irresponsible and inappropriate”, adding that the Student List also condemned it. Vukicevic, a member of the United Serbia parliamentary group, was doused with yoghurt as she entered parliament on Tuesday.

The next steps for parliament include electing deputy speakers and other parliamentary officials, while the country moves towards forming a new government, which must be elected within 90 days of parliament’s constitution.

Cupic is an assistant professor at the University of Belgrade’s Faculty of Transport and Traffic Engineering, where he has worked for more than two decades. Alongside his academic career, he is an organic farmer, growing fruit and vegetables with his wife on their family farm in Sopot, near Belgrade.

A father of six, Cupic entered politics through his involvement in the student-led movement and was nominated for the post of Speaker by the Student List. He has openly supported the student-led movement since the university blockades began in late-2024. He gained wider public attention after hosting hundreds of students on his property during their protest march to the city of Kragujevac.

On Tuesday, after 14 years, six parliamentary elections and an equal number of terms of parliament in which Vucic’s Serbian Progressive Party and its coalition partners held a majority of seats, the new legislature was constituted.

New MPs that day confirmed their mandates and formed parliamentary groups, with Jovo Bakic appointed leader of the Student List group and Aleksandar Vucic heading the United Serbia group, which mostly consists of Serbian Progressive Party MPs. Their respective deputies are Aleksandra Stimac and Milenko Jovanov.

World.title: Media Capture: How Turkey Wrote the Manual on Building an Authoritarian State
World.content:
Television went first because it reaches the most people. The next targets are YouTube channels, independent streamers and social media, which have become a sanctuary for unemployed and exiled journalists.

The tools are already in place. Since 2019, the broadcasting regulator, RTUK, has had the power to demand licences for online broadcasting. Those who refuse can be blocked.

The 2022 Disinformation Law, which the ruling party promised would never be used against news media, has been used against journalists ever since. There have been access bans and bandwidth throttling at moments of political crisis. Global platforms, always ready to compromise rather than lose the Turkish market, have done the rest.

My forecast is a media landscape split in three: a loyal media machine that reaches every living room and says only what the government wants; a lively but fragile critical media, on YouTube and in exile, living on viewer donations and platform ads, that mostly reaches those who already disagree with the government; and, between these blocs, millions of voters who will hear only one side of the story.

That middle ground is the real target. Closing Halk TV and Sozcu TV was not only about silencing journalists. It was about making sure undecided voters never hear the other side.

The timing is no accident. The government wants to rush the country, with aggressive haste, toward the next election, with voices of opposition stifled and no free media.

When that day comes, it will have two options. It can accept a democratic change of power, or it can go down in history as the government that ended free elections in Turkey.

People outside Turkey often ask why Turks are not filling the streets. The answer is not indifference. When Imamoglu was arrested in 2025, hundreds of thousands protested. Nearly 2,000 people were detained, university students were put on trial and journalists covering the protests were arrested. People learned the price.

Fear is only part of it. Families are exhausted by years of high inflation, and many are simply trying to get to the end of the month. The opposition, whose own party has been handed to a trustee, is fighting for survival rather than leading a movement.

Each new seizure is news for a day before it becomes the new normal. That is how media capture works: not through one big shock, but through a series of smaller ones, none of them big enough on its own to start a revolt.

Ankara is not afraid of Brussels

World.title: Serbian Anti-Corruption Agency Files Criminal Complaint Against Belgrade Mayor
World.content:
Belgrade mayor Aleksandar Sapic. Photo: www.beograd.rs.

Serbia’s Anti-Corruption Agency has told BIRN that it has filed a criminal complaint to prosecutors about Belgrade Mayor Aleksandar Sapic, following a review of his assets and income, which the Agency launched back in 2018 and ended in January this year.

“During the extraordinary verification procedure, the Agency obtained data from public authorities and legal entities holding data relevant to the verification. After obtaining and analysing the collected documentation, the conditions were met for submitting a report/complaint, which the Agency filed with the Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office in Belgrade,” the Agency stated.

The Agency did not specify which irregularities were established, or which assets and income the complaint relates to.

It said the proceedings before the prosecutor’s office had been classified as secret. Because of this, the Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office also declined to provide details about the proceedings.

The Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office in Belgrade is handling a number of other high-profile cases, such as the disputed nocturnal demolitions in the Savamala district of Belgrade and the fatal 2023 shootout in Banjska in Kosovo. None of them has yet reached a conclusion.

The office recently came under scrutiny, after a commission established by Serbia’s Supreme Public Prosecution Office said it had committed irregularities in handling several high-profile cases, adding that the report had been forwarded to the Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office for the start of criminal proceedings. Following this, the Higher Public Prosecutor’s Office said it “rejected the allegations”.

Mayor Sapic’s assets first drew public attention in 2023, when BIRN and the Serbian news weekly Vreme published an investigation into his villa in Trieste, Italy. Data obtained by BIRN and Vreme showed that in May 2018, while President of the Municipality of New Belgrade, Sapic had bought the estate for 820,000 euros.

The property extends over almost 400 square metres and includes 13 rooms, a garage, part of a forest and an access road. However, in his asset declaration, submitted to the Agency in January 2019, the only new property listed was a 150-square-metre flat.

After the article was published, Sapic denied having tried to conceal the property, claiming he had reported it to the Agency along with the purchase contract. Sapic later claimed the assets declaration which listed only a 150-square-metre flat, had been filled in by his secretary and he had merely signed it.

In March 2023, Sapic filed two lawsuits against BIRN and sought 12 million dinars [102,000 euros] in damages, claiming that his honour and reputation had been harmed and that he had suffered mental anguish because of the published articles.

BIRN described these proceedings as SLAPP lawsuits, strategic lawsuits against public participation, which put journalists and media outlets under legal and financial pressure for reporting on matters of public interest.

Court proceedings in these lawsuits has continued into 2026.

World.title: Black Sea Attacks Threaten Ukrainian Grain Trade, Disrupt Region’s Exports
World.content:
Infrastructure bottlenecks

UkrAgroConsult’s Kharchenko acknowledges that the increase in Ukrainian agricultural transit through Poland, Slovakia, Hungary and other neighbouring nations creates additional opportunities for their transport and logistics sectors.

“In particular, railway and road transport companies, transshipment terminals, and logistics operators stand to benefit from higher cargo volumes and increased revenues. Poland may also gain from additional Ukrainian grain shipments handled through Baltic Sea ports,” Kharchenko said, noting at the same time that growing transit flows place additional pressure on border crossings, railway networks and port infrastructure.

“Another concern is dissatisfaction among local farmers, who fear that Ukrainian agricultural products could enter their domestic markets. However, as Poland and Hungary continue to maintain restrictions on imports of major Ukrainian grain crops, the direct impact of increased transit on domestic grain prices remains limited,” Kharchenko added.

Ukraine’s neighbours completely banned Ukrainian grain exports as a result of the pressures being put on local farmers several years ago. Ukrainian farmers can sell their grain in other EU countries, but Brussels currently cap wheat sales to the bloc at 1.3 million tonnes a year.

As for the pressure on border crossings mentioned by Kharchenko, the increase in agricultural exports by rail and road has indeed led to persistent congestion at Ukraine’s borders with its EU neighbours.

According to Ukrainian Railways, more than 20,000 freight wagons had accumulated along routes leading to the country’s western borders in late October, with the waiting time exceeding 20 days on some routes. The longest queues are at the borders with Poland and Slovakia.

Jakub Olipra, senior economist at Credit Agricole Bank Polska, says the fundamental problem is that the existing rail infrastructure on both sides of the border is not prepared to handle such large volumes of Ukrainian agricultural exports.

According to the expert, the same situation was observed in the opening months of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, in 2022. “Relatively little has changed since then, with insufficient transshipment capacity, differences in railway gauges and limited border infrastructure remaining major bottlenecks, while Russian attacks on Ukraine’s railway infrastructure have created additional disruptions,” Olipra told BIRN.

Poland’s Infrastructure Ministry did not respond to a request for comment on cross-border cargo transportation conditions.

Meanwhile, Slovakia’s state-owned freight company Cargo Slovakia said that the volumes of agricultural commodities transported by the firm in September and October were the highest recorded since 2023.

However, during the same period, the traction power supply system at Slovakia’s Zilina railway junction was undergoing conversion. “As approximately 80 per cent of these food shipments pass through this junction, the works resulted in a reduction in railway line capacity. Furthermore, upon completion of the conversion works, a fire broke out at the junction, resulting in restrictions on rail freight operations for two weeks,” Silvia Kuncova, director of the company’s CEO office, told BIRN.

She added that following the blockade of Ukraine’s Black Sea ports, the volume of other commodities transported across the Ukrainian-Slovak border, not just agricultural products, had also increased. This, among other factors, had led to greater utilisation of the available railway network capacity.

“In view of the above circumstances, it was not possible to accommodate and transport the exceptionally high volumes of agricultural commodities within the required timeframe and to the extent requested,” Kuncova said.

World.title: Trump’s Balkan Policies Face Scrutiny, Not Reversal, After Midterm Losses
World.content:
The most potent countermeasure to US’s malign influence in the region thus far has come from bottom-up in the Balkans. The October 25 parliamentary election victory of the Student List in Serbia against President Aleksandar Vucic focused on political and legal accountability. The opposition victory was boosted by the venture of Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner, to raze and redevelop the General Staff building in downtown Belgrade.

Likewise, in nearby Albania, the ongoing six-month “Flamingo Revolution” protests against Prime Minister Edi Rama was catalyzed by a luxury development project in the Vjosa-Narta delta on the Adriatic, greenlit by Rama. A US administration inclined to one-stop shopping with strongmen has yet to develop an antidote to people power – once intimidation and repression fails.

However, the European Union also has demonstrated a deep-seated aversion to supporting people power, even when the demands from below largely coincide with its own declared values.

It clung to its relationship with Vucic until he lost decisively and conceded – and it remains unknowable what its policy response would have been had the result been less clear-cut.

Brussels only embraced the new Student List majority once the election projections were clear. It remains on the fence regarding Albania, sticking to a relationship with Rama which was just as personalized as that with Vucic, but considerably more accommodating in a geopolitical sense. The impression to be drawn from the region and beyond, is of a Union caught flatfooted by challenges to the status quo.

And, despite the pronounced change in US Congressional dominance made by voters in the Midterms, the challenges emanating from the Trump administration to the EU, its enlargement area, its interests, and values, will not be curtailed so long as Trump or MAGA hold executive power.

And the American challenge is not the only one buffeting the EU.

On the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation, APEC, meeting in Shenzhen, Chinese President Xi Jinping will host Russian President Vladimir Putin and President Trump for what might be termed a “Hegemons’ Summit”. This trio is at least implied in the US administration’s National Security and National Defense Strategies, issued in late 2025 and early 2026, respectively.

Ostensibly, the US-Israeli war on Iran will be on the agenda, along with artificial intelligence, but it is unlikely that Russia’s imperial assault on Ukraine and unrelenting aim to rewind the European security order by more than three decades will be absent.

While the EU and other Europe+ powers – most notably Canada and the UK – have recognised the challenge, no coherent strategic concept has resulted – let alone been operationalized. And as far as both Washington and Moscow are concerned, Europe as a whole is on the menu. That not only includes Ukraine, but the Western Balkans.

While the EU and Europe+ (the EU and its wider circle of allies, as represented in the “Coalition of the Willing”) have proven a vital lifeline and diplomatic support base for Ukraine’s war effort, the Western Balkans remains the only region where the EU can be decisive.

Yet, to date, the Union and its member states continue to attempt to patch up, rather than overhaul a Balkan policy that has been failing by its own metrics for two decades. At the same time, while the EU is still relatively popular compared to other geopolitical actors in the Western Balkans, it is far from universally so.

The further its policies toward the Balkans deviate from its proclaimed values and standards – on democracy, human rights, fighting corruption, or environmental protection – the more the EU’s relative valence diminishes. Increasingly, to repurpose a phrase recognisable to those leading Ireland’s presidency, Balkan peoples are concluding that those seeking dignity and agency can rely on “ourselves alone” rather than European solidarity.

Therefore, while there is reason to hope that more Congressional and media daylight will shine on the Trump administration’s policies in Europe, including the so-called ‘Western Balkan Six’ states (Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Montenegro, North Macedonia and Serbia), this alone cannot arrest the downward trajectory that Trump’s return accelerated but did not initiate.

Only the combined forces of popular democratic demand and European enlightened self-interest, in accord with its proclaimed values, can accomplish that. The opportunities are greater now than on November 2 – or October 24. What has been lacking is catalytic vision and leadership in several Western Balkan Six states – and in the EU and its member states.

Kurt Bassuener is co-founder and Senior Associate of the Democratization Policy Council, DPC, through which he has published numerous policy briefs.

The opinions expressed are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the views of BIRN.

World.title: Kosovo Ex-President’s Second Sentence Revives Controversy over Hague Court
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp

Two months after being sentenced for war crimes at the Kosovo Specialist Chambers in the Hague, former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci was found guilty of attempting to tamper with prosecution witnesses in the same case.

The verdict has brought new controversy for the Specialist Chambers, which has held six trials – three for war crimes, and three for attempts to influence witnesses in the war crimes cases. The court was set up in The Hague in an attempt to avoid witness-tampering, which had been an issue in some Kosovo-related trials at the Yugoslav war crimes tribunal.

Thaci was served with an arrest warrant for alleged obstruction of justice in December 2024 while he was already in detention in The Hague. According to the indictment, he tried to influence witnesses at his war crimes trial via allies Fadil Fazliu, Bashkim Smakaj and Isni Kilaj, who visited him at the detention centre in separate visits in July, September and October 2023.

World.title: Turkish Court Hands Imamoglu New Jail Term, Political Ban
World.content:
A Turkish court on Wednesday sentenced jailed Istanbul Mayor and presidential candidate Ekrem Imamoglu to two years and one month in prison and imposed a political ban on him over alleged vote-rigging at the Republican People’s Party, CHP, congress in 2023.

Eight other defendants, including the New Party’s Istanbul provincial chair, Ozgur Celik, received the same sentence, while three others were acquitted. The bans will not take effect unless the convictions are upheld on appeal.

Celik criticised the proceedings, pointing to the acquittal of Izmir Mayor Cemil Tugay, a former CHP politician who recently joined President Recep Tayyip Erdogan’s ruling Justice and Development Party, AKP.

“It was said that Ozgur Celik and Cemil Tugay were distributing money to delegates,” Celik told the court. “Cemil Tugay is acquitted, while Ozgur Celik receives a prison sentence and a political ban. What kind of dual system of justice is this? Does someone in this country have to betray their cause and defect to the AKP to be cleared by a court?”

The New Party was founded in July by Ozgur Ozel and 90 other lawmakers who left the CHP after a court annulled the 2023 congress that elected Ozel chairman and reinstated his predecessor, Kemal Kilicdaroglu.

Wednesday’s ruling is the second prison sentence carrying a political ban imposed on Imamoglu. The first sentence was for insulting a public official.

Imamoglu is meanwhile on trial in the much larger Istanbul Municipality corruption case.

Prosecutors accuse him of leading a criminal organisation and committing offences including bribery, fraud, money laundering and bid-rigging, seeking 2,352 years in prison.

Imamoglu and the New Party deny all the accusations. The trial, involving more than 400 defendants, remains ongoing.

World.title: Vukovar Remembers 1991 Victims as Croatia Renews Call for Serbia’s Cooperation
World.content:
Vukovar’s wartime hospital staff led the procession this year. Of more than 1,000 people working there before the aggression started, only around 250 remained alive when the city fell under occupation. On November 20, 18 members of the hospital staff were killed at Ovcara farm near the city, alongside 182 other victims.

The Siege of Vukovar was the bloodiest battle of the Croatian War of Independence. The city was razed to the ground by artillery attacks that lasted for three months, and following the collapse of its last defences, mass killings of prisoners and the wounded from the hospital took place. However, those three months bought time for Croatia to organise its defence against the Yugoslav People’s Army, JNA, which served as an instrument of Slobodan Milosevic’s regime in Belgrade.

This secured Vukovar its heroic status in the creation of the modern-day Croatian state.

World.title: European prosecutors charge individual in 213.7M euro fraud probe into rail modernisation in Bulgaria
World.content:
The European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) in Bulgaria has filed an indictment in the Sofia City Court against one suspect, following an investigation into a project for the modernisation of the Bulgarian railway infrastructure, EPPO said on November 19.

The project, which concerns parts of the railway section between Sofia and Plovdiv, is worth more than 213.7 million euro in EU financing.

The contract for the execution of the project was awarded to a consortium formed by three companies.

The accused is the legal representative of a company participating in the consortium.

According to the investigation, through the manager of the consortium, he submitted false information to the National Company Railway Infrastructure (NRIC) regarding the company he represented to illegally obtain EU funds.

His conduct enabled the consortium to be eligible to and to be awarded in 2019 the EU-funded grant agreement amounting to 213 714 235.14 euro.

Between 2019 and 2024, a total of 68 213 186.03 euro was paid out by the NRIC to the consortium, co-financed by the Connecting Europe Facility (CEF) and the national budget.

In particular, the accused used the manager of the consortium, who had no knowledge of the relevant criminal circumstances, to declare that the company was not subject to insolvency proceedings. In reality, based on the evidence, it was declared insolvent already in 2012.

The investigation was supported by Bulgaria’s Interior Ministry National Police General Directorate and the State Agency for National Security.

Numerous searches and seizures were carried out throughout the investigation across various locations in Bulgaria, including company headquarters and private residences. Documents concerning the tender procedure and its implementation were also seized.

The initial crime report was submitted by OLAF, which also conducted a complementary investigation, EPPO said.

(Archive photo: NRIC)

World.title: Arrests in Bulgaria, the Netherlands and Poland in probe into multimillion euro VAT fraud
World.content:
At the request of the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) in Munich, three suspects were arrested this week in an investigation into a multimillion VAT fraud, EPPO said on November 19.

The arrests took place in Bulgaria, the Netherlands, and Poland. Searches and seizures were also carried out in those countries.

The criminal organisation under investigation is suspected of operating a cross-border VAT carousel fraud – a complex criminal scheme that takes advantage of EU rules on cross-border transactions between its member states, as these are exempt from value-added tax.

It is understood that they sold AirPods via companies and missing traders based in Germany and Bulgaria.

The activities of these suspects alone may have caused an estimated tax loss of 23 million euro in Germany.

With the support of national authorities from Bulgaria, Germany, the Netherlands and Poland, searches were carried out at the premises of the suspects and companies under investigation.

These investigative measures are part of investigation Midas , targeting a transnational criminal organisation behind a 195 million euro VAT fraud scheme involving the sale of smartphones, small electronic devices and protective face masks.

(Archive photo: Interior Ministry)

World.title: EC opens two new infringement cases against Bulgaria
World.content:
The European Commission said on July 8 that it opened two new infringement cases against Bulgaria for failing to correctly transpose EU rules on deforestation and non-cash payments fraud.

In its latest infringements package, the EC said that it sent a letter of formal notice, the first stage in the infringement process, after Bulgaria failed to correctly implement the directive on non-cash payments fraud, which defines criminal offences and sanctions regarding fraud and counterfeiting of non-cash means of payment.

The Commission also found Bulgaria in breach of the EU Deforestation Regulation, which aims to ensure that key goods placed on the EU market do not contribute to deforestation and forest degradation, requiring member states to designate competent authorities responsible for implementing and enforcing the rules. Bulgaria did so for all commodities covered by the regulation, except rubber, the EC said.

Separately, the Commission also said that it was advancing an existing case by issuing a reasoned opinion, the second stage in the infringement process.

In that case, Bulgaria is accused of failing to correctly transpose the rules of the Seasonal Workers Directive, which outlines rules for the admission of third-country seasonal workers to the EU to meet seasonal labour demand.

(Entrance to the Berlaymont building, headquarters of the European Commission. Photo: EU Audiovisual Service)
