World.title: Saudi health minister visits Italy to deepen healthcare cooperation
World.content:
RIYADH: Saudi Minister of Health Fahad Al-Jalajel recently undertook a two-day official visit to Italy to strengthen bilateral relations, expand health cooperation and explore opportunities to establish strategic partnerships between the two countries.

During the trip, the minister held high-level meetings with Italian health sector officials and leaders to discuss cooperation in advanced and specialized healthcare, health investment, digital health, biotechnology and health workforce development.

The visit comes within the framework of the strong relations between Saudi Arabia and Italy and reflects both countries’ commitment to strengthening partnerships, concluding agreements and exchanging knowledge to advance their health sectors and create opportunities for investment and innovation.

World.title: Motor racing-FIA to introduce full-time Formula One stewards from 2027
World.content:
LAS VEGAS: Formula One’s governing body will begin introducing full-time race stewards in 2027 as part of an effort to improve consistency in officiating and strengthen oversight across its championships, the FIA said on Thursday.

The governing body said it would recruit a small initial group of full-time stewards during the 2027 Formula One season, before expanding the program in 2028 and beyond.

The longer-term aim is to create a department of between 12 and 15 full-time stewards, who would eventually also support other FIA single-seater series.

A new chapter for FIA Formula 1 officiating. 🏁 From 2027, the FIA will begin introducing full-time stewards to the FIA Formula One World Championship, strengthening consistency, expertise and continuity in race decision-making. Building towards a department of 12–15 full-time stewards over the next five years, the initiative represents an important investment in the people behind the sport and the future of officiating. #FIA #F1 — FIA (@fia) November 19, 2026

Stewards are responsible for reviewing on-track incidents and enforcing Formula One’s sporting regulations, with their decisions often attracting scrutiny from teams, drivers and fans.

The FIA said its existing part-time stewards would continue to work alongside the new full-time officials, while driver stewards — former drivers who provide racing expertise at each event — would remain part of the process.

The move is intended to provide greater continuity in decision-making, allow officials to identify areas where regulations may require clarification and help train future FIA personnel, the federation said.

The recruitment drive will target experienced international stewards, supplementing the FIA’s current pool of qualified officials.

The initiative follows a broader restructuring of FIA race management since FIA President Mohammed Ben Sulayem took office.

That has included a reorganization of Race Control in 2022, the creation of an FIA Officials department and the opening last month of a Remote Operations Center at Biggin Hill in Britain.

“This latest major investment in FIA officiating reflects our dedication to delivering the highest standards of decision-making, fairness and integrity in motorsport,” Ben Sulayem said in a statement. The FIA said the program was enabled by an improvement in its financial position, allowing it to reinvest in sporting operations and officiating infrastructure.

World.title: Ancient Egyptian burial site gives up its priceless secrets
World.content:
CAIRO: Archaeologists have uncovered an ancient necropolis in northern Egypt containing a priceless treasure trove of rare gold artifacts, jewelry, gold foil, scarabs and terracotta figurines.

The tombs at the burial site at Tell Kom Abu Billo in the Menoufia governorate date from about 2,350 years ago.

The discovery was a significant contribution to understanding ancient Egyptian history from the end of the Late Period, the Macedonian period and the Ptolemaic period, which ended with the death of Cleopatra and Egypt’s annexation by Rome, Egyptologist Dr. Hussein Bassir told Arab News.

“The coffins and funerary artifacts offer insight into ancient Egyptian beliefs surrounding life, death, rebirth and immortality, as well as the relationship between the deceased, the gods and the afterlife,” he said.

Among the finds were tongue-shaped gold pieces, and large numbers of faience ushabti figurines in various shapes and sizes. The mission also discovered terracotta figurines depicting Isis-Aphrodite seated on a lotus flower, as well as small sphinx and Horus figures, amulets, offering tables and two falcon burials — an ancient practice in which falcons were mummified, placed in coffins or shrines, and buried either as sacred votive offerings or alongside human bodies.

The necropolis also contained pottery coffins, remnants of wooden coffins, vaulted mud-brick tombs and a tomb lined with limestone.

Dr. Hisham El-Leithy, secretary-general of the Supreme Council of Antiquities, said the discovery was the first of its kind at the site because of the large number of burials and coffins found within an open courtyard.

World.title: Syria hails historic UN resolution recognizing post-war progress
World.content:
NEW YORK: Syria’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Ibrahim Olabi, said the UN General Assembly had already adopted a resolution acknowledging the ongoing challenges Syrians face.

Olabi said the resolution marked a shift in the international community’s perspective on Syria.

The focus is moving from documenting past crimes and violations to recognizing progress and supporting Syrians. It also aims to help them build a future where their rights and dignity are protected.

He made the remarks during the UN General Assembly’s Third Committee meeting on the draft resolution regarding human rights in Syria.

Olabi thanked member states for adopting the resolution by consensus for the first time.

“Syria views the resolution as both recognition of its achievements and a reminder of its responsibility to continue building on this progress,” Olabi added.

The Syrian envoy emphasized that the resolution recognizes the government’s efforts to improve the lives of all Syrians. It welcomes tangible steps to rebuild institutions, strengthen rights, and broaden participation.

“The resolution welcomes the formation of the People’s Assembly and the Supreme Constitutional Court, the reforms undertaken, and the abolition of exceptional courts. It also welcomes progress on freedom of expression, assembly, and association, as well as on civil society participation,” Olabi said.

He added that the resolution welcomes the establishment of the National Commission for Transitional Justice and the National Commission for Missing Persons.

It also supports equal rights for all citizens, protects Syrian Kurds’ cultural and language rights, and addresses cases where people have been denied nationality.

“The resolution welcomes efforts to create the conditions for the safe and voluntary return of refugees and displaced people,” Olabi added.

“These efforts help build a state that protects its citizens’ rights, delivers justice for victims, and enables all Syrians to help shape its future.”

He said the resolution establishes a strong foundation for closer cooperation between Damascus, the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, and relevant UN mechanisms.

This cooperation considers Syria’s current realities, respects the mandates of these mechanisms, and supports Syrian leadership.

“We look forward to cooperation that supports Syrian priorities, provides assistance, builds capacity, and coordinates efforts to ensure they complement each other and avoid duplication,” Olabi said.

He added that Syria seeks international expertise to help its institutions fulfill their responsibilities to uncover the truth, deliver justice, and protect the rights of all Syrians. “Syria attaches particular importance to the resolution’s new language on full respect for the 1974 Disengagement Agreement, the protection of civilians, and the preservation of Syria’s sovereignty and territorial integrity,” Olabi said.

The Syrian diplomat emphasized that the resolution’s adoption by consensus, participation of 45 countries in the September 11 gathering organized by Syria, and the Security Council’s consensus on implementing the agreement all send a clear message that the 1974 agreement must be fully respected.

“Civilians in southern Syria continue to suffer from violations by the Israeli occupation that affect their safety, homes, children, land, and livelihoods,” Olabi added.

“We still have much to do to achieve our aspirations for a new Syria,” the ambassador said.

“We hope the adoption of this resolution will be accompanied by tangible support for the Syrian government’s efforts in reconstruction, recovery, mine clearance, support for initiatives, and capacity-building.”

He added: “We call on member states, regional organizations, international financial institutions, and relevant UN agencies, funds, and programs to heed the resolution’s call to contribute to these efforts.”

Olabi said that after 15 years, “we made history today by adopting this resolution by consensus. To Syrians everywhere, I say that your determination has inspired peoples and nations, and that you make history at the UN today and every day.”

For the past 15 years, the suffering and resilience of the Syrian people have shaped this resolution. Today, their renewal and achievements continue to define it, Olabi said.

World.title: Iran war costs surpass $48bn amid calls for base damage estimates
World.content:
WASHINGTON: The costs of the Iran war have risen to an estimated $48.3 billion as of Nov. 13, but because that total does not include damage to US bases attacked in the Middle East, lawmakers are pushing for the Pentagon to provide those figures.

Arthur Miller, a Pentagon budget official, provided the latest overall cost estimate Thursday to the Senate Armed Services Committee, which is considering his nomination to be Navy comptroller. The $48 billion figure includes the costs of military operations, as well as for replacing equipment and munitions.

Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut pressed Miller for an estimate on damage to US installations, which Miller said he didn’t have. Republican Sen. Roger Wicker of Mississippi, the committee’s chair, directed Miller to try to provide an answer as soon as possible.

An Associated Press analysis found that Iran attacked aircraft hangars, systems that detect incoming strikes, warehouses, troop housing and more, causing billions of dollars in equipment damage.

The war’s price tag has been a flashpoint in Congress, with debates over costs intensifying as the Trump administration asks lawmakers to pass a $1.5 trillion defense budget. After the unpopular war and its economic effects contributed to severe Republican losses in the midterm elections, financial battles over the conflict will only escalate once Democrats take control of Congress in January for the remainder of President Donald Trump’s term.

The Pentagon has faced growing calls from Democrats to release estimates on the damage Iran has done to American bases in the Middle East through missile and drone attacks.

Senator Elizabeth Warren, a Democrat from Massachusetts, grilled acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao on the costs of the war at his confirmation hearing Tuesday for the permanent job.

Citing independent estimates and media reports, Warren said the US naval blockade on Iranian shipping costs about $32.5 million a day, while an Iranian attack on the Navy’s regional headquarters in Bahrain did at least $400 million in damage.

Cao confirmed the figure for the blockade but said he could not offer a full damage assessment in Bahrain because “it’s a nonpermissive area for us to go.”

World.title: Cincinnati Zoo says Fiona the hippo has died, days after ingesting a visitor’s hat
World.content:
CINCINNATI, USA: Fiona, the hippo whose premature birth and fight for survival at the Cincinnati Zoo turned her into a global sensation nearly a decade ago, died Thursday from complications after swallowing a knit hat that was accidentally flung into her enclosure more than a week ago.

“It is with extreme sadness that we share with you the devastating news that Fiona did not make it after multiple attempts from our amazing vets and keeper team to help her through what ended up being a medical emergency,” the zoo said in a statement.

The zoo said Monday that Fiona was undergoing care around the clock after swallowing the hat more than a week ago.

Before she died, veterinarians had been keeping Fiona hydrated, giving her treats and monitoring her every move, the zoo said. They even borrowed a vibration plate from a horse farm, encouraging her to stand on it several times a day in the hopes that the shaking would help move things along through her digestive tract.

Grace Brooks, of Cincinnati, and her two children, ages 3 and 5, had Fiona on their minds when they arrived at the zoo Thursday, before her death was announced. Her kids have been talking about Fiona at preschool, she said.

“They said she needed to poop, which is, you know, true,” Brooks said with a laugh. “They know all about Fiona, and we have lots of books about her.”

The zoo was mostly empty, though a small crowd was gathered inside the “Hippo Cove,” where two other hippos were swimming.

Even without Fiona in the cove, her presence was felt. There’s a holiday-themed Fiona statue just outside the entrance, and the gift shop has an entire wall filled with hippo-themed shirts, coffee mugs, shot glasses and books, including “A Very Fiona Christmas” and “You’ve Got This, Fiona.”

Fiona was under close care

Fiona captivated people worldwide after her premature birth in 2017. She swallowed the hat about 11 days ago after a zoo visitor tossed it in the air. A ceiling fan caught and catapulted the hat through a small opening above the area’s viewing windows.

It was an accident, said zoo spokesperson Michelle Curley.

Before she died, Mike Wenninger, the zoo’s director of animal health, said veterinarians had sedated her twice to evaluate her condition.

An ultrasound on Tuesday showed some bunching of her intestines, indicating she was still trying to pass the obstruction, Wenninger said. They also conducted a colonoscopy using a 9-foot scope, but were unable to detect anything, he said.

“Her care team even offered her a sniff of coffee, a scent she has always liked,” Curley said Wednesday in the latest update on Fiona’s condition. “And they were happy to see her respond.”

Surgery would be challenging

Specialists told the zoo that surgery wasn’t an option for full-grown hippos, the zoo said.

Hippos have a digestive system that would make Fiona’s situation tricky, Jack Kottwitz, an assistant professor at Michigan State University’s College of Veterinary Medicine, said before her death was announced.

“They have a multichambered stomach for digesting plants — sort of like a cow — but they don’t regurgitate and chew cud like a cow does. Those multiple chambers, tissue folds, fluid, and digesting food easily ‘hide’ the hat, making removal with an endoscope from the stomach chambers very difficult,” Kottwitz told The Associated Press in an email.

Surgery is a major logistical challenge for many reasons, he said.

In order to find the hat, multiple incisions might be needed during a very long surgery, he said. But hippos are notoriously difficult to anesthetize and have skin over 2 inches (5 centimeters) thick in places. Hippos also really need access to water, and Fiona would have to be kept out of the water for several days post-surgery to allow any incisions to heal, he said.

“Because there is no reliable way to pinpoint whether the hat is in the stomach, intestine, or colon, surgeons may have to carefully explore the entire digestive tract — stomach, intestine and colon — to find it,” Kottwitz said.

Jan Hawkins, doctor of veterinary medicine at North Carolina State University, said Fiona’s situation was difficult because it was hard to tell exactly where the hat was.

“You just don’t know because you can’t do the normal imaging and things that you can do in some of the smaller animals, or even horses,” Hawkins said.

Other zoo animals have also died from eating foreign objects

Zoos around the world have warned for years about the dangers posed by objects that are tossed or blown into animal habitats.

Two years ago, a rare antelope choked to death after eating the plastic lid from a squeezable fruit pouch at a zoo in Tennessee. A polar bear at a German zoo died in 2014 after swallowing a jacket dropped into his enclosure by a visitor.

Veterinarians say a common reason for pet owners to make emergency visits is after their dogs have swallowed balls, toys and strings.

Fiona became a sensation after Harambe’s death

Fiona survived her first health scare when she was born six weeks premature. She weighed just 29 pounds (13.2 kilograms), which was less than the lowest recorded birth weight for her species at that time.

Fiona was unable to nurse, so a zoo staffer hand-milked her mother. The zoo recorded her progress with photos and videos, while fans worldwide followed her progress online.

Her survival brought an uplifting turn for the Cincinnati Zoo after months of backlash over the shooting of Harambe, the gorilla who became a pop culture phenomenon after he was killed because a child got into his enclosure.

World.title: Target for land mine-free Zimbabwe by 2030 threatened by aid cuts
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG: Global aid cuts threaten the target for Zimbabwe to be free by 2030 of mines planted during the 1970s liberation war, with only four percent of land remaining to be cleared, a demining charity said Thursday.

The previous Rhodesian government laid belts of mines along the borders with Mozambique and Zambia during the war to prevent fighters from entering the country.

“Just four percent of land remains contaminated,” the HALO Trust said in a statement.

The leading demining charity operating in Zimbabwe and the largest in the world said it had destroyed 250,000 land mines in the southern African country since 2013.

“Drones, state-of-the-art detectors and mini excavators are helping HALO clear faster and more safely,” it said.

However, “sweeping global aid cuts... threaten Zimbabwe’s aim to achieve mine-free status by 2030,” it said, estimating it would take $6.5 million in donations to meet the target.

Many demining programs in Zimbabwe were significantly affected by the reduction of US funding in early 2025. The cuts led the APOPO non-profit group, which used rats and dogs to detect mines, to withdraw from the country.

Mines had killed or injured more than 1,500 people and 120,000 cattle since Zimbabwe achieved independence in 1980, said HALO.

While human casualties were now rare, livestock was still being killed by mines every month, HALO representative Nokutenda Masiyanize told AFP.

“Most of the land that is cleared is used for farming... so food security increases when clearance happens,” she said.

In southern Africa, Angola, Zimbabwe and Zambia are the main countries still affected by land mines and explosives left over from conflict, HALO said.

Angola — where a 27-year civil war ended in 2002 — is one of the most heavily mined countries globally, it said.

Since beginning operations in Angola in 1994, HALO had cleared more than 123,000 land mines and 1,000 minefields.

Mozambique was officially declared land mine-free in September 2015. HALO said its teams cleared more than 171,000 land mines there between 1993 and 2015, destroying roughly 80 percent of all land mines in the country.

World.title: Kompany vows to ‘look forward’ after Bayern return
World.content:
MUNICH: Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany pledged to “look forward” after returning from a month out due to meningeal irritation but said he would learn from the health scare.

Speaking with his arm in a sling at a press conference on Thursday, his first official Bayern media outing since returning, Kompany said he had made a full recovery since being hospitalized.

“I feel very good and am happy to be back with the team. I am in very good health,” Kompany said, adding he had “undergone a lot of check-ups.”

Bayern host strugglers Cologne in the Bundesliga on Friday, with Kompany in the dugout for the first time since their Champions League clash with Arsenal on October 21.

Kompany collapsed on the training pitch two days after the Arsenal match and was hospitalized with what was later diagnosed as meningeal irritation as a result of a viral infection. The fall also caused him to dislocate his shoulder.

He spent a month out, missing five Bayern matches.

The former Manchester City and Belgium captain said he was pleased to get back to the day-to-day of coaching.

“I would prefer for things to return to normal as quickly as possible — and for the focus to be on whether a match is won or lost,” he said.

“I want to look forward. It has been a long process. It is time for the next step.”

The 40-year-old said he was thankful for all of the support he received during his lay-off, particularly from fellow coaches.

“We are so competitive against each other all the time,” Kompany said. “But I think nearly every coach got in touch. It didn’t matter if we were competing or had an argument, they got in touch.”

German media reported Kompany was known to put in long hours since arriving at the defending Bundesliga champions in 2024, with some speculating his work ethic may have contributed to his condition.

Club powerbroker Uli Hoeness said Kompany “works 12 hours a day, six days a week — it’s simply too much.”

Kompany refused to address media speculation about his work habits, but said he would learn from the episode.

“I simply carried on when I was at a point when I should have taken some time to rest,” Kompany said, adding: “I don’t want to downplay it, it was certainly a shock...

“You have to learn from every situation and this was one of those situations.”

The Belgian said he was pleased to be back on the sidelines for big games, revealing he had struggled while watching Bayern’s matches on television during his recovery.

“The best place to be is in the dugout, not at home on the couch in front of the television,” he added.

Defending Bundesliga champions Bayern sit atop the Bundesliga table, level on points but ahead on goal difference of Borussia Dortmund. Bayern are the only side in Europe’s top-five leagues to be unbeaten in all competitions.

World.title: Gulf alternatives may save Excelerate Energy’s LNG project in Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The liquefied natural gas (LNG) project in Iraq is witnessing rapid on-site progress amid efforts to overcome geopolitical challenges and navigation risks associated with the Strait of Hormuz.

According to project updates, the field team and the materials required for constructing the marine jetty and terminal infrastructure have arrived in Iraq, Attaqa News reported.

US-based Excelerate Energy, which is carrying out the project, expects the pace of work to accelerate over the coming weeks, with construction activities progressing at the marine terminal and the facility’s infrastructure.

The firm aims to complete and commission the project during the second quarter of 2027, following a delay in 2026 caused by the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz.

Once Iraq begins imports, it will become the sixth Arab nation in history to import LNG—joining Kuwait, Egypt, the UAE, Jordan, and Bahrain.

The consequences of the Iranian conflict have caused delays for Iraq’s LNG project, which had originally planned to open in the third quarter of 2026. As a result, Excelerate Energy has moved the Excelerate Acadia, its floating storage and regasification unit (FSRU), to Jordan for nine months.

To overcome disruptions to maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the company plans to utilize an FSRU already stationed within the region, eliminating the need to traverse the strategic waterway.

The company is likely to utilize the FSRU currently stationed in the UAE, known as Express.

The US firm indicated that it is working to arrange the import of LNG from countries within the Gulf region, a statement that strongly suggests Qatar or the UAE.

World.title: US dollar exchange rate rises in Iraq’s parallel market
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar experienced a slight increase on Thursday in both Baghdad, the Iraqi capital, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,706.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,706 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,710 Iraqi dinars and 1,700 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also increased, fluctuating between 1,709.5 and 1,708.5 Iraqi dinars.

US dollar exchange rates rose noticeably in the Baghdad and Erbil markets on October 7, following the cabinet’s decision to revalue the official rate of the local currency, causing turbulence and instability in the parallel market.

Iraq officially depreciated its national currency, with the baseline dropping from about 1,300 Iraqi dinars to 1,500 dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet approved the structural adjustment, which marks a 14.5 percent decline compared to the previous official framework that had been in place since early 2023.

Following the announcement, parallel market rates in Baghdad and Erbil soared, with exchange shops reporting market gains of more than 1,700 Iraqi dinars per US dollar.

World.title: Iraqi PM orders reopening of closed roads in Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, Ali al-Zaidi, ordered on Thursday to expedite the reopening of all closed roads in the Jurf al-Sakhar district in the central province of Babil.

During his meeting with security officials, al-Zaidi emphasized that the army and security forces would uphold the authority of the state across all Iraqi territory, according to a statement released by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

The prime minister emphasized that the enforcement of state authority would be carried out in accordance with the constitution and the law. He affirmed the government’s commitment to protecting the lives and interests of citizens across the country and to preventing any violations or assaults on public and private properties.

According to al-Zaidi, the security forces operate as a unified entity, with their numerous branches and units cooperating with one another.

These directives come ahead of the deadline set by the government for Kataib Hezbollah, an Iran-backed militant faction, to withdraw from Jurf al-Sakhar—a deadline expiring on Friday—paving the way for security forces to enter and redeploy in the area.

The deadline for the withdrawal from Jurf al-Sakhar, also known as Jurf al-Nasr, follows an investigation by a government committee, which Baghdad stated uncovered evidence of oil smuggling operations in the area.

The armed faction rejected the smuggling allegations, claiming the sites inspected by investigators were abandoned facilities or fuel tanks for military vehicles.

World.title: Iraq’s trade exchange with China drops to $19.8 billion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Chinese Ambassador to Iraq, Xiang Bo, said on Thursday that the decline in trade exchange with Iraq—which fell to $19.8 billion—is due to the escalating security tensions in the region.

During a press conference in Baghdad, Bo projected that trade between the two countries would recover, reaching $26 billion by the end of 2026 or early 2027.

According to Bo, China is a trusted partner to Iraq. He noted that the two countries share deep historical and cultural ties, dating back thousands of years.

Bo emphasized that bilateral relations have seen significant development, with Iraq serving as a key trade partner. Trade volume between the two countries reached $51 billion in 2025, reflecting the strength of their mutual commitments and relationship.

Bo mentioned earlier that major Chinese firms are involved in the construction and development of several industries in Iraq, such as oil, energy, and infrastructure.

The Chinese diplomat expressed his hope that this collaboration will continue and grow into other sectors, contributing to the development of a complete partnership between Iraq and China.

Chinese companies have been heavily involved in the oil industry and in significant infrastructure projects, such as the construction of major bridges and schools, with more than 600 schools completed in several Iraqi provinces.

World.title: Iraq studies issuing electronic dinar to expand financial inclusion
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq is investigating an electronic dinar as a digital extension of the current national currency to modernize payments, increase financial inclusion, and lessen reliance on physical cash.

Prime Minister’s financial adviser Mazhar Mohammed Saleh highlighted the initiative in remarks to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA) on Wednesday, though no launch date, technical specifications, or formal issuance decision have been announced.

The electronic dinar will serve as a digital representation equal in value to the physical paper dinar rather than a new currency issue. It will not automatically generate new liquidity but will improve the management and circulation of existing funds.

According to the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI), approximately 102 trillion dinars ($67.38 billion)—nearly 92 percent of all currency issued—is held outside the formal banking system.

The purpose of a digital currency is to direct the financial reserves into formal savings, lending, and profitable ventures.

Moving transactions onto official digital channels will help curb unregulated financial dealings, reduce cash-printing costs, and align Iraq with the CBI’s financial inclusion strategy.

The digital dinar plan is different from suggestions to eliminate zeros from the physical currency.

Although the CBI has expanded bank cards, digital wallets, and points of sale, it has not yet declared a formal launch date or technical introduction timetable.

World.title: Egypt expresses interest in Iraq’s Development Road project
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Egyptian officials have renewed their push for national firms to participate in Iraq’s Development Road project and broader infrastructure initiatives.

Egyptian Minister of Transport Kamel el-Wazir said that Egyptian companies are ready to join the Development Road and railway projects with competitive pricing, quality standards, and fast delivery.

El-Wazir’s remarks took place during his meeting with the Iraqi Ambassador to Egypt, Qahtan Taha Khalaf, in Cairo, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

Egypt’s Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs, Hussein Issa, also met with Khalaf to discuss expanding trade, investment, and Egyptian company involvement in Iraqi development and reconstruction projects.

During a regional transport summit held two weeks ago in Alexandria, Egypt, Iraqi Transport Minister Wahab al-Hassani said that Iraq is moving toward the early implementation of land transport agreements with Jordan and Egypt to boost regional trade and cross-border movement.

Al-Hassani confirmed that Baghdad has finalized several land transport agreements with Amman and Cairo that are expected to enter into force soon.

The deals build upon a previously signed memorandum of understanding between the Iraqi and Egyptian transport ministries covering the overland movement of both passengers and goods.

Alongside the deals with Jordan and Egypt, al-Hassani highlighted Iraq’s broader push to establish itself as a regional transit hub through the country’s strategic project of the Development Road.

The strategic corridor spans 1,200 kilometers from the al-Faw Grand Port in the southern province of Basra to the Turkish border, combining new highway and railway networks.

World.title: Baghdad replaces forces holding Jurf al-Sakhar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi ordered on Wednesday the replacement of the forces holding Jurf Al-Sakher, following an investigation into alleged oil smuggling.

The move seeks to end the 12-year control of the strategic Babil province area by the Iran-backed armed faction Kataib Hezbollah.

Iraq’s Supreme Committee for Security Sector Reform, chaired by Al-Zaidi in his capacity as Commander-in-Chief, ordered the replacement of the current force stationed in Jurf al-Sakhar with joint units from the Iraqi army, federal police, and other Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) brigades.

The Energy Police, an Interior Ministry force, was officially assigned to secure the three branches of the strategic Basra-Haditha oil pipeline running through the area.

Findings from a government investigative committee alleging oil theft and pipeline tampering were referred to the judiciary for legal action.

Before Wednesday’s deployment order, al-Zaidi dismissed nine senior security, intelligence, and oil ministry officials—including the director of the Oil Pipelines Company—in connection with the smuggling investigation.

The orders follow escalating tensions between Baghdad and Kataib Hezbollah, which has controlled the area south of Baghdad since recapturing it from ISIS in 2014.

The armed faction rejected the smuggling allegations, claiming the sites inspected by investigators were abandoned facilities or fuel tanks for military vehicles.

World.title: Najaf refinery expansion to raise Iraq’s refining capacity by 70,000 bpd
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s oil refining capacity is set to increase further as the expansion project at the Najaf refinery progresses.

The project aims to add 70,000 barrels per day to the country’s refining output, aligning with Baghdad’s broader plans to boost the production of petroleum products and reduce reliance on imports.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi visited the refinery expansion site on Tuesday to evaluate the progress made and to assess the technical and logistical challenges encountered during the project’s implementation.

The project is being carried out amid Iraqi efforts to improve the efficiency of its refining sector and increase its capacity to meet the domestic market’s fuel needs.

The expansion of the Najaf refinery will increase fuel production to meet the requirements of surrounding industrial projects, create new job opportunities, and boost economic activity within the province.

The Najaf refinery expansion project includes the construction of a new refining unit with a capacity of 70,000 barrels per day. This development encompasses the completion of essential facilities and services needed to support its operation.

The project includes the development of energy infrastructure, an industrial water treatment unit, oil storage tanks, and other facilities associated with the refining unit.

The refinery’s current processing capacity stands at 30,000 barrels per day. With the addition of 70,000 barrels per day from the new unit, the expansion plans aim to increase the total capacity to 100,000 barrels per day.

World.title: SC: Assess buyer's liability before home loan recovery
World.content:
NCLT or NCLAT cannot ask flat buyers to repay the financier without first examining the âunholyâ bank-builder nexus, said SC

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a big relief to lakhs of homebuyers, SC has ruled that in housing projects that remained incomplete despite banks releasing major portion of loan instalments to rogue or insolvent builders, the commercial courts, NCLT or NCLAT cannot ask flat buyers to repay the financier without first examining the "unholy" bank-builder nexus.The order came from a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana on a petition by homebuyers in Krishna housing project, Gurgaon, by Raheja Developers, which has gone into insolvency proceedings.The petitioners said the bank had started recovery proceedings against them in a commercial court in Saket, New Delhi, even though they had not yet got their flats.The CJI-led bench said, "It is the bounden duty of the commercial court to determine the nexus between the builder and bank officials and to see whether the bank disbursed the loan amount to the builder strictly in terms of the tripartite agreement."It said unless a categorical finding is returned that the homebuyers are in default, no interim direction regarding payment of instalments can be issued. "We direct the civil court not to take any coercive action against the petitioners or similarly placed homebuyers without first determining the above-mentioned issue," it said.As per the tripartite agreement between buyers-builder-banks, the financier was to disburse the loan amount directly to the builder in proportion to the progress in construction on ground.However, in many cases, because of builder-bank officials nexus, the financial institutions released loan amounts against each flat buyer much more than the money that should have been disbursed to the builder given the stage of construction of the housing project.When the project remained incomplete for decades, the bank filed recovery suits against homebuyers who, without getting the flats, kept paying EMIs and house rent. A decree in the suit would mean fastening crippling financial liability on the homebuyers.In Sept last year, a Justice Kant-led bench ordered a CBI inquiry against a large number of builders and banks across India for colluding to misuse the tripartite subvention scheme and fleece the homebuyers even when the projects remained incomplete for decades.On Thursday, the bench found its sympathy for the homebuyers has virtually opened the floodgates of litigation and thousands of them suffering under the tyranny of builders and banks have rushed directly to SC. It said, "Our hands are full and we may not be able to handle fresh litigation."In a similar case from Bengaluru involving over 4,000 homebuyers, it protected homebuyers against possible recovery proceedings from banks as the housing project remained incomplete for nearly a decade despite the petitioners paying 95% of the cost of the flat. After granting protection, the bench asked the petitioner's counsel to move Karnataka HC for appropriate relief.

World.title: Archaeological Experience Pavilion at Purana Qila to bring alive India's civilisational journey through layers of excavations
World.content:
Purana Qila has hidden in its heart approximately 2600 years of human history

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Archaeologists and workers carefully scrape away the soil inch by inch to uncover treasures that have been witness to Indiaâs civilisational journey at the iconic Purana Qila complex. An adjoining trench at the excavation site that goes 6.5 metres down reveals eight layers from Mauryan to Mughal period bearing stories of homes that once thrived, the utensils people used, the wood that survived and nuggets of daily life that evolved through Indiaâs many ages.This curated first-of-its-kind archaeological experience pavilion exhibiting a live excavation site and discoveries made at Purana Qila mapping Delhiâs story going back almost 3,000 years will be open to visitors from Monday.Purana Qila, popularly known as Pandavon-ka-Qila, has been identified as the ancient city of Indraprastha, mentioned in the literary work Mahabharata. The standing ramparts and other buildings were built by Sher Shah Suri (1538-1545 CE) after demolishing and re-modeling Dinpanah, a city founded here by Humayun, the sixth city of Delhi, around 1533 CE after his return from Persia.Usually, after excavation a site is filled up with soil but in an attempt to allow people to experience history this exhibition site with the theme "Astitva" - "The Essence Of Our Existence" is being curated to show the layers while ensuring the sanctity of the site is maintained.Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the first Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Forum for Civilisational Dialogue on Friday evening at Purana Qila followed by sessions over Saturday and Sunday. The opening ceremony will feature a special program titled âDialogue of Civilizationsâ Cultural Performance.â It will feature a unique blend of music, dance, visual storytelling, and narration. Based on the theme Vasudhaiva KutumbakamâThe World is One Family, the presentation will highlight the cultural ties between India and Eurasia. World leaders coming for the Dialogue will get to see the 'Astitva' exhibition which will also be inaugurated on Friday evening.Archaeological Survey of India director Vasant Kumar Swarnkar who has been working at the Purana Qila site since 2013-14 and has led the most recent excavations undertaken in 2022-2023, said the excavations across the complex from the 1950s to date have revealed a nine-fold cultural sequence, beginning with Pre-Mauryan habitations to the Mughal Period, without any breaks.Among the oldest are Sherds of PGW (Painted Grey Ware)â pre-Mauryan levels and these will be part of the experience pavilion that includes the Mauryan Ashvamedha Yagya, ring well and SungaâKushana house complex, offering insights into ancient rituals, water management and domestic life.When TOI visited the site on Wednesday, we observed an elevated deck over and around the trenches which will offer visitors a view of the exposed archaeological remains. We explored a space that is likely to have been a room in a house in the Mughal period, a brick platform of Kushan period, rammed floor of Gupta period, pottery pieces from the Rajput period and a kiln from Mauryan era.Equipped with artefact showcases, interpretative panels, the exhibition will highlight to the visitors discoveries ranging from pottery, coins, seals, beads, terracotta figurines, a Kushan period Gajalakshmi terracotta plaque and a Vaikuntha Vishnu stone sculpture from Rajput periodâeach revealing stories of craftsmanship, trade, beliefs and everyday life.

World.title: AERB approves first approach to criticality for RAPP-8 in Rajasthan

MUMBAI: The Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB), Indiaâs nuclear safety regulator located next to the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) at Trombay, on Thursday gave the go-ahead for what is known as the First Approach to Criticality (FAC) of Rajasthan Atomic Power Project Unit-8 (RAPP-8), following the satisfactory completion of safety reviews.An AERB announcement on Thursday night said the permission followed a comprehensive safety review of the reactorâs design, construction, commissioning test results and operational preparedness.The regulatory review process included detailed assessments by AERB and its safety review committees, regulatory inspections and deliberations by the AERB Board.FAC marks an important stage in the commissioning of RAPP-8, paving the way for subsequent commissioning phases leading to commercial electricity generation.AERB will continue to oversee the subsequent commissioning activities through safety reviews and regulatory inspections, including monitoring by its resident site observer team.RAPP-8 is the fourth unit in Indiaâs indigenously designed and constructed 700 MWe Pressurised Heavy Water Reactor (PHWR) series. The other three units of this design are Kakrapar Atomic Power Station Units 3 and 4 in Gujarat and RAPP Unit-7 in Rajasthan.RAPP-8 is located at the Rawatbhata Nuclear Power Plant site in Rajasthanâs Chittorgarh district, which currently has eight nuclear power plant units.

World.title: UNFPA puts India's population at 1.47 billion in 2026, calls for investment in 'youth dividend'
World.content:
Indiaâs population was 1.46 billion in 2025, 1.44 billion in the year before that

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Continuing to be the most populous country in the world, Indiaâs population for 2026 is estimated to be 1.47 billion (147.66) crores with the population doubling time of 81 years, according to the UNFPAâs State of The World Population Report 2026 released on Thursday. Indiaâs population is expected to grow to about 1.7 billion (170 crores) before it begins to fall, around 40 years from now.Indiaâs population was 1.46 billion in 2025, 1.44 billion in the year before that. More than one in four Indians are aged 10 to 24, the report highlights citing it to be Indiaâs âyouth momentâ and calling for investing while the dividend window is open.Surpassing China, India became the worldâs most populous country with 142.86 crore people in 2023 with China falling behind India with a population of 142.57 crore.Meanwhile, Chinaâs estimated mid - year population for 2026 stands at 1.41 billion (141.29 crores) with 70% of the population in the 15-64 years bracket. 15% of Chinaâs population is 65 and above. Fertility rate stands at 1.0 and life expectancy is high at 76 for men and 82 for women.The demographic indicators show that in India those in the 0-14 years age group account for 24% of the population; for 10-19 years this is 17% and for 10-24 it is a strong 26% reflecting Indiaâs youth dividend.The data shows that 69% of Indiaâs population is in the 15-64 years bracket and the population aged 65 and older account for 8%.Life expectancy for males is 71 years and that for females is 74. If one looks at world population in 2026 it is estimated at 8.3 billion with population doubling time 84 years. Globally life expectancy at birth stands at 71 for men and 76 for women.The report, flags Indiaâs Total Fertility Rate at 1.9, the same as last year, which is below the replacement level fertility of 2.1 births per woman indicating that women are having fewer children than needed to maintain the population size from one generation to the next.The 2026 report also draws on UNFPAâs global Demographic Futures Survey of more than 108,000 internet-connected adults in 73 countries, including 1,722 in India to highlight aspirations around relationships, parenthood and life goals, and the conditions that influence peopleâs ability to realise them.It further states that young peopleâs aspirations regarding family and relationships will play a central role in shaping the nationâs demographic trajectory.Survey findings from India show that optimism runs high with 83% of respondents feeling positive or very positive about the future, despite concerns about conflict, economic insecurity and inequality, UNFPA highlights. Women aged 18 to 39 describe an ideal family size of 2.1 children and parenthood remains a strong aspiration: nearly 85% of childless respondents aged 35 to 39 would ideally like to become parents.âYoung people need confidential, non-judgmental âSexual Reproductive Healthâ information and services (contraception, menstrual health, STI prevention, referral) alongside pre-pregnancy, maternal and postnatal care,â UNFPA states while emphasising the need for India to expand and strengthen youth-responsive primary care.

World.title: 3 leopards found dead in North Kashmir, poisoning suspected

SRINAGAR: Three leopards, including two female cubs aged 8-9 months, were found dead in the forests of north Kashmirâs Kunzar area, prompting J&Kâs wildlife protection department to file an FIR Thursday against unknown people after autopsies raised suspicion of poisoning.Wildlife official Shahid Sultan said the cubs were found dead on Nov 17, with no visible injury marks. Their bodies were kept overnight at the departmentâs control room in Tangmarg because a veterinarian was unavailable. Autopsies were conducted the next day. On Wednesday, police informed the department about another dead leopard, an 8-9-year-old male. All three were found in the same area, though not together, Sultan said.âThe doctors in their reports have mentioned a suspected case of poisoning,â he said, adding they had also raised the possibility of infectious poisoning, suspecting the animals might have eaten contaminated meat, possibly a rabid dog. Samples were collected for forensic examination to establish the cause of death. âWe have not come across such a case of suspected poisoning before,â he said.Leopard sightings are common, particularly in north Kashmir, where mountainous terrain and expanding apple orchards provide suitable habitat. On Nov 10, six-year-old boy Kifayat Bhat was mauled to death by a leopard in Kreeri.

NEW DELHI: Amid recent attacks on commercial vessels with Indian crew members in the Persian Gulf, shipping minister Sarbananda Sonowal on Thursday directed the countryâs maritime regulator to step up surveillance of high-risk areas, issue timely security advisories and sensitise seafarers about potential threats and precautionary measures.Between Nov 10 and 18, at least five reported incidents involving commercial vessels carrying Indian seafarers occurred in the Persian Gulf and around the Strait of Hormuz. The attacks involved projectiles and missiles, leaving Indian crew members injured, one missing and vessels damaged or evacuated.Chairing a review meeting on Thursday, Sonowal also directed the directorate general of maritime administration (DGMA) to maintain regular communication with shipping companies and vessel operators to ensure the safety of Indian seafarers. He asked officials to coordinate closely with the ministry of external affairs, Indian diplomatic missions, maritime stakeholders and international agencies to ensure prompt assistance in the event of an incident involving Indian vessels or seafarers.Currently, nine Indian-flagged or Indian-interest vessels carrying 161 Indian seafarers are in the Persian Gulf. In the Red Sea, eight Indian-flagged vessels have 210 Indian seafarers on board.The ministry is tracking more than 1,200 vessels and nearly 9,500 Indian seafarers in high-risk regions through a live dashboard launched for this purpose.So far, 104 incidents have been reported in the Persian Gulf, claiming 12 Indian lives. World.title: Shenzhen Trilateral: India cautious amid possible vindication and strategic concerns
World.content:
The Shenzhen trilateral summit may not signal a crisis for India but the government is closely following the likely outcomes, realising the meeting's potential to alter several dynamics that it has to manage almost on a daily basis in its ties with the US, China and Russia.

There was no official response from India to the "historic" 90-minute meeting that President Donald Trump had with his Chinese and Russian counterparts â Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin respectively â in China's global tech hub but official sources said India is following the summit and likely ramifications with strategic caution.

The meeting, which was described as positive and highly productive by the Chinese state media, ended with a declaration that committed to UN reforms, to deal more effectively with global challenges, stable energy flows, nuclear risk reduction and the "abuse" of its jurisdiction by the International Criminal Court (ICC) that issued an arrest warrant against Putin.



India is not a party to the ICC and mainatins safe distance from it.

Overhauling the UN â with focus on expanding the Security Council permanent membership - and securing stable and predictable energy supplies have been core pillars of India's foreign policy in a world marred by conflicts. Any indication of urgency for UN reforms is a positive development. However, there's also little for India to believe that the call for the UN to conform to its "fundamental mission" of peace and security is more than just lip service.





India holds P5 countries responsible for the delay in Security Council reforms and external affairs minister S Jaishankar has accused these countries of being "short-sighted" by not agreeing to any dilution of their powers.

The focus on stable energy flows does provide some diplomatic vindication for its long-standing position that Russian oil purchase helped stabilize global energy markets. It's also important that the declaration talks about expanding the production and supply of refined petroleum products, as India emerges as a crucial processing hub, refining Russian crude.

For India, any potential easing of the rigid US position on India's energy policy would be a welcome development.

The statement that in the declaration shunning nuclear war also aligns with India's core nuclear doctrine. India had welcomed the same formulation in a P5 2022 joint statement, saying that it creates a security environment conducive to global disarmament.

Looking ahead, there are concerns that India might have about the likely implications from the meeting, and the answers to which might lie in doubling down on its strategic autonomy and multi alignment.

Despite its time-tested ties with Russia, a great power cartel or a G3 that operates as an exclusive club to manage global affairs may not sit easily with India's focus on a multipolar world and multipolar Asia or its efforts to lead the Global South into a decision-making role.

There was no direct mention of the wars in West Asia and Ukraine where India is keen to support early resolution and has even put forward a proposal for safety of commercial shipping, while working to secure shipping lanes also in the Strait of Hormuz.

India has argued that the Global South cannot remain a helpless spectator and must have a role in shaping peaceful settlements of conflicts that have most impacted the developing world.

While much has been made about the US signalling to China through the Manila Quad summit, India realizes it must remain vigilant against the consequences of a US-China accommodation. Any understanding between Washington and Beijing that upsets the Indo-Pacific balance may not be in India's interest. Even the Quad summit took place after 2 years and only on the margins of a multilateral event.

World.title: Karnataka Cabinet okays confiscation of book that ‘insults’ Basavanna and ‘distorts’ his philosophy
World.content:
With several Veerashaiva-Lingayat community leaders up in arms against the book Basava Mantapa, alleging that it distorts the teachings and philosophy of Basavanna and insults him, the Karnataka Cabinet on Thursday decided to confiscate copies of the book by Ravi Hanj, which are in circulation. It has also cleared action against publisher-journalist Vishveshwar Bhat.

After a prolonged discussion in the Cabinet meeting, a decision to confiscate the book and take legal action against the author was arrived at, announced Deputy Chief Minister G. Parameshwara. “Normally, we do not take swift action based on petitions. But in this case a decision was taken since its impact is likely to be felt across the State,” he said.

Earlier in the day, the Basava Samiti not only demanded a ban of the book, but also filed a police complaint seeking action against the author and the publisher. In a social media post, BJP State president B.Y. Vijayendra had also sought action against the publisher and the author.

When asked why an expert committee was not set up and an immediate decision taken after the samiti petitioned Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, the Deputy Chief Minister said that senior Ministers had discussed the issue in the Cabinet meeting. “This is only the inittial reaction and we will look into the legality later. Action has been taken as per the provisions of BNS. We could not be silent spectators,” he said.

Addressing a press conference in Bengaluru, Basava Samiti president Aravind Jatti said the book hurt the sentiments of the Lingayat community and Basavanna’s followers in the name of research. He also called for criminal cases to be registered against those responsible for disturbing peace in society.

“Mr. Hanj has attacked Basavanna, who propagated the ideals of equality, a casteless society, the dignity of labour and the concept of a parliament, by describing him in derogatory terms. However, following the backlash, he is now trying to apologise and promise corrections. We want neither. They have mistaken the peaceful nature of the Veerashaiva-Lingayat community for weakness. It is condemnable that the book has been presented as a work of research to disguise its objectionable content,” he said.

“What is happening now is an ideological conspiracy aimed at undermining the Sharana philosophy and Lingayat identity. We know who is behind it,” he said.

Mr. Jatti alleged that such objectionable developments had intensified since the government declared Basavanna the “cultural leader of Karnataka.”

Large and Medium Industries Minister M.B. Patil warned that attacks on Basavanna and the Lingayat community would no longer be tolerated. “We will take to the street and launch an intense agitation. Protests have already begun in several parts of Karnataka,” he said.

“It is condemnable that Veerashaiva Mahasabha president Shankar Bidari and former Kannada Sahitya Parishat president Manu Baligar attended the launch of such a book. It is up to the Veerashaiva Mahasabha to decide what action should be taken against Mr. Bidari,” he said.

MLA for Aland B.R. Patil said, “There have always been elements that cannot tolerate the ideals of Basavanna, Mahatma Gandhi and B.R. Ambedkar. Mr. Hanj has written the book with malicious intent and attempted to tarnish Basavanna’s reputation.”

Former Mayor of the London Borough of Lambeth, Neeraj Patil, and thinker J. S. Patil also called for stringent action against the author and the publisher.

Rural Development and Panchayat Raj Eshwar Khandre, who is also president of the All-India Veerashaiva Mahasabha, has welcomed the decision of the Cabinet. In a release, he said that a demand to remove Mr. Hanj’s videos on social media had been made in the Cabinet, and the Cabinet had agreed to write to the Centre to get it removed.

World.title: Wall Street ends sharply lower as Anthropic’s debut fails to revive AI fervour
World.content:
U.S. stocks slumped on Thursday (November 19, 2026) after Anthropic’s super-sized IPO ‌failed to revitalise faded enthusiasm over artificial intelligence, as an early spike in its ​share price ebbed.

All three major U.S. stock indexes ended the session ⁠sharply lower, with the benchmark S&P 500 logging its fifth straight session of losses.

The S&P 500 was on course to post its steepest weekly loss since April 2025.

Anthropic’s debut, the largest IPO on record, was priced ‌on late Wednesday (November 18, 2026) at $83 per share and was widely viewed as the next high bar to clear for the AI trade. The stock opened at $111.50 shortly ‌before noon. After the company’s market valuation briefly surpassed $2 trillion, its momentum began ‌to lose ⁠steam.

“The Anthropic IPO is attracting gobs of attention,” said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager ⁠at Argent Capital in St. Louis, Missouri.

Even so, Ellerbroek’s enthusiasm for ‌the AI trade has waned.

“My beliefs about the growth in data centre capex spending have come down a little bit over the last month or two,” he added. “Nvidia’s crisis situation is a big deal. The midterm elections have had an impact. Data centres are ‌going to be more expensive to build and they’re going to be built more ​slowly.”

Advanced Micro Devices shares tumbled after investigative outlet Hunterbrook said its affiliated fund, Hunterbrook Capital, had taken a short position in the company.

Most chipmakers were ⁠lower, including Micron and Broadcom, among others.

Nvidia marked its sixth straight session of losses after the chipmaker’s upbeat revenue forecast did little to lift sentiment.

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index closed lower. Neocloud firms CoreWeave ‌and Nebius sustained steep losses.

In other stocks, Palo Alto Networks shares jumped after the cybersecurity firm raised its 2027 revenue guidance. Walmart dipped after the retail giant’s annual sales forecast disappointed investors.

According to preliminary data, the S&P 500 lost 148.39 points, or 2.03%, to end at 7,175.24 points, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 544.00 points, or 2.23%, to 23,885.88. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1,102.71 points, or 2.20%, to 49,095.46.

Focus turns to the FED

Following Wednesday’s release of ‌minutes from the U.S. Federal Reserve’s October policy meeting, investors are recalibrating their expectations pertaining to upcoming rate decisions.

The ​minutes revealed a desire to rein in inflation even prior to the recent release of consumer and producer price indexes, which showed price pressures heating ⁠up.

Financial markets are currently pricing in about a 94% likelihood of a 25-basis-point rate hike at ⁠the central bank’s December meeting, with a small but growing chance of a super-sized 50-basis-point increase, according to CME’s FedWatch tool.

Next week, the Commerce Department is expected to ‌release its personal consumption expenditures (PCE) report, which includes the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge, the PCE price index. Analysts expect the report to show year-on-year core inflation of 3.2%, well above ​the central bank’s 2% annual target.

World.title: The Rohingya question: International solidarity, accountability and the missing road home
World.content:
The Rohingya question has returned to the centre of international attention following the landmark judgment delivered by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) on November 19, 2026. Yet, for more than a million Rohingya living outside Myanmar, legal recognition is only one part of a much larger struggle. The fundamental question remains: how does a community that has been systematically marginalised, displaced and denied its identity reclaim its place in the country it considers home? The crisis also exposes the international community’s inability to translate diplomatic declarations, humanitarian assistance and legal proceedings into a sustainable political settlement.

When I began working on Myanmar in the United Nations Department of Political Affairs in 2011, the Rohingya question was largely confined to perfunctory diplomatic talking points. Although concerns about discrimination, communal tensions and citizenship were acknowledged, there appeared to be limited understanding in many diplomatic discussions of the geographical and postcolonial nuances underlying the crisis.

This began to change with the outbreak of communal violence in May 2012, which dealt an early blow to Myanmar’s fragile democratisation process. The developments gradually compelled interlocutors to recognise that the country’s transition was not simply about moving away from military rule or introducing electoral reforms. It also involved confronting deeply entrenched postcolonial challenges, competing historical narratives, unresolved questions of identity and citizenship, and the complex relationship between the centre and its ethnic peripheries.

The Rohingya question could not be understood simply as another episode of communal tension between religious communities. It was deeply embedded in the history of colonial-era migration, the changing political geography of the Arakan region, competing narratives of belonging and the post-independence construction of citizenship in Myanmar. The historical relationship between the territories that now constitute Bangladesh and Myanmar, population movements during British colonial rule and the subsequent politicisation of identity were essential to understanding the dispute. The tendency to reduce the issue to a humanitarian concern or communal violence obscured these deeper historical and political dimensions.

The ICJ verdict takes me back to August 25, 2017. At the time, a colleague and I constituted a two-member Political Affairs team working on Myanmar at UN Headquarters. We were engaged in preparations relating to the UN response to the Kofi

World.title: Several Bengal districts under alert as cyclone Akvan likely to bring heavy rainfall
World.content:
Several districts in the southern part of West Bengal, including Kolkata, will receive heavy rainfall until November 21 due to the cyclonic storm Akvan.

The storm, which lay over the east-central Bay of Bengal on Thursday morning (November 19, 2026), is expected to make landfall around noon on Friday (November 20, 2026), along the coast between Narsipatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and Puri (Odisha), close to Gopalpur.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) issued a warning of heavy rainfall with thunderstorms and gusty winds in Kolkata, North 24 Parganas, Howrah, Hooghly, and Purulia districts, while South 24 Parganas, Purba Medinipur, Paschim Medinipur, Jhargram, and Bankura are likely to receive heavy to very heavy rainfall.

Since Wednesday night (November 18, 2026), Kolkata and several other south Bengal districts have experienced overnight and morning rainfall under the influence of the weather system.

The intensity of rain in Kolkata increased as the day progressed after the city woke up to a drizzle on Thursday (November 19, 2026). Squally wind speeds of 40–50 kmph, gusting to 60 kmph, are also likely to prevail along and off the West Bengal coast until Friday noon and decrease thereafter, while sea conditions will remain very rough, said IMD.

The IMD also advised fishermen not to venture into the deep sea toward the Northwest and West-Central Bay of Bengal until Saturday (November 21, 2026). The South Eastern Railway has cancelled about 19 trains on November 19 and 20 due to the possible impact of the cyclone.

“We are prepared for any unprecedented situation. Our workers and officers are all at alert. If there is any waterlogging, we will pump it out with motors. We are coordinating with other departments and doing this as teamwork, including the power department, port authorities, disaster management, PWD, and others,” Minister of Urban Development and Municipal Affairs Agnimitra Paul said.

World.title: Anthropic shares close 17% higher on first day of trading
World.content:
Anthropic shares closed about 17% higher on their first day of trading on Thursday (November 19, 2026), as investors shrugged off the Nvidia spy scandal and fears of a tech bubble to snap up the AI giant’s stock after a record-breaking IPO.

The shares ended the session at around $97, up from an IPO price of $83, after opening at $111.50 and briefly valuing the maker of the Claude chatbot at about $2 trillion.

The debut marks a milestone in the AI boom. A company founded five years ago by OpenAI defectors worried about AI safety has become the first of the leading model developers to list on Wall Street, at a valuation rivalling decades-old tech brands.

The listing, under the ticker “ANT,” gives ordinary investors their first chance to bet directly on a stand-alone AI giant.

‘Breath of fresh air’

SpaceX’s total ultimately rose to $86 billion after its underwriters exercised an option to buy additional shares. Anthropic has granted its underwriters a similar option, which would lift its total to about $93.5 billion.

“This may be the breath of fresh air that the tech trade needed to move beyond the fog of artificial intelligence that we’ve been living in for the last couple of weeks,” Art Hogan of B. Riley Wealth Management told AFP.

The strong demand comes even as AI stocks have swung sharply, with investors questioning whether heavy spending on the technology will pay off.

Nvidia, the chip giant at the centre of the AI investment boom and an investor in Anthropic and dozens of other AI companies, has been shaken by the resignation of chief executive Jensen Huang after a reported affair with a woman suspected by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy.

Anthropic’s Claude models are among the most powerful in the world, hailed for their problem-solving potential but also feared for their capacity to destabilise societies and replace human workers.

The five-year-old company’s revenue has surged at a pace few U.S. companies have ever matched, reaching $17 billion in the third quarter, up from $1.4 billion a year earlier.

Much of that revenue comes from customers paying to use its AI models for computer coding. Its massive computing costs remain a major question for investors.

Anthropic has disclosed about $900 billion in commitments for computing capacity and warned in its filing that it must make many of those payments even if demand falls short.

‘One stop’

Mr. Amodei and his sister Daniela, the company’s president, founded Anthropic with several colleagues in 2021 after leaving ChatGPT-maker OpenAI.

Daniela Amodei told CNBC the listing was only “one stop on the journey” for the company.

“We’re going to wake up tomorrow and we’re going to be the same company,” she said.

Anthropic’s IPO filing went into extensive detail on the risks of AI technology, reflecting the company’s focus on safety even as it builds ever more powerful models.

It warns that advanced AI systems “could pose catastrophic or existential risks to society if not developed and deployed responsibly.”

Critics accuse the company of using its safety message as cover while releasing powerful technology, casting itself as the responsible steward of an industry it is racing to lead.

“The company uses safety branding to court investors, employees, and the public — even as it has quietly weakened its safety pledges and lobbied for self-serving regulation,” said a public statement, titled Misanthropic, signed by prominent academics.

World.title: Delhi rolls out ‘Ehsaas 2026’ policy to support students’ mental health
World.content:
The Delhi Government on Thursday (November 19, 2026) launched the ‘Ehsaas 2026’ Mental Health and Well-Being Policy for schools and higher educational institutions in the national capital. The policy aims to ensure one counsellor for every 500 students, besides providing helplines and mental and emotional support services.

Lieutenant-Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu, Chief Minister Rekha Gupta, spiritual leader Sri Sri Ravi Shankar and Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa were present at the launch.

The policy seeks to raise awareness about mental health and encourage students, teachers and parents to speak openly about the subject, making mental and emotional well-being an integral part of education.

Under the policy, special attention will be given to examination pressure, academic stress, anxiety, depression, interpersonal relationships and challenges related to digital behaviour. Students dealing with the pressure of board and entrance examinations will also receive guidance and support, according to the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO).

The policy also provides for opportunities for students to develop stress-management and social-emotional skills, while sensitising teachers and parents to recognise early signs of mental health concerns. It also emphasises confidential mechanisms for reporting bullying, identity-based discrimination and cyberbullying, timely action on complaints, and protection from harassment for those filing complaints, according to an official statement.

Equal support for all children

The Lieutenant-Governor said making mental health and emotional well-being an integral part of education was the need of the hour. At a time when young people were facing increasing stress, the Delhi government’s initiative was timely and commendable.

Mr. Sandhu said, “Every child’s feelings, aspirations and needs matter. No child should face discrimination on the basis of their background, abilities or circumstances. Children with disabilities and those from disadvantaged communities must be given equal opportunities, acceptance and support.”

He added that responsibility for mental health rested not only with students but also with teachers, parents and school management.

Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said the policy had been introduced keeping in mind the mental health and overall well-being of students and would be implemented across schools and higher educational institutions in Delhi.

She said ‘Ehsaas’ would give millions of students studying in Delhi’s schools and colleges an opportunity to move forward with greater mental and emotional resilience. “The Delhi government wants every child to progress in life with happiness, positivity and confidence, and to know that the government, teachers and parents will stand by them through every challenge,” she said.

Six-tier mechanism

According to an official statement, the ‘Ehsaas’ policy will have a six-tier escalation mechanism to ensure student safety and address serious mental health crises. The mechanism will include the class teacher, school counsellor/first responder, school head/wellness team, District Well-Being Centre, hospital/emergency mental health services and relevant statutory agencies.

Students will have access to specialised mental health services through District Well-Being Centres established at the district level. These centres will provide psychological assessments, therapeutic interventions and psychiatric consultations.

“Schools will be responsible for early identification, initial psychosocial support and referrals, while clinical assessments and treatment will be handled by trained specialists, ensuring that students who need help receive appropriate care in time,” the statement further added.

Staff to receive training

Education Minister Ashish Sood said the government took up the issue after a school student attempted suicide a few days ago. Following the incident, he wrote to school principals and held discussions with them and mental health experts to work towards a comprehensive policy.

He said the policy was an important initiative to understand children’s emotional needs, listen to them and provide appropriate support. He also thanked the Art of Living, UNESCO, IHBAS and expert institutions for their contribution to developing the policy.

Mr. Sood said teachers, parents, principals, Educational and Vocational Guidance Counsellors (EVGCs), officials, drivers and other support staff would be trained to identify early changes in children’s behaviour and respond with sensitivity and appropriate support.

Four key pillars

The ‘Ehsaas’ policy is based on four key pillars. The first, the “Whole-Institution Approach”, seeks to make mental health part of an institution’s overall culture, with the participation of students, teachers, faculty, institutional heads, hostel staff and parents, according to the CMO.

The second pillar, Proactive and Preventive Care, focuses on identifying early signs of mental health concerns, promoting social-emotional and life skills, and building mental resilience.

The third, System-Level Accountability and Governance, seeks to ensure clearly defined responsibilities within institutions, staff training, capacity building and accountability of institutional leadership.

The fourth pillar, Ethical Safety and Rights-Based Support, will protect students’ dignity, privacy and confidentiality, ensure age-appropriate consent for minors and respect the autonomy of adult students.

World.title: FIR against two former Bengal Ministers over sexual assault charges
World.content:
A First Information Report (FIR) has been lodged against two former Ministers in the West Bengal government, Indranil Sen and Bratya Basu, along with several senior government officials, over multiple charges, including sexual assault.

The FIR was lodged at Baguiati Police Station under the Bidhannagar Commissionerate by social activist Rajib Sarkar on behalf of multiple women who have either been artists or employed by the West Bengal Information and Cultural Affairs Department.

The two Ministers have been accused of rape, wrongful confinement, extortion, criminal breach of trust, cheating, repeated sexual assault, corruption and criminal conspiracy.

“Several women approached me and levelled serious allegations against the two ministers. They have been threatened, harassed, and tortured when they asked for what they deserved. They should now get justice,” said Mr. Sarkar, speaking to the media.

A zero FIR has been registered against 40 accused individuals, including the two former Ministers, he said.

Mr. Basu, an actor and playwright, served as the Education Minister in the previous Trinamool Congress government led by then Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee. Mr. Sen, a singer-turned-politician, served as the Minister of State with independent charge for the Cultural Affairs and Tourism Departments. Mr. Sen was arrested by the Kolkata Police on October 28, 2026, in connection with a Durga Puja ticket scam case by the Enforcement Directorate.

Five former Ministers, who had been part of Mamata Banerjee’s cabinet, have been arrested since the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government came to power in May 2026.

The arrests of former ministers began with former state Fire Services Minister Sujit Bose. Three other former ministers were subsequently arrested: Dilip Mondal, who served as Minister of State for Transport; Ujjal Biswas, the former Correctional Services Minister; and Udayana Guha, who held the North Bengal Development portfolio. Ujjwal Biswas, who was out on bail, passed away on November 11, triggering strong reactions from Mamata Banerjee, who claimed political vendetta behind the arrests.

World.title: Cyclone ‘Akvan’ updates: Three lakh evacuated, 423 rescue teams deployed as cyclone heads to Odisha
World.content:
This live blog is closed.

Severe Cyclonic Storm Akvan is likely to cross the North Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and South Odisha coasts between Narsapur and Puri, close to Gopalpur, by noon on Friday (November 20, 2026), the IMD said.

Over 3 lakh people have been evacuated, and 423 rescue teams have been deployed in vulnerable areas of Odisha as the state stepped up its preparations.

Also read: Why is Bay of Bengal so active? Expert explains

Also on Thursday (November 19, 2026), the East Coast Railway cancelled 41 trains and rescheduled 29 others as a precautionary response to the cyclonic storm, an official said. The South Eastern Railway also cancelled at least 28 express trains, mostly going to or passing through the temple town of Puri on Friday (November 20, 2026).

Also read: Why is Andhra Pradesh facing a third cyclone in a month?

The IMD issued a red alert for Srikakulam and Vizianagaram districts, an orange alert for Parvatipuram Manyam, Alluri Sitaramaraju and Anakapalli districts, and a yellow alert for Kakinada.

World.title: President, PM agree on resolving 'all matters' through dialogue amid rising political temperatures
World.content:
President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif have decided that all matters will be resolved through dialogue, the Presidency said on Thursday after the two leaders met in Islamabad.
